You will need to prove your household income and this can be done by: Applying for a Student Finance loan If you have applied for a means tested maintenance loan, then we are able to access your household income information very quickly. However, you need to ensure your ‘sponsor’ has consented for Aston University to see your household information. To change your consent, so that Aston can see your household information, please ask your ‘sponsor’ to call Student Finance to change the consent. Proving your household income without taking a loan You do not need to take out a Student Finance loan to have your household income assessed for Scholarship purposes. You may not want to take out Student Finance loans to fund your study for religious or personal reasons. However, if you have been awarded a scholarship with the eligibility criteria of a household income below a specific threshold, you will need to provide information to prove this. To do this, you will need to have your household income (HHI) assessed by Student Finance. You will also be expected to provide this information if you choose to take out a Maintenance Loan. You will need to submit a loan application to Student Finance and pass their eligibility checks. However, you will be able to specify that you want a loan for £0 so you won’t borrow any money. Student Finance can then carry out the HHI assessment and the outcome will be shared with Aston. To do this (UK students only): Create an online Student Finance account and select that you would like to apply for a maintenance loan. Follow the steps of the application as if you were applying for the loan and provide all the necessary information. When asked ‘Do you want to apply for the higher amount of Maintenance Loan? select ‘Yes, I want to apply for a higher amount of Maintenance Loan’. This lets Student Finance know to assess your household income. Later, when asked ‘How much Maintenance Loan do you want to borrow?’ select ‘I want to borrow a specific amount’. When you are asked to input the amount, type ‘NIL’. This lets Student Finance know that you are not taking out any loan. When you have completed the application, your parents / sponsor will be asked to submit their household income information. What bursaries and scholarships will be available? There will be a number of different Scholarship schemes available to students in 2026/27 and you do not have to repay this type of funding. You can find more information about Aston Scholarships on our scholarships page and information about bursaries here . Is there any additional funding for nursing students? Aston University students that commence study after September 2024 and are studying the below courses may be eligible for additional funding from the NHS Learning Support Fund (NHS LSF): BSc (Hons) Adult Nursing BSc (Hons) Nursing Studies (Registered Nurse Mental Health Nursing) The NHS LSF is non-repayable supplementary funding for eligible students and is offered alongside the mainstream student loans system. The NHS LSF is offered to support students whilst they work towards professional registration. Provisions provided by the NHS LSF include: Training Grant of £5000 per student per academic year - each academic year, each student will receive a non-means-tested grant Travel and Dual Accommodation Expenses - reimbursement for excess travel and accommodation expenses incurred whilst undertaking placement Exceptional Support Fund up to £3000 per student per academic year - a grant available to students in unexpected financial hardship Parental Support up to £2000 per student per academic year - available to students with parental responsibility for a child (age restrictions apply) Eligibility To be eligible for the NHS LSF, enrolled adult nursing students will need to be ordinarily resident in the UK. Students will also need to be eligible for funding (tuition fee loan and maintenance loan) from the Student Loans Company. How to apply All applications must be made via the NHS LSF application system. For students applying for the NHS LSF for the first time, an NHS LSF Account will need to be created. Register for an account here . Students must apply for the NHS LSF annually. For existing students that are already in receipt of the NHS LSF, invites to reapply will be received via email. The above is for guidance only. For further information including the full eligibility criteria, please visit NHS Learning Support Fund (LSF) NHSBSA . What if I'm considering deferring my offer to 2027/28? Those entering an undergraduate degree programme from September 2027 or a postgraduate degree programme from January 2027 and seeking funding from Student Finance England will fall under the new Lifelong Learning Entitlement. It is important to know that September 2026 is the last intake to fall within the current student finance system. Full details for the Lifelong Learning Entitlement are not yet available from Student Finance England but you can find information here , which could assist in your consideration of whether to defer your offer of study. How and when do I have to repay my student loans? You will become liable to repay your student loans in the April after you complete your studies. Your repayments are linked to your income. You only make repayments when your income is over £25,000 a year. If your income drops below this amount, repayments stop. Your repayments are normally collected directly through your wages whilst you are working in the UK by HMRC (the UK tax authority). Interest will be charged on your student loans from when the first payment of the loan is received and continues until the loan has been repaid in full. The interest rate varies as it is linked to inflation and is set in September each year. FAQ Video Finance for returning students What amount of tuition fees will I have to pay in 2026/7 as a continuing student? Tuition fees will increase for 2025/6 to £9,790. What is student support funding? Student support funding is UK government funding which is available to all full time “home students” to help cover the costs of their studies whilst at University. What is a home student? The rules about who qualifies as a “home” student, and who can get this type of funding, are very complicated and depend on your nationality, the immigration status of you and your family members and where you have been living. If you are a British national or hold full 'settled' status and have lived in the UK for at least three years before the start of your course, then it is likely you will qualify. If you have any questions about “home” funding status and whether you will qualify then please feel free to contact one of our advisers in the Student Life and Funding Team at The Student Solutions Centre on 0121 204 4007 or book an appointment through: https://outlook.office365.com/book/studentadvice_msb@bookings.aston.ac.uk/ How do I apply for this funding? Student support funding for “home” full time students is assessed and paid through Student Finance England. You can make an application online at the Student Finance England website or you can apply using a form. If you have not applied to Student Finance England before then you will need to use form PN1 for 2026/7 (even though you are not a new student!) If you had funding through Student Finance England last year and will be returning to your studies this year then you will need to use form PR1 for 2026/7. You can download these forms from the gov.uk website. When should I apply? Key Dates for applications In order for your student funding to be in place in time for the start of term in September 2025 you must complete your application by: Returning students: 26 June 2026 New students: 29 May 2026 There absolute deadline for existing students to apply for 2026/7 funding is 9 months after the start of the academic year which would be the end of May 2027. What funding is available from Student Finance England? You can use the online finance calculator on the Student Finance England website to get an idea of how much funding you may be able to receive. Tuition Fee Loan You can borrow tuition fee loan of up to £9,790 in 2026/7. This type of funding is not based on your household income and is available to all eligible students. It is paid directly to the University and you have to repay this type of funding after you have finished your studies. Maintenance Loan This is a loan which is available to help you pay your living costs. Part of the loan is assessed based on your family’s income and there are different amounts according to where you study and if you live at home whilst you study. The Maintenance Loan will be paid into your bank account at the start of each term. You have to repay this type of funding after you have finished your studies. Special Support Grant This grant is to help pay for living costs and is available to students who have an underlying benefit entitlement. Most full time student students do not qualify to apply for social security benefits, but there are some special groups who can apply (for example students who are single parents or those in receipt of DSA). The Special Support Grant is assessed according to your household income. The Special Support Grant will be paid into your bank account at the start of each term. This type of funding does not have to be repaid. What funding is available whilst I am on placement? Please see our section above on placement funding under information for new students. Do I have to pay tuition fees if I have to retake my modules? This depends on what course you are studying and what the Exam Board has decided it wants you to do. You do not normally need to pay extra for exams or assessments taken during the referred exam period. If you are an undergraduate student repeating with attendance then you will normally only pay for the modules you are repeating. You can calculate this by dividing your annual tuition fee by 8 (the number of 15 credit modules you would take in a normal year). This will give you the cost for one 15 credit module. You then need to multiply this by the number of modules you are repeating (remember 30 credit modules count as 2 modules). This fee is charged regardless of the attempt number. If you an undergraduate student repeating without attendance then you will normally only have to pay the cost of one module. You can calculate this by dividing your annual tuition fee by 8 (the number of modules you would take in a normal year). If you are repeating 'without attendance' you will not be eligible for a tuition fee loan or maintenance loan from Student Finance Loans company. Are there any additional scholarships available from Aston University? To find out if you qualify for scholarships please visit the scholarship webpage . I have dependent children - is there any additional funding available through Student Finance England? There are additional grants available to students who have children financially dependent upon them. This type of funding is assessed on the income. If you are living with a partner then their income will also be taken into account. Childcare Grant You can apply for a grant to help you with up to 85% of your childcare costs. You will need to complete a separate application form called the CCG1 for 2026/7 to apply for this grant. You can download the form from the Student Finance England website The Childcare Grant will be paid directly to your childcare provider at the start of each term. This type of funding does not have to be repaid. Parents’ Living Allowance You can receive a grant of up to a maximum of £2,024 depending on your income. You do not need to complete a separate application form for this grant and it can be assessed as part of your main funding application. The Parents’ Living Allowance will be paid into your bank account at the start of each term. This type of funding does not have to be repaid. Is there any additional funding for medical students? From year 5 onwards, students on the MBChB course can apply for funding from the NHS Bursary. To help eligible students meet the cost of study, the NHS Bursary may contribute towards tuition fees and maintenance costs. The NHS Bursary may also provide additional allowances for students that meet certain conditions. 2025/6 provisions provided by the NHS Bursary include: A means-tested bursary (based on household income) A non-means tested grant of £1052 (not based on household income) A tuition fee contribution of up to £9,535 Additional allowances dependant on circumstances e.g. Childcare Allowance, Disabled Student Allowance, Travel and Dual Accommodation Expenses and the NHS Bursary Hardship Grant. Students can also apply to Student Finance for a reduced rate maintenance loan for living costs. Please note, NHS funding is subject to change. New and prospective students should not rely on the current funding information when planning finances. Eligibility To be eligible for the NHS Bursary, enrolled MBChB students will need to be ordinarily resident in England. Students will also need to be eligible for funding (tuition fee loan and maintenance loan) from Student Finance England. How to apply For students applying for the NHS Bursary for the first time, an NHS Bursary Account will need to be created. A step by step guide to applying via the NHS Bursary Application System (NHSBSA) can be found here . During eligible funding years, students must apply for the NHS Bursary annually. For existing students that are already in receipt of the NHS Bursary, invites to reapply will be received via email. The above is for guidance only. For further information including guidance about intercalating students and the full eligibility criteria, please visit Student Services NHSBSA . How and when do I have to repay my student loans? You will become liable to repay your student loans in the April after you complete your studies. Your repayments are linked to your income. You only make repayments when your income is over £25,000 a year. If your income drops below this amount, repayments stop. Your repayments are normally collected directly through your wages whilst you are working in the UK by HMRC (the UK tax authority). Interest will be charged on your student loans from when the first payment of the loan is received and continues until the loan has been repaid in full. The interest rate varies as it is linked to inflation and is set in September each year. Please contact email studentadviceteam@aston.ac.uk or call 0121 204 4007. If you are having difficulty paying If you believe your payment is likely to be late or are having difficulty paying, you must contact the Accounts Receivable team immediately, via the contact form on solve . They will be able to discuss your situation and where possible agree a payment plan with you, within University regulation. If you are facing financial difficulties and require help and advice you can contact The Student Advice Team at The Hub . There are advisers who will assist you, in addition a Funds Administrator is available to help with an application for financial assistance if you are in hardship. What happens if I fail to pay my tuition fees? The complete University Policy on Sanctions for Student Debt can be accessed in the Tuition Fee Charging Policy . If you fail to pay your tuition fees instalments in full by the due date or fail to set up and maintain a suitable payment plan, university sanctions will be applied to your student account. Sanctions will restrict you access to Library and IT facilities. This will prevent you from accessing your Aston Email, MAP and Blackboard, and block access course material or submitting work. Sanctions will also prevent you from graduating dependant on the level of debt owed. Any applied sanction would remain in place until such time that a suitable arrangement to pay fees is in place and/or the outstanding account balance is settled. Transparency is vitally important to us, and we're proud to benefit our students, staff and wider community. Find out more or download the PDF . Can I get a refund if I leave my programme part way through? Yes, in certain circumstances a refund or partial refund will be considered. Please refer to the University Tuition Fee Charging Policy which outlines the withdrawal process. Please note there is a deadline for informing the University of your wish to withdraw, after which there can be no refund. You can find a copy of our policy on our policies page, under Integrity - Responsible Charging Can invoices, letters, statements and other financial correspondence be sent to an (personal) email address other than the Aston University email? No, all communication will be sent to you at your Aston University email address. It is important that you check your email on a regular basis. Tuition Payments Do I have to pay the fees on or before enrolment? During your enrolment you will automatically be setup to pay by instalment, allowing you to pay 50% of your tuition fees by 30 October. Alternatively your fees maybe paid by one of the following methods: Undergraduate student who have taken out a loan with Student Finance England will have the funds paid directly to the University on your behalf. Postgraduate students who have taken out a loan with Student Finance will have the funds paid directly your bank account. In order to amend your instalments inline with Student Finance's payment dates and amounts Finance Centre require a copy of your notification along with payment of the 1st instalment. A sponsor, normally when a company or institute (not a family member or individual) is paying your fees on your behalf, see Sponsored Students for further detail. Will any debt to the University stop me from graduating? Yes, for further details please go to the Sanctions page . Can I pay at enrolment? Yes, payments can be made during enrolment. Finance staff are located in the Finance Centre and will be available to help you with the payments. You may also use the online card payment this option, which means you do not have to queue and is accessible outside of normal office hours. What happens if I do not pay at enrolment? If payment is not made in full, or insufficient evidence is given on how your fees will be paid, then financial clearance will be blocked. You will have until 31 October to pay in full or provide a sponsorship letter, failure to do so may result in you being asked to withdraw. It is important that you speak to staff in the Finance Centre. I have not received my Tuition Fee Loan confirmation, will I still be able to enrol? Will I still have to pay my fees then request a refund from the University? Yes, you can still enrol but we advise that during online enrolment you complete an instalment request, allowing you to pay 50% of the fees by the deadline date of 31 October. The Student Loans Company will provide confirmation of your loan to Student Academic Services who will credit any invoices raised for tuition. You will then be required to complete the refund request, for further details click on Refunds . Can I pay by monthly instalments? No, the University only allows the following; 50% Term 1, 25% Term 2 and 25% Term 3 by online card instalments only. When will I be invoiced for my tuition fees? You will receive an invoice once you are formally enrolled. This will be sent to your Aston University email, it is important that you check your email on a regular basis. If you have already paid, this will be confirmed on the invoice which will be printed ‘PAID’. How much are my tuition fees? The tuition fees are calculated by the Academic Services who can confirm the charge. What happens for subsequent academic years? The same deadline of 30 October for the relevant academic year applies. You will not be permitted to re-enrol for the following academic year if you have not paid the fees and other amounts due to the University. What sanctions are imposed for the late payment of tuition fees? Tuition fee sanctions will be imposed, for example the use of both library and computer facilities will be withdrawn. For further details please go to the Sanctions page . Scholarships What Scholarships are offered by Aston? Will this reduce my fees? Aston offers a range of scholarships click the link to find additional details Aston Scholarships . Any - True False Apply filters Clear all Home Current Students Support with Fees and Finance Tuition Fees and Payments Tuition Fees Tuition Fee Sponsorship Tuition Fee Sponsorship Tuition Fee Sponsorship Student Finance Student Finance England (SFE) is the largest provider of tuition fee loans within the UK and is accessible to both Home and EU students. Home and EU students planning to use a student loan to pay tuition fees will be able to make an application here: https://www.gov.uk/apply-online-for-student-finance The application process can take on average between 6 – 8 weeks, so we strongly advise all students to apply early and secure their funding before the beginning of term. If you are experiencing any delays with your application, notify Credit Control immediately. The team will be able to discuss your situation and, where possible, agree either an extension or payment plan with you. If you have any questions about SFE, need assistance making an application or require help resolving an SFE-related issue, please contact the Student Advice Team based in The Hub. Sponsorships Sponsored Students You are a sponsored student if all or part of your tuition fees will be paid by an external organisation. This may be an employer, government body or embassy (not a family member). On receipt of an official letter purchase order, the University will send a tuition fee invoice directly to your sponsor. Confirming Your Sponsorship Once you have accepted a place at Aston, please let us know as soon as possible that you are a sponsored student. The sponsor must provide an official letter (on company headed paper) or organisation purchase order confirming the following: Your full name Student University Number Full details of where the invoice should be sent Organisation contact name Organisation address Organisation email Payment reference that needs to be quoted on the invoice. (i.e a Purchase order number) GBP amount the organisation is paying for your tuition fees MUST BE GBP or % percentage of the fees being paid The period/academic year of study that the organisation is paying for Confirmation Instructions The letter or purchase order will need to be uploaded on My Aston Portal as per your enrolment instructions. Late arrivals should upload the confirmation document to the fundedsponsorships@aston.ac.uk . In addition, a copy of the confirmation will need to be sent to the Admissions Office (as detailed on your offer letter). If you do not provide us with a confirmation letter, you will be responsible for paying the fees. Please note that we reserve the right to reject a confirmation document and, if the sponsor does not pay, sanctions can be applied to your student account as per the University Policy on Sanctions for Student Debt, which can be accessed in section 7 of the Tuition Fee Charging Policy. We have a range of international scholarships to recognise your academic, professional, and personal experience. To apply for a scholarship, you will need to apply for and receive an offer for an Aston University course first. Scholarship applications open on key dates throughout the year, and we will share information on how to apply closer to those dates. Scholarships for January 2027 Postgraduate International Community Scholarship (Postgraduate) The International Community Scholarship offers a discount to tuition fees to all international applicants who pay their deposit by a specific date. January Intake: £4,000 Pay deposit by the offer acceptance deadline stated in your offer letter This discount will be automatically subtracted from the tuition fees of those who meet the above criteria, there is no need to apply. Applicants must hold an offer for a full-time postgraduate taught programme delivered on campus at Aston University. Exclusions - the following programmes will not be subject to this discount: MBA PGDIP/ MSc in Overseas Pharmacy Assessment Programme MSc in Physician Associate Practice MRes programmes Any postgraduate research degree Online courses Postgraduate International Community Scholarship January 2027 T's & C's 232.82 KB Sir Adrian Cadbury Chancellor's Scholarship (Postgraduate) - £10,000 Named after Sir Adrian Cadbury, a champion of ethical business and education, this scholarship backs international students who want to use their studies and career to make a positive difference. Show us how you’ll make an impact and you could take £10,000 off your tuition. Scholarship value: £10,000 tuition fee reduction Who can apply: Open to self-funded international offer-holders on postgraduate taught course (excludes All MRes programmes, MBA, PhD and research programmes, Overseas Pharmacists Assessment Programme (OSPA), PgDig, MSc Physician Associate Practice, MPH) How to apply: You will receive a personal application link by email after you receive your offer to study. Application requirements: Submit an application form and a 500-word statement on how you will make a positive impact and use your degree to support communities. (Statement of 550 or more, or 450 or fewer, will not be assessed.) Deadline to apply: 1 November 2026 (Sunday), 23:59 (UK time) Decision date: 6 November 2026 (Friday) Sir Adrian Cadbury Scholarship Terms & Conditions 2027 237.05 KB Please note: Scholarships cannot be combined. Scholarships for September 2027 Undergraduate International Community Scholarship (Undergraduate) - apply for a £9,000 tuition fee discount The Undergraduate International Community Scholarship is a competitive, application-based award for eligible undergraduate applicants joining Aston University in September 2027. Value: £9,000 total, applied as a tuition fee discount across the degree: Year 1: £3,000 Year 2: £3,000 Year 3: £3,000 Year 2 and 3 are awarded automatically on progression. The scholarship applies to taught years only. Placement years, repeated years, and repeated modules are excluded. Deadlines Early application round: Application: TBC Scholarship Outcome: TBC Deposit Payment: TBC Final application round: Application: TBC Scholarship Outcome: TBC Deposit Payment: TBC Acceptance/confirmation process Once an application round closes, the University will allow up to 14 working days to review and assess applications. Applicants will be notified if they have been awarded a scholarship, subject to conditions. Awarded applicants for the Early Application Round will be given 21 calendar days to pay their tuition fee deposit. Awarded applicants for the Final Application Round will be given 14 calendar days to pay their tuition fee deposit. Scholarship confirmation occurs only after the applicant has paid their deposit, at which point the award is applied to the student record. Application link The scholarship application link will be emailed directly to eligible undergraduate international offer-holders and will not be hosted publicly. If you believe you are eligible but have not received your scholarship application link, please contact hello@aston.ac.uk . Submission of this form does not guarantee the award of a scholarship. All applications are assessed against the published eligibility criteria and Terms & Conditions. Awards are subject to approval and availability. Eligibility Open to self-funded international undergraduate offer-holders only For direct entry to Year 1 Subject to programme and progression exclusions, as detailed in the Terms and Conditions. Please note: Applicants entering a Top-up BSc (Hons) programme (that is, direct entry into the final year of a Bachelor's degree) will receive the Year 1 payment of £3,000 only. Applicants must hold an offer for a full-time, taught undergraduate degree programme delivered on campus at Aston University. Global Articulation and Progression Scholarship T's & C's 145.21 KB NCUK The NCUK Articulation and Progression Scholarship supports international students progressing/articulating from an NCUK pathway programme to continue their studies at Aston University, Birmingham. The scholarship provides a tuition fee reduction for eligible students progressing/articulating from an NCUK International Foundation Year (IFY), International Year One (IY1), or Master's Preparation programme (MP) and enrolling at Aston University for the September 2026 intake. The scholarship is competitive and application-based , meaning applicants must submit a scholarship application to be considered. Meeting the eligibility criteria does not guarantee that a scholarship will be awarded. All applications are assessed in line with the published eligibility requirements and scholarship availability. Scholarships are applied as a tuition fee reduction to the eligible programme of study and cannot be exchanged for cash or transferred to another programme, applicant, or intake. Scholarship values The available scholarship awards for NCUK students progressing/articulating to Aston University are shown below. NCUK Students currently studying Scholarship Value NCUK International Foundation Year (IFY) £6,500 tuition fee reduction (first year at Aston University) NCUK International Year One (IY1) £5,000 tuition fee reduction in Year 2 (first year at Aston University), with the potential to receive an additional £5,000 in the final year of study NCUK Master's Preparation Programme (MP) £5,000 tuition fee reduction (first year at Aston University) For students progressing/articulating from NCUK International Year One , the scholarship may be awarded across two academic years . Students who meet the continuation requirements during their first year at Aston University may receive a further £5,000 tuition fee reduction in their final year of study. Continuation of the final-year award requires students to achieve an overall 60% average at first attempt , pass all modules at first attempt, and remain enrolled as an Overseas fee payer. How to apply To be considered for the NCUK Articulation and Progression Scholarship, applicants must complete the scholarship application form after receiving an offer to study at Aston University. Applicants will be asked to submit a short written statement as part of the application explaining why they should be considered for the scholarship. Applications are reviewed following the submission deadline. Where the number of eligible applications exceeds the available scholarship allocation, applications will be assessed competitively using the University’s internal evaluation process. Key dates Submission deadline: 14th June 2026 (midnight UK time) Scholarship outcome: 30th June 2026 Deposit deadline: 21st July 2026 (midnight UK time) Eligibility To be eligible for the NCUK Articulation and Progression Scholarship, applicants must: Be classified as an Overseas fee payer Hold an offer for a full-time Undergraduate or Postgraduate Taught programme at Aston University, Birmingham Be progressing/articulating directly from one of the following NCUK pathway programmes: NCUK International Foundation Year (IFY) NCUK International Year One (IY1) NCUK Master's Preparation programme (MP) Meet all academic and English language entry requirements Submit a completed scholarship application before the published deadline Pay the required programme deposit and enrol for the September 2026 intake. The scholarship is open to self-funded international students . Applicants whose studies are fully or partially funded by a sponsor are not normally eligible unless a formal agreement with Aston University confirms eligibility. Programme exclusions The following programmes are not eligible for the NCUK Articulation and Progression Scholarship. Undergraduate MBChB Medicine MPharm Pharmacy MOptom Optometry BSc Nursing Studies BSc Healthcare Science (Audiology) Postgraduate PGDip / MSc Overseas Pharmacy Assessment Programme (OSPAP) MSc Physician Associate Practice All MBA programmes All MRes programmes All research-only programmes. Additional programme exclusions may apply where specified by the University. Terms and Conditions Full eligibility criteria, scholarship conditions and continuation requirements are outlined in the NCUK Articulation and Progression Scholarship Terms and Conditions. The full Terms and Conditions can be found below. NCUK Articulation and Progression Scholarships T's & C's 707.19 KB North East Forestry University (NEFU) - £5,000 The NEFU Articulation Scholarship supports eligible students progressing to Aston University through the dual-degree partnership between Northeast Forestry University (NEFU) and Aston University. The scholarship provides a £5,000 tuition fee reduction for students joining Aston University through the approved 3+1 articulation pathway, where students complete three years of study at NEFU before progressing to Aston University to complete the final year of the programme. This scholarship is automatic and non-competitive . Eligible students do not need to submit a separate scholarship application. Students progressing through the NEFU partnership route will be informed of the scholarship by their partner institution and the Aston University Partnership Lead. The award is confirmed once the required programme deposit has been paid and becomes active following successful enrolment at Aston University. Scholarship Value Value Programme £5,000 tuition fee reduction BSc (Hons) Construction Project Management The scholarship is applied as a tuition fee reduction for the single academic year studied at Aston University. The award has no cash value and cannot be transferred or used for accommodation, living expenses, or other costs. Eligibility To be eligible, applicants must: Successfully complete the required stage of study at Northeast Forestry University Progress to Aston University through the approved 3+1 articulation agreement Hold an offer for BSc (Hons) Construction Project Management Be classified as an Overseas student for tuition fee purposes Be self-funded Meet all academic and non-academic conditions of their offer The scholarship is available only to students progressing through the formal articulation pathway and is not available to applicants applying independently outside the agreement. How the Scholarship Works Eligible students are identified through the NEFU articulation pathway and informed of the scholarship by their partner institution and the Aston University Partnership Lead. The scholarship is confirmed once the programme deposit has been paid and is applied to the student record before enrolment. The tuition fee reduction becomes active once the student successfully enrols at Aston University. If a student withdraws before enrolment, does not enrol, or is unable to obtain a visa, the scholarship will automatically lapse. Important Information Students may normally hold only one Aston University scholarship per programme. The award applies to one academic year of study only. Sponsored students are not eligible . The scholarship cannot be deferred, transferred, or converted to cash. Full Terms and Conditions Full Terms and Conditions for the NEFU Articulation Scholarship are available below and should be read carefully before accepting your offer. NEFU Articulation Scholarship T's & C's 149.31 KB OnCampus Aston OnCampus Aston Merit Scholarships The OnCampus Aston Merit Scholarships recognise high-achieving international students who progress from OnCampus Aston to study at Aston University, Birmingham. These scholarships provide a tuition fee reduction of up to £6,000 for eligible students joining Aston University in September 2026. All scholarships are awarded automatically, based on academic performance. There is no separate application process. Eligible students will normally be identified through the OnCampus Aston progression process . The scholarship is confirmed once the required tuition fee deposit has been paid and becomes active after successful enrolment at Aston University. OnCampus Aston Progression Scholarships The value and allocation of the OnCampus Aston Progression Scholarships are determined by OnCampus Aston. Applied as a tuition fee discount, the scholarship awarded by Aston University will match the value of the scholarship awarded to the student by OnCampus Aston during the foundation year. Scholarship value Students may receive one of the following awards: Scholarship Maximum Value OnCampus Aston Gold Merit Scholarship Up to £6,000 OnCampus Aston Silver Merit Scholarship Up to £5,000 OnCampus Aston Progression Scholarship Match-funded award. Value and allocation determined by OnCampus Aston. Where a student holds both a Progression Scholarship and a Merit Scholarship, the Merit award will act as a top-up to reach the maximum scholarship value. The maximum total scholarship available to any individual student is £6,000. Scholarships are applied as a tuition fee reduction for the first academic year at Aston University only. Eligibility To be eligible, applicants must: Progress to Aston University from OnCampus Aston (Birmingham campus) Hold an offer for an eligible full-time programme Be classified as an Overseas student for tuition fee purposes Be fully self-funded Successfully complete their OnCampus Aston pathway programme Meet all conditions of their Aston University offer Scholarships are awarded automatically based on progression status and academic performance within the OnCampus Aston cohort. Programme exclusions The scholarship does not apply to the following programmes: BSc Nursing Studies (Adult or Mental Health) MBChB Medicine MOptom Optometry BSc Healthcare Science (Audiology) PGDip / MSc OSPAP MPH MSc Physician Associate Practice All MRes programmes All PhD programmes All MBA programmes Important information Scholarships are available for the September 2026 intake only The award applies to the first academic year at Aston University Students may normally hold one Aston University scholarship per programme Scholarships cannot be deferred to a later intake he scholarship is applied as a tuition fee discount only Full terms and conditions Full Terms and Conditions can be found below and should be read carefully before accepting your offer. These scholarships benefit asylum seekers or those who have been granted a form of limited permission to stay in the UK, following an unsuccessful asylum application, and who are therefore prevented from accessing student finance. These sanctuary scholarships are known as The Ernest Edward Scholarships in memory of the generous donor’s grandfather, Ernest Edward Crummack, who left school aged 12 to work in a coal mine. 100 years on, so many young people and especially young refugees still find themselves deprived of the opportunity to grow and fulfil their potential. Ernest Edward Scholars receive a full tuition fee waiver, support with accommodation and living costs, and additional non-cash support. The scholarship is worth up to £20,000 for postgraduate taught courses and up to £45,000 for undergraduate courses over the duration of the programme. The actual amount awarded may vary, as support is calculated according to individual need and determined on a case by case basis . Scholars also have access to tailored support, including language support where needed, Sports Aston membership, professional mentoring, and support from Aston’s Students’ Union. Summary of eligibility criteria Ernest Edward Scholarship not for you? Aston University offers many other undergraduate and postgraduate for home and international students . Ernest Edward Scholarships 2026 Course: You must have applied to study a course at Aston University. Most three-year undergraduate and one-year postgraduate courses are eligible but certain courses such as medicine and nursing are not eligible. You must be: In the UK An asylum seeker or the partner/dependant of an asylum seeker; OR An unsuccessful asylum seeker/refugee or the partner/dependant of an unsuccessful asylum seeker/refugee who has instead been granted Discretionary Leave to Remain (DLR) or some other form of temporary status in the UK. How do I apply? Applications for the Ernest Edward Scholarship 2026/27 have now closed Applications for 2027/28 will open in Spring 2027 so please check back on this web page and contact us at that time. What happens next? We will contact you by email after each stage to let you know if your application is successful. Please note, we will communicate scholarship decisions two weeks after each deadline date. If you have any further questions, you are welcome to contact us . Can I apply for more than one scholarship? You can only receive one scholarship, but you are able to apply for multiple scholarships. If you are successful in being awarded multiple scholarships, the highest value scholarship will be awarded to you. Summary Key facts How to apply Summary The British Council is the UK’s international organisation for cultural relations and educational opportunities. They build connections, understanding and trust between people in the UK and other countries through arts and culture, education and the English language. The British Council has established programmes to support Women and Girls in STEM around the world, designed with a lifecycle approach in mind, from inspiring young girls to stay in STEM to supporting women working in STEM fields reach positions of leadership and network with their peers in their region and the UK. This year, supported by the British Council, Aston University is delighted to announce our participation in the fully funded scholarships for female students from the state of Paraíba, Brazil . Each of these scholarships covers full tuition fees, monthly stipends, a return economy class ticket and other costs such as IELTS exam fee, visa application and NHS surcharge. Key facts This year, supported by the British Council, Aston University is delighted to announce our participation in the fully funded scholarships for female students from the state of Paraíba, Brazil, pursuing master’s studies in the fields of: MSc Artificial Intelligence MSc Artificial Intelligence for Health MSc Artificial Intelligence with Business Strategy MSc Data Science and Artificial Intelligence MSc Future Vehicle Technologies MSc Mechanical Engineering MSc Robotics and Autonomous Systems MSc Smart Manufacturing Each of these scholarships covers full tuition fees, monthly stipends, a return economy class ticket and other costs such as IELTS exam fee, visa application and NHS surcharge. Number of scholarships Five scholarships will be available to Aston University Students. Important dates Applications are now open. 12 April, 2026 – applications close. Mid June, 2026 – successful scholars notified. Duration The scholarship will last for the duration of your one-year MSc course starting in September 2026. How to apply To apply for the British Council Scholarships for Women in STEM, you must reside or work in the state of Paraíba, Brazil. You must have already completed an application to study on one of the eligible Aston University programmes, and demonstrate a need for financial support. Stage 1 Apply for your chosen MSc degree. Apply for your MSc Stage 2 Complete the form below for your submission for the scholarship. Scholarship submission form Eligibility critieria The Women in STEM scholarship is a partnership between Aston University, the British Council, and FAPESQ (Paraíba State Research Support Foundation). As a result, candidates selected for the scholarship must reside or work in the state of Paraíba, Brazil . To be eligible for the British Council Scholarships for Women in STEM, applicants must meet all of the following criteria: Be a woman, as defined under UK legislation. Be a permanent resident of, and hold a valid passport or recognised international travel document from, an eligible country, and be able to obtain a UK visa. Applicants must agree to return to their country of citizenship or residence for a minimum of two years after the scholarship ends, except in exceptional circumstances where return would be impossible or unsafe. Meet the entry requirements of Aston University for the chosen course, including academic qualifications and English language proficiency. Have completed all components of an undergraduate degree at the time of application. Final-year undergraduate students may be considered if they will complete their degree in time for enrolment and meet all matriculation requirements. Demonstrate a need for financial support. Applicants must not be able to privately fund their UK studies and must not be receiving financial support from another source that duplicates the core benefits of this scholarship. Private savings to supplement the scholarship are permitted. Preference may be given to applicants who have not previously had significant international exposure or studied in the UK. Short-term visits such as study tours or conferences are permitted. Clearly indicate their preferred course and institution if applying to more than one institution. Demonstrate the motivation and academic ability to successfully undertake a UK postgraduate taught course. Be active in the STEM field through relevant work experience or demonstrate a proven interest in the proposed subject area. Be willing to contribute to capacity-building and socio-economic development in their home country after completing their studies. Agree to maintain contact with the British Council, act as an ambassador for the UK, and engage with Alumni UK activities during and after their studies. Demonstrate a plan and commitment to encouraging and supporting women and girls to engage in STEM in their home country. Agree to their personal data being shared with the British Council for assessment and promotional purposes as part of the application process. Further information The scholarship covers the full costs associated with studying at Aston University, including: • Tuition fees • Up to 12-months monthly stipend at the rate of £1,731 p/month to cover costs of living, including accommodation • IELTS exam fee (for scholars without a valid Test of English) • Return economy-class travel from home country to UK • Visa and insurance / NHS surcharge costs More information about the scholarship programme can be found on the British Council website . This strategic partnership provides a valued route to Aston University. By completing an NCUK qualification - such as the International Foundation Year, International Year One, or Master's preparation programme - international students develop the skills, knowledge and confidence needed to study in the UK. They can then progress to Aston to gain a globally recognised degree from a leading UK institution. NCUK – Study at one of 100+ centres around the world Since 1987, NCUK has helped over 30,000 international students gain access to university. You have a choice of over 80 study centres worldwide to study the skills and qualifications you need to succeed at university, including the language preparation module, English for Academic Purposes (EAP). Please email us for more information on applying. Undergraduate Pathways You can study the NCUK International Foundation Year and gain entry to the first year of our undergraduate degrees. You can also study the NCUK International Year One programme and gain entry to the second year of the following programmes: BSc (Hons) Accounting and Finance BSc (Hons) Business and Management BSc (Hons) International Business and Management LLB Law For more information, visit the NCUK website . Postgraduate Pathways You can study a Master’s Preparation programme and gain the qualifications and skills you need to study a Master’s programme at Aston. For more information, visit the NCUK website . NCUK Articulation and Progression Scholarships 2026/27 NCUK Articulation and Progression Scholarship The NCUK Articulation and Progression Scholarship supports international students progressing/articulating from an NCUK pathway programme to continue their studies at Aston University, Birmingham . The scholarship provides a tuition fee reduction for eligible students progressing/articulating from an NCUK International Foundation Year (IFY), International Year One (IY1), or Master's Preparation programme (MP) and enrolling at Aston University for the September 2026 intake . The scholarship is competitive and application-based , meaning applicants must submit a scholarship application to be considered. Meeting the eligibility criteria does not guarantee that a scholarship will be awarded. All applications are assessed in line with the published eligibility requirements and scholarship availability. Scholarships are applied as a tuition fee reduction to the eligible programme of study and cannot be exchanged for cash or transferred to another programme, applicant, or intake. Scholarship values The available scholarship awards for NCUK students progressing/articulating to Aston University are shown below. NCUK Students currently studying Scholarship Value NCUK International Foundation Year (IFY) £6,500 tuition fee reduction (first year at Aston University) NCUK International Year One (IY1) £5,000 tuition fee reduction in Year 2 (first year at Aston University), with the potential to receive an additional £5,000 in the final year of study NCUK Master's Preparation programme (MP) £5,000 tuition fee reduction (first year at Aston University) For students progressing/articulating from NCUK International Year One , the scholarship may be awarded across two academic years . Students who meet the continuation requirements during their first year at Aston University may receive a further £5,000 tuition fee reduction in their final year of study . Continuation of the final-year award requires students to achieve an overall 60% average at first attempt , pass all modules at first attempt, and remain enrolled as an Overseas fee payer . How to apply To be considered for the NCUK Articulation and Progression Scholarship, applicants must complete the scholarship application form after receiving an offer to study at Aston University. Applicants will be asked to submit a short written statement as part of the application explaining why they should be considered for the scholarship. Applications are reviewed following the submission deadline. Where the number of eligible applications exceeds the available scholarship allocation, applications will be assessed competitively using the University’s internal evaluation process. Key dates Submission deadline: 14th June 2026 (midnight UK time) Scholarship outcome: 30th June 2026 Deposit deadline: 21st July 2026 (midnight UK time) Eligibility To be eligible for the NCUK Articulation and Progression Scholarship, applicants must: Be classified as an Overseas fee payer Hold an offer for a full-time Undergraduate or Postgraduate Taught programme at Aston University, Birmingham Be progressing/articulating directly from one of the following NCUK pathway programmes: NCUK International Foundation Year (IFY) NCUK International Year One (IY1) NCUK Master's Preparation programme (MP) Meet all academic and English language entry requirements Submit a completed scholarship application before the published deadline Pay the required programme deposit and enrol for the September 2026 intake . The scholarship is open to self-funded international students . Applicants whose studies are fully or partially funded by a sponsor are not normally eligible unless a formal agreement with Aston University confirms eligibility. Programme exclusions The following programmes are not eligible for the NCUK Articulation and Progression Scholarship. Undergraduate MBChB Medicine MPharm Pharmacy MOptom Optometry BSc Nursing Studies BSc Healthcare Science (Audiology) Postgraduate PGDip / MSc Overseas Pharmacy Assessment Programme (OSPAP) MSc Physician Associate Practice All MBA programmes All MRes programmes All research-only programmes Additional programme exclusions may apply where specified by the University. Terms and Conditions Full eligibility criteria, scholarship conditions and continuation requirements are outlined in the NCUK Articulation and Progression Scholarship Terms and Conditions . The full Terms and Conditions can be found below. pages.text:
INTERNATIONAL SCHOLARSHIP SCHEME TERMS & CONDITIONS:  
 2025/26 ACADEMIC YEAR INTAKE 
1. Purpose and Scope  
1.1. This document outlines the eligibility and assessment criteria for full-time International 
fee paying students to receive scholarships from Aston University. This policy is correct 
at the time of publishing (October 2024) but may be subject to change.  
1.2. Applicants who are classed as Home for tuition fee purposes should consult 
http://www.aston.ac.uk/scholarships/ and navigate to the UK student scholarship pages 
of the Aston website for details of available scholarships and terms and conditions.  
1.3. This policy applies to applicants who are classed as Overseas for tuition fee purposes. 
The relevant scholarship awards and their application criteria can be found at  
https://www2.aston.ac.uk/scholarships/international. 
1.4. The International Scholarships Scheme is subject to the terms and conditions set out in 
this document. The University reserves the right to terminate a scholarship where a 
student is in breach of any of these terms and conditions, or, if any information 
provided to the University as part of a scholarship application is found to be false or 
misleading. In such circumstances, the student will be liable for any tuition fees 
incurred.  
1.5. Joint or externally funded scholarships may be subject to different terms and conditions. 
 
2. General Provisions  
2.1 A student may be eligible for an Aston International Scholarship if:  
2.1.1 They are classed as an Overseas student for tuition fee purposes;  
2.1.2 They are holding an offer for a full-time taught programme at Aston 
University, Birmingham campus, which will start in 2025/26  
academic year (autumn, winter and spring terms);  
2.1.3 They are entering into the first year of study on a degree 
programme taught by Aston University, Birmingham campus;  
2.1.4 They meet all of the conditions set out in their offer letter;  
2.1.5 They pay their programme deposit (if applicable) by the deadline 
stipulated in their offer letter;  
2.1.6 They complete any application requirements and meet any 
additional criteria required for the scholarship schemes being 
offered, as set out on our website for each individual scholarship 
scheme.  
2.2 A student who has all or part of their fees paid by a sponsor will not be eligible for 
an Aston Scholarship unless that sponsor has an official agreement confirming 
eligibility with Aston University.  
2.2.1 Sponsors include, but are not limited to, His Majesty’s UK 
Government, overseas governments or another national body, the 
British Council or any international organisation, any international 
company, or any other university.  
2.3 Any student considered to be in debt to Aston University will not be eligible to 
receive a scholarship award in full or in part.  
2.3.1 For the purposes of this policy, a student will be considered to be in 
debt to the University if they have received the third notice that a 
payment is overdue.  
2.4 A student may only receive one Aston University discount and one Aston University 
scholarship per programme studied.  
2.5 Where a student is eligible for more than one scholarship/discount the student will 
be awarded the one of the highest value.  
2.6 Successful scholarship applicants will be awarded a scholarship in the form of a 
discount on their tuition fees for the first year of study only, unless otherwise 
advertised. Applicants will be informed by the Scholarship Panel the level of 
scholarship which has been awarded to them.  
2.7 Scholarships advertised for multiple years of study will be reconfirmed at the start 
of each academic year; you must fulfil the requirements below: 
2.7.1 Maintenance of an average grade equivalent to an upper second-
class degree grade at Aston University and passing all modules of 
study at first attempt. For NCUK multi-year scholarships, students 
must maintain an average grade equivalent to a first class degree 
and pass all modules of study at first attempt.  
2.7.2 Pass all modules without any re-assessments of any assessment 
components (retake of examination, coursework, test etc.) 
2.8 At Aston’s discretion, clauses 2.2-2.7 may be waived under specific conditions or for 
specific scholarships schemes or campaigns. Details of any waiver will be set out on 
our website.  
 
3. Applying for a Scholarship  
3.1 Applications for International Scholarships must be made by following the 
instructions set out on our website for each scholarship. Failure to follow these 
instructions fully may render an application void.  
3.2 There are a number of different categories of scholarships. Under some 
categories, student’s eligibility will be assessed automatically by the University’s 
Admissions Office based on the information provided in the application to study 
on an Aston University degree programme. Students who are eligible for 
scholarship categories which automatically apply, will receive an offer of a 
scholarship from Aston’s Admissions Office.  
3.3 The University reserves the right to limit the number of awards under certain 
scholarship schemes, this will be indicated on the web site when the scholarship 
is announced. The deadline for the application or consideration for the awards 
will also be stated on the web site. 
3.3.1 The University may change the number of awards and move the 
application deadline by providing a minimum of 30 days notice to 
the students on the website. 
3.3.2 Where there is a limited number of awards available, the 
consideration and award allocation may be conducted on a first 
come first served basis. In such cases the scholarship scheme will be 
closed without notice once all awards are accepted. 
3.4 Other categories of scholarship require an additional scholarship application to 
be submitted, usually in the form of a short personal statement or a video, or an 
interview to be conducted. Please consult our website for more information on 
how to apply for each scholarship scheme before submitting the application. 
Students are required to confirm that any material submitted as part of their 
application is their own work and does not infringe the intellectual property 
rights of a third party. The Use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools in scholarship 
application will render the application void. Scholarship interviews must be 
undertaken by the student who has applied for the scholarship.  
3.4.1 Any scholarship applications with materials not accessible to Aston 
University staff to review and assess will not be considered and not 
be eligible for later reconsideration.  
3.4.2 Aston University has the right to re-use scholarship application 
material in future marketing campaigns.  
3.5 In order to be awarded a scholarship, a student must meet the scholarship 
application deadline of the particular scholarship award. For automatic 
scholarships, this means accepting the course place before the acceptance 
deadline, outlined in the offer letter. For application or interview-based 
scholarships, this means completing the scholarship application form through 
our website by the deadline stated for that particular scholarship award which 
will be advertised on our website.  
3.6 Scholarship applicants should read in full the scholarship application and 
eligibility criteria prior to applying for a scholarship, as set out on our website.  
3.7 Students are entitled to apply for more than one scholarship award; however, 
students will only be awarded one scholarship, of the highest value (see 2.2-2.7).  
3.8 Applications will only be considered for international students holding an offer 
to study a full-time taught programme at Aston’s Birmingham campus in the UK.  
3.9 Students studying online, via blended learning, part time or any other method of 
learning, research programmes are not eligible for scholarships covered by these 
terms and conditions.  
3.10 Some scholarship awards come with additional benefits or responsibilities, 
for example, working as an ambassador for Aston University. Any additional 
benefits or responsibilities will be listed on Aston’s website.  
 
4. Approving and Awarding of Scholarships 
4.1 Scholarships are a discount made against the tuition fee applicable to the 
specific programme of study that the student is seeking to enrol upon. No cash 
or cost of living alternative is available.  
4.2 Scholarship entitlement will normally be approved before the commencement of 
the degree programme. It is not possible to consider a student for a new 
scholarship award once the degree programme has commenced.  
4.3 If a Scholarship has been awarded, the fee discount will be applied to the 
student’s tuition fee liability. Aston Scholarships will normally be available only 
to students who have been in attendance, as defined by the University 
throughout term one and term two and are still in attendance at the start of 
term three. Students who withdraw from Aston University part way through an 
academic year will not be eligible to receive a scholarship in respect of that year. 
Any tuition fee discount applied to the student for that academic year as the 
result of an Aston Scholarship will be withdrawn and the student will be liable 
for the full cost for that period.  
4.4 Students who are repeating any modules within the programme are not eligible 
for scholarships regardless of whether they are repeating with attendance, 
without attendance, or with partial attendance.  
4.5 Where a student suspends their studies and takes a Leave of Absence for a 
complete academic year (i.e. October to October) no tuition fee is charged and, 
therefore, the student will not be eligible to receive a scholarship.  
4.6 Students who suspend their studies part way through an academic year and take 
a Leave of Absence will be eligible to receive a scholarship for the academic 
terms they have completed in full. The amount of the scholarship will be 
calculated on a pro rata basis and in line with Aston University’s Tuition Fees 
Charging Policy.  
4.7 Scholarships are valid for study on a taught programme at Aston University, 
Birmingham Campus and are not transferable to another campus or University.  
4.7.1 Specific programmes are excluded from this scholarships schemes 
unless otherwise stated. The affected programmes are: 
1. MBCHB in Medicine 
2. PGDIP/ MSC in OSPAP 
3. MSC in Physician Associate Practice 
4. BSc Nursing Studies (Registered Nurse Mental Health Nursing/ 
Registered Nurse Adult Nursing) 
4.8 The scholarships are valid for programmes of study commencing in the academic 
year 2025/26 only and cannot be carried forward to another academic year.  
4.9 Scholarships are valid for the specified programme of study at Aston University 
and may not normally be transferred to a different programme.  
4.10  Any evidence submitted after the final decision on the student’s eligibility 
has been made will not be considered, unless the student can demonstrate 
there was a good reason why the information could not be made available at the 
time of submitting the scholarship application.  
4.11 The decision of the awarding panel is final. Applicants may appeal against 
the decision only if they can show that there has been a procedural error. 
Appeals should be addressed to the Director of Student and Academic Services.  
 
Terms & Conditions published: October 2024  
Terms & Conditions validity: Academic year 2025/26 only  
Further Information: Contact Aston’s International Office (international@aston.ac.uk)  
END

We are excited to announce THREE Ferguson scholarships for September 2026. Each candidate can look to receive full tuition cover (value of £22,500) exclusively available to students from Africa and India for the 2026/27 academic year. With £6,000 additional contribution towards living costs. These scholarships are supported by the Allan and Nesta Ferguson Charitable Trust who are dedicated to improving educational opportunities for students who would not otherwise be able to consider studying in the UK. Apply for a chance to receive a full tuition fee cover of £22,500 and contribution of £6,000 towards living cost. Please note applications for the Ferguson Sholarship have now closed. Who can apply? The Ferguson Scholarships are available to students applying for one of the following postgraduate taught programmes: MSc Pharmaceutical Sciences MSc Drug Delivery MSc Pharmacokinetics MSc Stem Cells & Regenerative Medicine MSc Biotechnology MSc Psychology (Conversion programme) MSc Neuroscience for Drug Discovery MSc Addiction and Mental Health MSc Bioinformatics and Genomic Medicine Master of Public Health (MPH) What is the eligibility criteria? You must hold a conditional or unconditional offer for one of the above courses Be a national from India or an African country Hold a 2:1 degree or equivalent in a relevant subject for the course you are applying for Be a self-funded student. No agency referred candidates would be eligible. If successful, note you will be required to provide evidence to the UKVI that you can fully contribute to your living costs. How do I apply? Submit an application for your chosen course by selecting ' APPLY NOW ' on the course web pages (select appropriate programme from list above). NB: you will be asked to include your 9 digit application number beginning 25……… The announcements for the applications for this scholarship are to be made by 30 June 2025 (midnight UK time). Please note that this is the final extended deadline for applications. No agency referred candidates would be eligible. (Your submission will be automatically removed for review). What happens next? The announcement of the awards will be in June 2026 via email. If you have any further questions or queries regarding this scholarship, please contact Bhavisha Koner HLS_Exchange@aston.ac.uk . XJTU ARTICULATION SCHOLARSHIP 
2026/27 Academic Year – September 2026 Intake  
1. Purpose and Scope 
1.1 These Terms and Conditions govern the XJTU Articulation Scholarship available 
to eligible students progressing to Aston University under the formally approved 
Articulation Agreement between Xi’an Jiaotong University (XJTU) and Aston 
University. 
1.2 The Scholarship applies exclusively to students articulating under the agreed 
articulation structure and approved programme mapping for the defined intake. 
1.3 The Scholarship is automatic, fixed-value, non-competitive, and applies only to the 
intake specified above. 
1.4 No precedent is created for future academic years. 
2. Definitions 
For the purposes of these Terms and Conditions: 
2.1 Articulation Agreement 
The formally approved academic progression agreement between Xi’an Jiaotong 
University and Aston University governing the defined articulation structure, 
academic mapping, entry requirements, and progression framework. 
2.2 Agreed Articulation Programmes 
The Aston University programmes formally approved under the Articulation 
Agreement for the relevant intake cohort. 
2.3 Articulating Student 
A student who has successfully completed the required stage of study at Xi’an 
Jiaotong University and is progressing directly to Aston University in accordance with 
the Articulation Agreement. 
2.4 Overseas 
A student classified as Overseas for tuition fee purposes under Aston University’s fee 
status assessment regulations. 
2.5 Self-funded 
A student whose tuition fees are not wholly or partially funded, sponsored, 
reimbursed, or otherwise supported by: 
• An employer 
• A government body 
• A scholarship agency 
• A commercial sponsor 
• Any third-party organisation 
Family financial support and personal bank loans are treated as self-funded. 
5 
XJTU ARTICULATION SCHOLARSHIP 
2026/27 Academic Year – September 2026 Intake  
2.6 Programme Deposit 
The tuition fee deposit required to secure an offer of study, as specified in the 
applicant’s offer letter. 
2.7 Enrolment 
Completion of all academic registration, immigration compliance, and attendance 
requirements as determined by Aston University. 
3. General Eligibility Requirements 
3.1 Applicants must be Articulating Students under the approved Articulation 
Agreement. 
3.2 Award of the Scholarship remains conditional upon formal confirmation from Xi’an 
Jiaotong University that the student has successfully completed the required stage of 
study in accordance with the Articulation Agreement. 
3.3 Applicants must hold a valid offer for one of the Agreed Articulation Programmes. 
3.4 Applicants must satisfy all academic and non- academic conditions stated in their 
offer letter. 
3.5 Applicants must articulate in the immediate intake following completion of the 
required stage at XJTU. The Scholarship is not deferrable. Students who defer entry 
will be reassessed under the Terms and Conditions applicable to the new intake. 
3.6 Applicants must be classified as Overseas for tuition fee purposes. Fee status will 
be assessed at the point of enrolment. Where fee status changes at any time prior to 
or during enrolment, eligibility will be reassessed. 
3.7 Applicants must be self -funded at the point of enrolment. Where funding status 
changes at any time prior to or during enrolment, eligibility will be reassessed and the 
Scholarship may be withdrawn. 
3.8 The Scholarship is available only to students progressing under the formal 
Articulation Agreement and is not available to applicants from XJTU applying 
independently outside the articulation route. 
3.9 Eligibility for the Scholarship does not constitute a contractual entitlement. The 
Scholarship remains subject to verification, institutional approval processes, and 
compliance with University regulations. 
3.10 Aston University reserves the right to verify articulation eligibility, academic 
completion, fee status and funding status directly with Xi’an Jiaotong University or 
relevant authorities. 
4. Scholarship Structure 
4.1 The Scholarship provides a fixed tuition fee discount of £5,000. 
6 
XJTU ARTICULATION SCHOLARSHIP 
2026/27 Academic Year – September 2026 Intake  
4.2 The Scholarship is calculated from the gross published international tuition fee 
applicable for the academic year of enrolment. 
4.3 The Scholarship applies to one academic year of study at Aston University only. 
4.4 The Scholarship value will be deducted from tuition fees only and will not reduce 
or replace the Programme Deposit payable. 
4.5 The Scholarship has no cash value and cannot be exchanged, transferred, or 
offset against accommodation, living expenses, immigration costs, repeat study, 
additional modules, or placement or study abroad years. 
4.6 Awarding this Scholarship does not create entitlement to any continuation award 
beyond the defined articulation year. 
5. Scholarship Availability, Confirmation, and Activation 
5.1 Offer Stage 
Where eligibility is confirmed, the Scholarship may be referenced within the offer 
letter as part of the articulation arrangement. Inclusion in an offer letter does not 
constitute application of the award to the tuition fee account and does not create 
unconditional entitlement. 
5.2 Deposit Deadline and Trigger 
Payment of the required Programme Deposit in full by the deadline specified in the 
offer letter is the formal trigger for scholarship confirmation. 
5.3 The Scholarship will not be applied to the student record unless and until the 
deposit has been received in full. 
5.4 Failure to meet the deposit deadline may result in withdrawal of the Scholarship. 
5.5 Activation on Enrolment 
The Scholarship becomes active only upon successful Enrolment at Aston 
University. 
5.6 Where a student withdraws prior to enrolment, fails to obtain a visa, fails 
credibility or immigration compliance requirements, or does not complete enrolment, 
the Scholarship will lapse automatically. 
5.7 Administrative Accuracy and Audit 
Where a Scholarship has been applied in error, including due to administrative or 
system error, Aston University reserves the right to amend or withdraw the award, 
including after enrolment. Application in error does not create entitlement. 
5.8 Aston University reserves the right to audit articulation eligibility, fee status, 
funding status and enrolment records at any stage. Where discrepancies are 
identified, the Scholarship may be amended or withdrawn. 
7 
XJTU ARTICULATION SCHOLARSHIP 
2026/27 Academic Year – September 2026 Intake  
6. Combination and Exclusivity 
6.1 A student may normally hold only one Aston University scholarship per programme 
of study. 
6.2 The Scholarship cannot be combined with any other Aston University scholarship, 
bursary, tuition fee discount, partnership award, or financial incentive unless explicitly 
confirmed in writing by Aston University. 
6.3 Where awards are calculated using different methodologies, Aston University will 
determine which single award represents the higher value. Only one award will apply. 
6.4 Where tuition fees become wholly or partially funded by an employer, government, 
organisation, or third party at any stage prior to or during enrolment, the Scholarship 
will normally be withdrawn. 
7. Receiving and Retaining the Scholarship 
7.1 The Scholarship will be applied only after the Programme Deposit has been paid 
and the student has successfully enrolled. 
7.2 Students must remain fully enrolled and in attendance. 
7.3 Students must comply with all University regulations and UK immigration 
requirements. 
7.4 If a student’s fee status changes from Overseas to Home at any stage prior to or 
during enrolment, the Scholarship will be withdrawn. 
7.5 The Scholarship is strictly linked to the Agreed Articulation Programmes as defined 
for the intake cohort. Any transfer outside the approved articulation mapping will result 
in automatic withdrawal of the Scholarship. 
7.6 Where a student withdraws after enrolment, the tuition fee discount may be 
recalculated proportionately in accordance with the University’s Tuition Fees Charging 
Policy. 
7.7 Students repeating modules are not eligible in respect of repeated study. 
7.8 Where a student suspends studies, eligibility will be reassessed in line with 
University policy. 
8. Appeals and Final Decision 
8.1 Decisions are made in accordance with these Terms and Conditions and internal 
procedures. The University’s decision is final. 
8.2 Appeals may be submitted only on the grounds of procedural error. 
8 
XJTU ARTICULATION SCHOLARSHIP 
2026/27 Academic Year – September 2026 Intake  
8.3 Appeals will not be considered on the basis of academic judgement, articulation 
verification, fee status assessment, funding changes, immigration outcomes, or 
personal circumstances. 
8.4 The University is not required to disclose internal assessments, deliberations, or 
verification processes. 
8.5 The University will not enter into further correspondence once the appeals process 
has concluded. 
9. Interpretation, Precedence, and Governing Law 
9.1 In the event of any inconsistency between these Terms and Conditions and any 
other University publication, webpage, correspondence, or third-party communication, 
these Terms and Conditions shall take precedence. 
9.2 No representation made by an agent, representative, or third party shall be binding 
unless confirmed in writing by Aston University. 
9.3 Any discretion exercised by the University does not create precedent or entitlement 
for other applicants or future intakes. 
9.4 These Terms and Conditions are governed by and construed in accordance with 
the laws of England and Wales. 
Terms & Conditions Validity 
These Terms and Conditions apply solely to the intake specified above. Aston 
University reserves the right to amend, suspend, vary, or withdraw the Scholarship for 
future intakes. 
Further Information and Enquiries 
All enquiries relating to the XJTU Articulation Scholarship should be directed to: 
Aston University International Office 
Email: international@aston.ac.uk 
 
 
END

VNUK ARTICULATION SCHOLARSHIP
