1. Purpose and Scope 
1.1 These Terms and Conditions govern the VN-UK Institute for Research and 
Executive Education Articulation Scholarship available to eligible students 
progressing to Aston University under the formally approved Articulation Agreement 
between the VN-UK Institute for Research and Executive Education and Aston 
University. 
1.2 The Scholarship applies exclusively to students articulating under the agreed 
articulation structure and approved programme mapping for the defined intake. 
1.3 The Scholarship is automatic, fixed-value, non-competitive, and applies only to 
the intake specified above. 
1.4 No precedent is created for future academic years. 
2. Definitions 
For the purposes of these Terms and Conditions: 
2.1 Articulation Agreement 
The formally approved academic progression agreement between the VN-UK 
Institute for Research and Executive Education and Aston University governing the 
defined articulation structure, academic mapping, entry requirements, and 
progression framework. 
2.2 Agreed Articulation Programmes 
The Aston University programmes formally approved under the Articulation 
Agreement for the relevant intake cohort. 
2.3 Articulating Student 
A student who has successfully completed the required stage of study at the VN-UK 
Institute for Research and Executive Education and is progressing directly to Aston 
University in accordance with the Articulation Agreement. 
2.4 Overseas 
A student classified as Overseas for tuition fee purposes under Aston University’s fee 
status assessment regulations. 
2.5 Self-funded 
A student whose tuition fees are not wholly or partially funded, sponsored, 
reimbursed, or otherwise supported by: 
• An employer 
• A government body 
• A scholarship agency 
• A commercial sponsor 
• Any third-party organisation 
5 
VNUK ARTICULATION SCHOLARSHIP 
2026/27 Academic Year – September 2026 Intake  
Family financial support and personal bank loans are treated as self-funded. 
2.6 Programme Deposit 
The tuition fee deposit required to secure an offer of study, as specified in the 
applicant’s offer letter. 
2.7 Enrolment 
Completion of all academic registration, immigration compliance, and attendance 
requirements as determined by Aston University. 
3. General Eligibility Requirements 
3.1 Applicants must be Articulating Students under the approved Articulation 
Agreement. 
3.2 Award of the Scholarship remains conditional upon formal confirmation from the 
VN-UK Institute for Research and Executive Education that the student has 
successfully completed the required stage of study in accordance with the 
Articulation Agreement. 
3.3 Applicants must hold a valid offer for one of the Agreed Articulation Programmes. 
3.4 Applicants must satisfy all academic and non-academic conditions stated in their 
offer letter. 
3.5 Applicants must articulate in the immediate intake following completion of the 
required stage at the VN-UK Institute for Research and Executive Education. The 
Scholarship is not deferrable. Students who defer entry will be reassessed under the 
Terms and Conditions applicable to the new intake. 
3.6 Applicants must be classified as Overseas for tuition fee purposes. Fee status 
will be assessed at the point of enrolment. Where fee status changes at any time 
prior to or during enrolment, eligibility will be reassessed. 
3.7 Applicants must be self-funded at the point of enrolment. Where funding status 
changes at any time prior to or during enrolment, eligibility will be reassessed and 
the Scholarship may be withdrawn. 
3.8 The Scholarship is available only to students progressing under the formal 
Articulation Agreement and is not available to applicants from the VN-UK Institute 
applying independently outside the articulation route. 
3.9 Eligibility for the Scholarship does not constitute a contractual entitlement. The 
Scholarship remains subject to verification, institutional approval processes, and 
compliance with University regulations. 
6 
VNUK ARTICULATION SCHOLARSHIP 
2026/27 Academic Year – September 2026 Intake  
3.10 Aston University reserves the right to verify articulation eligibility, academic 
completion, fee status and funding status directly with the VN-UK Institute for 
Research and Executive Education or relevant authorities. 
4. Scholarship Structure 
4.1 The Scholarship provides a fixed tuition fee discount of £6,000. 
4.2 The Scholarship is calculated from the gross published international tuition fee 
applicable for the academic year of enrolment. 
4.3 The Scholarship applies to one academic year of study at Aston University only. 
4.4 The Scholarship value will be deducted from tuition fees only and will not reduce 
or replace the Programme Deposit payable. 
4.5 The Scholarship has no cash value and cannot be exchanged, transferred, or 
offset against accommodation, living expenses, immigration costs, repeat study, 
additional modules, or placement or study abroad years. 
4.6 Awarding this Scholarship does not create entitlement to any continuation award 
beyond the defined articulation year. 
5. Scholarship Availability, Confirmation, and Activation 
5.1 Offer Stage 
Where eligibility is confirmed, the Scholarship may be referenced within the offer 
letter as part of the articulation arrangement. Inclusion in an offer letter does not 
constitute application of the award to the tuition fee account and does not create 
unconditional entitlement. 
5.2 Deposit Deadline and Trigger 
Payment of the required Programme Deposit in full by the deadline specified in the 
offer letter is the formal trigger for scholarship confirmation. 
5.3 The Scholarship will not be applied to the student record unless and until the 
deposit has been received in full. 
5.4 Failure to meet the deposit deadline may result in withdrawal of the Scholarship. 
5.5 Activation on Enrolment 
The Scholarship becomes active only upon successful Enrolment at Aston 
University. 
5.6 Where a student withdraws prior to enrolment, fails to obtain a visa, fails 
credibility or immigration compliance requirements, or does not complete enrolment, 
the Scholarship will lapse automatically. 
7 
VNUK ARTICULATION SCHOLARSHIP 
2026/27 Academic Year – September 2026 Intake  
5.7 Administrative Accuracy and Audit 
Where a Scholarship has been applied in error, including due to administrative or 
system error, Aston University reserves the right to amend or withdraw the award, 
including after enrolment. Application in error does not create entitlement. 
5.8 Aston University reserves the right to audit articulation eligibility, fee status, 
funding status and enrolment records at any stage. Where discrepancies are 
identified, the Scholarship may be amended or withdrawn. 
6. Combination and Exclusivity 
6.1 A student may normally hold only one Aston University scholarship per 
programme of study. 
6.2 The Scholarship cannot be combined with any other Aston University 
scholarship, bursary, tuition fee discount, partnership award, or financial incentive 
unless explicitly confirmed in writing by Aston University. 
6.3 Where awards are calculated using different methodologies, Aston University will 
determine which single award represents the higher value. Only one award will 
apply. 
6.4 Where tuition fees become wholly or partially funded by an employer, 
government, organisation, or third party at any stage prior to or during enrolment, the 
Scholarship will normally be withdrawn. 
7. Receiving and Retaining the Scholarship 
7.1 The Scholarship will be applied only after the Programme Deposit has been paid 
and the student has successfully enrolled. 
7.2 Students must remain fully enrolled and in attendance. 
7.3 Students must comply with all University regulations and UK immigration 
requirements. 
7.4 If a student’s fee status changes from Overseas to Home at any stage prior to or 
during enrolment, the Scholarship will be withdrawn. 
7.5 The Scholarship is strictly linked to the Agreed Articulation Programmes as 
defined for the intake cohort. Any transfer outside the approved articulation mapping 
will result in automatic withdrawal of the Scholarship. 
7.6 Where a student withdraws after enrolment, the tuition fee discount may be 
recalculated proportionately in accordance with the University’s Tuition Fees 
Charging Policy. 
7.7 Students repeating modules are not eligible in respect of repeated study. 
8 
VNUK ARTICULATION SCHOLARSHIP 
2026/27 Academic Year – September 2026 Intake  
7.8 Where a student suspends studies, eligibility will be reassessed in line with 
University policy. 
8. Appeals and Final Decision 
8.1 Decisions are made in accordance with these Terms and Conditions and internal 
procedures. The University’s decision is final. 
8.2 Appeals may be submitted only on the grounds of procedural error. 
8.3 Appeals will not be considered on the basis of academic judgement, articulation 
verification, fee status assessment, funding changes, immigration outcomes, or 
personal circumstances. 
8.4 The University is not required to disclose internal assessments, deliberations, or 
verification processes. 
8.5 The University will not enter into further correspondence once the appeals 
process has concluded. 
9. Interpretation, Precedence, and Governing Law 
9.1 In the event of any inconsistency between these Terms and Conditions and any 
other University publication, webpage, correspondence, or third-party 
communication, these Terms and Conditions shall take precedence. 
9.2 No representation made by an agent, representative, or third party shall be 
binding unless confirmed in writing by Aston University. 
9.3 Any discretion exercised by the University does not create precedent or 
entitlement for other applicants or future intakes. 
9.4 These Terms and Conditions are governed by and construed in accordance with 
the laws of England and Wales. 
Terms & Conditions Validity 
These Terms and Conditions apply solely to the intake specified above. Aston 
University reserves the right to amend, suspend, vary, or withdraw the Scholarship 
for future intakes. 
Further Information and Enquiries 
All enquiries relating to the VN-UK Institute for Research and Executive Education 
Articulation Scholarship should be directed to: 
Aston University International Office 
Email: international@aston.ac.uk  
END

Purpose and Scope 
This document outlines the eligibility criteria, assessment basis, award structure, 
allocation principles, and conditions for students articulating from approved Symbiosis 
International University (India) dual degree programmes to Aston University, 
Birmingham campus, for the September 2026 intake. 
The Scholarship applies only to students enrolled on the formally agreed dual degree 
programmes delivered under the Aston University – Symbiosis International University 
Articulation Agreement, as published by Symbiosis International University. 
The Symbiosis Articulation Scholarship is automatic, merit-based, subject to a capped 
allocation, and offered as a tuition fee discount for the first year of study at Aston 
University. 
Students complete their final award with Aston University. The Scholarship is assessed 
on academic performance achieved at Symbiosis prior to articulation. 
These Terms and Conditions apply to the September 2026 intake only. Aston 
University reserves the right to amend, suspend, vary, or withdraw the Scholarship for 
future intakes. No precedent is created for subsequent academic years. 
Definitions 
Articulation Agreement 
The formal academic agreement between Aston University and Symbiosis 
International University (India) defining approved dual degree progression routes. 
Overseas 
A student classified as Overseas for tuition fee purposes under Aston University’s fee 
status assessment regulations. 
Self-funded 
A student whose tuition fees are not wholly or partially funded or reimbursed by an 
employer, government, organisation, or third party. Family financial support and 
personal bank loans are treated as self-funded. 
Enrolment 
Completion of all registration, immigration, and attendance requirements as 
determined by Aston University. 
Programme Deposit 
The tuition fee deposit required to secure an offer of study, as specified in the 
applicant’s offer letter. 
1. General Provisions 
1.1 Applicants must be classified as Overseas for tuition fee purposes. 
3

1.2 Applicants must articulate directly under the approved Articulation Agreement from 
one of the formally mapped dual degree programmes. 
1.3 Applicants must hold a valid offer for a full -time undergraduate or postgraduate 
programme delivered on campus at Aston University, Birmingham, commencing in 
September 2026. 
1.4 The Scholarship remains conditional upon the applicant maintaining a valid offer 
of admission. If the offer is withdrawn, amended, or conditions are not met, scholarship 
eligibility will be reassessed or withdrawn. 
1.5 Applicants must meet all academic and non- academic conditions stated in their 
offer letter. 
1.6 Applicants must be self-funded. Students whose tuition fees are wholly or partially 
funded or reimbursed by an employer, government, organisation, or third party are not 
eligible. 
1.7 Applicants must articulate in the immediate subsequent intake following 
completion of the Symbiosis stage. The Scholarship cannot be deferred. Applicants 
who defer will be subject to the scholarship provisions and Terms and Conditions 
applicable to their new year of entry. 
1.8 The Scholarship is available only to students based at Symbiosis International 
University, India. Students studying at Symbiosis Dubai or any other campus are not 
eligible. 
1.9 Meeting the eligibility criteria does not create an unconditional entitlement to the 
Scholarship. The Scholarship is awarded only once academic verification, deposit 
payment, and enrolment requirements have been satisfied. 
2. Scholarship Basis and Academic Criteria 
2.1 Automatic Merit-Based Award 
The Scholarship is an automatic, non- competitive, merit-based award. No separate 
scholarship application is required. 
2.2 Academic Assessment 
2.2.1 Eligibility is based solely on academic performance achieved in the final stage 
completed at Symbiosis International University prior to articulation. 
2.2.2 Students must have passed all modules at first attempt. Resits are not permitted. 
2.2.3 Students with failed modules are not eligible. 
2.2.4 Rounding of academic averages is not permitted. 
4 
SYMBIOSIS ARTICULATION MERIT SCHOLARSHIP 
2026/27 Academic Year – September 2026 Intake  
2.2.5 Assessment is based only on official academic transcripts available at the point 
of offer. 
2.2.6 Amendments to transcripts after the offer stage will not be considered. 
2.2.7 UK classification equivalency is determined by Aston University Admissions in 
accordance with agreed internal mapping. The internal percentage mapping is 
confidential and not published. 
2.2.8 The equivalency framework applicable at the time offers are issued for the 
September 2026 intake will apply to all applicants for that intake. Changes to 
equivalency mapping will not be applied retrospectively. 
2.2.9 Equivalency decisions are final and not subject to academic re-evaluation. 
3. Scholarship Availability, Allocation, and Award 
3.1 Scholarship Levels

tuition fee applicable at the point of enrolment for the September 2026 intake. 
3.3 The percentage award is subject to an internal maximum monetary cap. Where 
the calculated percentage exceeds the internal cap, the lower value will apply. 
3.4 The Scholarship applies to the first year of study at Aston University only. 
3.5 The Scholarship has no cash value and cannot be exchanged, transferred, or 
offset against non-tuition charges. 
3.6 The Scholarship does not apply to deposits, accommodation, living expenses, 
immigration costs, repeat study, additional modules, or placement / study abroad years 
unless confirmed in writing. 
3.7 The Scholarship is subject to a capped allocation determined by Aston University.

3.9 The University is not required to disclose ranking positions, thresholds, or 
comparative cohort performance. 
3.10 The University reserves the right not to award all available scholarships. 
3.11 Scholarship Offer at Offer Stage 
Where an applicant is assessed as meeting the academic criteria, the Scholarship 
may be included in the offer letter as an incentive to convert. 
Inclusion in an offer letter does not constitute application of the award to the tuition fee 
account and does not create unconditional entitlement. 
3.12 Deposit Trigger 
Payment of the required Programme Deposit is the trigger for scholarship 
confirmation. 
The Scholarship will not be applied to the student record unless and until the deposit 
has been received. 
3.13 Activation on Enrolment 
The Scholarship becomes active only upon successful Enrolment at Aston University. 
3.14 Administrative Application 
Where a Scholarship has been applied in error, including due to administrative or 
system error, Aston University reserves the right to amend or withdraw the award, 
including after enrolment. Application in error does not create entitlement. 
Where an applicant withdraws prior to enrolment, the Scholarship offer will lapse 
automatically. 
4. Awarding the Scholarship 
4.1 The Scholarship is awarded as a tuition fee discount only. 
4.2 A student may normally hold only one Aston University scholarship per programme 
of study. 
4.3 The Scholarship cannot be combined with any other Aston University scholarship, 
bursary, tuition fee discount, or financial incentive. 
4.4 Where awards are calculated using different methodologies, Aston University will 
determine which award represents the higher value. 
4.5 The Scholarship is not transferable to another applicant, programme, intake, 
academic year, or institution. 
6 
SYMBIOSIS ARTICULATION MERIT SCHOLARSHIP 
2026/27 Academic Year – September 2026 Intake  
4.6 Scholarships are valid only for the September 2026 intake. 
5. Receiving and Retaining the Scholarship 
5.1 The Scholarship will be applied only after the Programme Deposit has been paid 
and the student has successfully enrolled. 
5.2 Students must remain fully enrolled and in attendance. 
5.3 Students must comply with all Aston University regulations and applicable UK 
immigration requirements. 
5.4 If a student’s fee status changes from Overseas to Home, the Scholarship will be 
withdrawn. 
5.5 Where a student transfers to a programme outside the approved articulation 
mapping, the Scholarship will be withdrawn. 
5.6 Students who withdraw part-way through an academic year may have the tuition 
fee discount removed. 
5.7 Students repeating modules are not eligible in respect of repeated study. 
5.8 Where a student suspends studies, eligibility will be reassessed in line with the 
University’s Tuition Fees Charging Policy. 
6. Appeals and Final Decision 
6.1 Decisions are made in accordance with these Terms and Conditions and internal 
procedures. The University’s decision is final. 
6.2 Appeals may only be made on the grounds of procedural error. 
6.3 Appeals will not be considered on the basis of academic judgement, equivalency 
determination, recalculation of averages, transcript interpretation, ranking outcome, 
personal circumstances, or comparison with other applicants. 
6.4 The University is not required to disclose internal assessments, ranking processes, 
or deliberative materials. 
6.5 The University will not enter into further correspondence once the appeals process 
has concluded. 
7. Interpretation, Precedence, and Governing Law 
7.1 In the event of any inconsistency between these Terms and Conditions and any 
other University publication, webpage, correspondence, or third-party communication, 
these Terms and Conditions shall take precedence. 
7

2026/27 Academic Year – September 2026 Intake  
7.2 No representation made by an agent, representative, or third party shall be binding 
unless confirmed in writing by Aston University. 
7.3 Any discretion exercised by the University does not create precedent or entitlement 
for other applicants. 
7.4 These Terms and Conditions are governed by and construed in accordance with 
the laws of England and Wales. 
Terms & Conditions Validity 
2026/27 Academic Year (September 2026 intake only)

All enquiries relating to the Symbiosis Articulation Merit Scholarship should be directed

6.6 Where a student withdraws after enrolment, the tuition fee discount may be 
recalculated proportionately in accordance with the University’s Tuition Fees Charging 
Policy. 
6.7 Students repeating modules are not eligible in respect of repeated study. 
6.8 Where a student suspends studies, eligibility will be reassessed in line with 
University policy. 
6 
NEFU ARTICULATION SCHOLARSHIP 
2026/27 Academic Year – September 2026 Intake  
7. Appeals and Final Decision 
7.1 Decisions are made in accordance with these Terms and Conditions and internal 
procedures. The University’s decision is final. 
7.2 Appeals may be submitted only on the grounds of procedural error. 
7.3 Appeals will not be considered on the basis of academic judgement, articulation 
verification, fee status assessment, funding changes, immigration outcomes, or 
personal circumstances. 
7.4 The University is not required to disclose internal assessments, deliberations, or 
verification processes. 
7.5 The University will not enter into further correspondence once the appeals process 
has concluded. 
8. Interpretation, Precedence, and Governing Law 
8.1 In the event of any inconsistency between these Terms and Conditions and any 
other University publication, webpage, correspondence, or third-party communication, 
these Terms and Conditions shall take precedence. 
8.2 No representation made by an agent, representative, or third party shall be binding 
unless confirmed in writing by Aston University. 
8.3 Any discretion exercised by the University does not create precedent or entitlement 
for other applicants or future intakes. 
8.4 These Terms and Conditions are governed by and construed in accordance with 
the laws of England and Wales. 
Terms & Conditions Validity

These Terms and Conditions apply solely to the intake specified above. Aston

future intakes without notice.

GLOBAL ARTICULATION AND PROGRESSION SCHOLARSHIP 
2026/27 Academic Year – September 2026 Intake 
Purpose and Scope 
This document outlines the eligibility, assessment criteria and conditions for self -
funded international applicants progressing to Aston University under a formally 
approved Progression or Articulation Agreement to be considered for the Global 
Partnership Scholarship. 
The Global Partnership Scholarship applies to all foundation, pathway and university-
level programmes delivered under a formal progression or articulation agreement 
where Aston University does not operate a separate, dedicated or ring -fenced 
scholarship or fee-discount arrangement for that partnership. 
All applications are assessed in line with the published eligibility criteria and these 
Terms and Conditions. Scholarship awards are subject to University approval and 
overall availability. 
These Terms and Conditions are correct at the time of publication and may be subject 
to change. 
Definitions 
For the purposes of these Terms and Conditions: 
Progression or Articulation Agreement 
A formally approved institutional agreement between Aston University and a partner 
institution governing academic mapping, entry requirements, progression structure 
and eligibility framework. 
Eligible Partnership Route 
A defined foundation, pathway, undergraduate or postgraduate progression route 
delivered under a formally approved agreement for which Aston University operates 
a separate scholarship or fee-discount framework. 
Progressing Student 
A student progressing directly to Aston University in accordance with an approved 
Progression or Articulation Agreement. 
Eligible Programme 
A full-time undergraduate or postgraduate taught programme delivered at Aston 
University, excluding programmes listed in Clause 3. 
Overseas 
A student classified as Overseas for tuition fee purposes under Aston University’s fee 
status regulations. 
Self-funded 
A student whose tuition fees are not wholly or partially funded, reimbursed or 
sponsored by: 
• An employer; 
5 
GLOBAL ARTICULATION AND PROGRESSION SCHOLARSHIP 
2026/27 Academic Year – September 2026 Intake 
• A government body; 
• A scholarship agency; 
• A commercial sponsor; 
• Any third-party organisation. 
Family support and personal loans are treated as self-funded. 
Programme Deposit 
The tuition fee deposit required to secure an offer of admission, as specified in the 
applicant’s offer letter. 
Enrolment 
Completion of all academic registration, immigration compliance and attendance 
requirements as determined by Aston University. 
Allocation 
The capped number of scholarships available for the defined intake, determined at 
the sole discretion of Aston University and not externally published. 
Assessment Panel 
The internal panel responsible for reviewing and confirming scholarship decisions in 
accordance with established procedures. 
1. General Provisions 
1.1 Applicants must be classified as Overseas for tuition fee purposes. 
1.2 Applicants must be progressing under a formally approved Progression or 
Articulation Agreement from an eligible partner institution delivering foundation, 
pathway, undergraduate or postgraduate study. 
1.3 Applicants must hold an offer for a full-time undergraduate or postgraduate taught 
degree programme delivered at Aston University for the defined intake. 
1.4 Applicants must meet all academic and non- academic conditions stated in their 
offer letter. 
1.5 Applicants must be self-funded. Students whose tuition fees are wholly or partially 
funded by a sponsor are not eligible. 
1.6 The Global Partnership Scholarship is a competitive, application- based 
scholarship. Meeting the eligibility criteria and submitting a scholarship application 
does not create an entitlement to a scholarship. 
1.7 By submitting a scholarship application, applicants confirm their understanding of: 
• the competitive nature of the award; 
• the conditional assessment process; 
• the allocation-based structure; and 
• the finality of scholarship decisions. 
6 
GLOBAL ARTICULATION AND PROGRESSION SCHOLARSHIP 
2026/27 Academic Year – September 2026 Intake 
1.8 In order for the scholarship to be applied, applicants must: 
• Submit a completed scholarship application by the published deadline; 
• Pay the required programme deposit by the deadline stated in their offer 
letter; and 
• Successfully enrol by the latest enrolment date for the relevant intake. 
1.9 The award of a scholarship does not amend, vary or supersede the terms of the 
applicant’s Offer of Admission or Student Contract. 
2. Programme Exclusions 
The following programmes are not eligible: 
• BSc Nursing Studies (Adult Nursing or Mental Health) 
• MBChB Medicine 
• MOptom Optometry 
• BSc Healthcare Science (Audiology) 
• PGDip / MSc OSPAP 
• MPH 
• MSc Physician Associate Practice 
• All MRes programmes 
• All PhD programmes 
• All MBA programmes 
3. Scholarship Structure 
3.1 The Scholarship has a value of £5,000. 
3.2 The Scholarship is awarded as a tuition fee discount applied to the gross published 
international tuition fee applicable for the academic year of enrolment. 
3.3 The Scholarship applies to the first year of study only and does not create 
entitlement to continuation funding. 
3.4 The Scholarship will not reduce or replace the Programme Deposit. 
3.5 The Scholarship has no cash value and cannot be exchanged, transferred or offset 
against accommodation, living costs, immigration costs, repeat study, additional 
modules, placement years or study abroad years. 
4. Scholarship Availability, Assessment and Allocation 
4.1 The Global Partnership Scholarship is limited in number. The University sets a 
capped allocation for each defined intake. 
4.2 The University is under no obligation to award a minimum number of scholarships 
in any intake. 
7 
GLOBAL ARTICULATION AND PROGRESSION SCHOLARSHIP 
2026/27 Academic Year – September 2026 Intake 
4.3 The Scholarship is a competitive, application- based award. Submission of an 
application does not guarantee the award of a scholarship. 
4.4 Scholarship applications will only be subject to competitive assessment where the 
number of eligible scholarship applications exceeds the available scholarship 
allocation. 
4.5 Where the number of eligible applications does not exceed the available 
scholarship allocation, all eligible applicants will be awarded the Scholarship, subject 
to meeting eligibility, deposit payment and enrolment requirements. 
4.6 Where the number of eligible applications exceeds the available scholarship 
allocation, applications will be assessed competitively, based solely on the applicant’s 
response to the assessed scholarship question contained within the application form. 
4.7 In oversubscription scenarios, applications will be evaluated using a consistent 
internal scoring rubric, applying agreed internal weightings, and reviewed through 
Aston University’s internal scholarship panel and decision-making processes. 
4.8 The assessment process follows this sequence: 
• Eligibility verification; 
• Allocation comparison; 
• Competitive scoring (if triggered); 
• Ranking and panel confirmation. 
4.9 The University is not required to disclose individual scores, ranking positions, 
scoring thresholds, internal weightings, assessor comments, panel discussions or 
deliberative materials. 
4.10 The University reserves the right not to award all available scholarships. 
4.11 Where a selected applicant fails to meet deposit or enrolment requirements by 
the stated deadline, the University reserves the right to reallocate the scholarship to 
the next highest ranked eligible applicant. 
4.12 All applicants within the same defined intake cohort are assessed under the same 
eligibility and allocation framework. No individual negotiation of scholarship value is 
permitted. 
5. Application Integrity, Verification and AI Use 
5.1 Applicants are responsible for ensuring that all information submitted is accurate, 
complete and truthful. 
5.2 The University reserves the right to verify any information provided in a scholarship 
application. 
5.3 Applications must represent the applicant’s own original work. 
8 
GLOBAL ARTICULATION AND PROGRESSION SCHOLARSHIP 
2026/27 Academic Year – September 2026 Intake 
5.4 The use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools to support drafting, language refinement 
or idea development is permitted. However: 
• The content must reflect the applicant’s own experiences, perspectives and 
intent; 
• Applicants remain fully responsible for the accuracy and authenticity of their 
submission; 
• Fabricated, misleading or materially inaccurate information is prohibited. 
5.5 The University reserves the right to withdraw a scholarship where an application 
contains materially misleading, plagiarised, fabricated or misrepresented content, 
whether generated independently or with the assistance of AI tools. 
5.6 The University may request clarification or supporting evidence where concerns 
arise regarding authenticity or accuracy. 
6. Awarding, Confirmation and Activation 
6.1 Where selected, the Scholarship may be referenced within offer communications. 
Inclusion does not constitute application of the award to the tuition fee account and 
does not create unconditional entitlement. 
6.2 Payment of the Programme Deposit in full by the stated deadline is the formal 
trigger for scholarship confirmation. 
6.3 The Scholarship will not be applied to the student record unless and until the 
deposit has been received in full. 
6.4 The Scholarship becomes active only upon successful Enrolment. 
6.5 Where a student withdraws prior to enrolment, fails immigration compliance checks 
or does not complete enrolment, the Scholarship will lapse automatically. 
6.6 Where a Scholarship has been applied in error, including administrative or system 
error, Aston University reserves the right to amend or withdraw the award. Application 
in error does not create entitlement. 
6.7 The University reserves the right to audit eligibility, assessment records, fee status 
and funding status at any stage. 
7. Combination and Exclusivity 
7.1 A student may normally hold only one Aston University scholarship per programme 
of study. 
7.2 The Scholarship cannot be combined with any other Aston University scholarship, 
bursary, tuition fee discount or partnership award unless expressly confirmed in 
writing. 
9 
GLOBAL ARTICULATION AND PROGRESSION SCHOLARSHIP 
2026/27 Academic Year – September 2026 Intake 
7.3 Where a student is eligible for more than one award, the award of the highest value 
will normally apply. 
7.4 Where tuition fees become wholly or partially sponsored at any stage prior to or 
during enrolment, the Scholarship will normally be withdrawn. 
8. Receiving and Retaining the Scholarship 
8.1 The Scholarship will be applied only after deposit payment and successful 
Enrolment. 
8.2 Students must remain fully enrolled and in attendance. 
8.3 Students must comply with University regulations and UK immigration 
requirements. 
8.4 If fee status changes from Overseas to Home at any stage prior to or during 
enrolment, the Scholarship will be withdrawn. 
8.5 Where a student withdraws part-way through an academic year, tuition fee liability 
will be recalculated in accordance with the University’s Tuition Fees Charging Policy. 
8.6 Students repeating modules are not eligible in respect of repeated study. 
8.7 Where a student suspends studies, eligibility will be reassessed in line with 
University policy. 
9. Appeals and Final Decision 
9.1 Scholarship decisions are made by a University panel operating in accordance 
with internal procedures. The panel’s decision is final. 
9.2 Appeals may only be made on the grounds of procedural error, defined strictly as 
a demonstrable failure by the University to follow the published Terms and Conditions 
or stated assessment process. 
9.3 Appeals will not be considered based on: 
• academic judgement or comparative merit; 
• the content, quality or score of an application response; 
• disagreement with the outcome of the assessment; 
• the exercise of panel discretion; 
• the availability, allocation or exhaustion of scholarship places; 
• comparisons with other applicants or awards made. 
9.4 The University is not required to disclose individual scores, ranking positions, 
scoring thresholds, assessor comments, internal weightings or panel deliberations in 
response to an appeal. 
10 
GLOBAL ARTICULATION AND PROGRESSION SCHOLARSHIP 
2026/27 Academic Year – September 2026 Intake 
9.5 Where no procedural error is identified, the original decision will stand and will not 
be reconsidered. 
9.6 The University will not enter into further correspondence once the appeals process 
has concluded. 
10. Interpretation, Precedence and Governing Law 
10.1 In the event of any inconsistency between these Terms and Conditions and any 
other University publication, webpage, correspondence or third-party communication, 
these Terms and Conditions shall take precedence. 
10.2 Applicants should rely only on these published Terms and Conditions. No informal 
communication, marketing material, webinar statement, agent representation or 
partner institution communication shall be binding unless confirmed in writing by Aston 
University. 
10.3 Any discretion exercised by the University does not create precedent or 
entitlement for other applicants or future intakes. 
10.4 These Terms and Conditions are governed by and construed in accordance with 
the laws of England and Wales. 
Terms & Conditions validity 
2026/27 Academic Year (September 2026 intake only) 
Further Information and Enquiries 
All enquiries relating to the Global Articulation and Progression Scholarship must be 
directed to:  
Aston University’s International Office 
Email: international@aston.ac.uk  
END

SIR ADRIAN CADBURY CHANCELLOR'S SCHOLARSHIP › 01 / 10
Purpose and scope
These Terms and Conditions set out the eligibility criteria, application process, assessment
framework, award conditions, and appeals process for the Sir Adrian Cadbury Chancellor’s
Scholarship for international students commencing study at Aston University in the January
2027, April 2027, or September 2027 intake.
The scholarship honours the legacy of Sir Adrian Cadbury and supports students who
demonstrate integrity, social responsibility, and a commitment to making a positive impact
through their academic and professional ambitions.
The Sir Adrian Cadbury Chancellor’s Scholarship is a competitive, application-based award.
Meeting the eligibility criteria and submitting an application does not create any expectation,
entitlement, or presumption that a scholarship will be awarded.
Website content is provided for guidance only. In the event of any discrepancy between
website content and these Terms and Conditions, these Terms and Conditions shall
take precedence.
These Terms and Conditions are correct at the time of publication and may be amended
where necessary.
1 SCHOLARSHIP VALUE › › ›
1.1  The Sir Adrian Cadbury Chancellor’s Scholarship provides a £10,000 tuition fee reduction.
1.2  The scholarship is applied as a tuition fee waiver only and has no cash value.
1.3  The award cannot be used for deposits, accommodation, maintenance, or any other costs.
SIR ADRIAN CADBURY CHANCELLOR'S SCHOLARSHIP › 02 / 10
2 ELIGIBLE PROGRAMMES › › ›
2.1  The scholarship is available to applicants holding an offer for an eligible full-time
undergraduate or postgraduate taught programme delivered on campus at Aston University,
commencing in the January 2027, April 2027, or September 2027 intake, unless explicitly
excluded below.
2.2  The following postgraduate programmes are excluded from eligibility:
All MRes programmes SEPTEMBER ONLY
All MBA programmes ALL INTAKES
All PhD and research programmes ALL INTAKES
Overseas Pharmacists Assessment Programme (OSPAP) PgDip SEPTEMBER ONLY
MSc Physician Associate Practice SEPTEMBER ONLY
MPH Public Health SEPTEMBER ONLY
2.3  The following undergraduate programmes are excluded from eligibility:
BSc Nursing Studies (Adult Nursing) SEPTEMBER ONLY
BSc Nursing Studies (Mental Health) SEPTEMBER ONLY
MBChB Medicine SEPTEMBER ONLY
MOptom Optometry SEPTEMBER ONLY
MPharm Pharmacy SEPTEMBER ONLY
BSc Healthcare Science (Audiology) SEPTEMBER ONLY
2.3a  The exclusions in clauses 2.2 and 2.3 apply to the January 2027, April 2027 and
September 2027 intakes alike. Each excluded programme is tagged to show the intakes in
which it is delivered: those marked September only are not offered in January or April, while
those marked All intakes remain excluded whenever they are delivered. PhD and research
programmes have variable start dates that do not align with taught intakes, and are excluded
throughout. The tags are provided for guidance only and do not extend or limit the exclusions
set out above. Where an excluded programme is subsequently made available in any 2027
intake, whether or not it is currently delivered in that intake, applicants for that programme will
remain ineligible for the Scholarship.
2.4  Aston University reserves the right to amend the list of eligible or excluded programmes
where required for regulatory, professional, or strategic reasons.
SIR ADRIAN CADBURY CHANCELLOR'S SCHOLARSHIP › 03 / 10
3 ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA › › ›
Applicants must meet all of the following criteria at the point of application:
3.1  Be classified as an international (overseas fee-paying) student for tuition fee purposes.
3.2  Hold an offer for an eligible programme at Aston University for January 2027, April 2027, or
September 2027 entry.
3.3  Meet all academic, English language, and non-academic conditions stated in their offer
letter by the required deadlines.
3.4  Be self-funded. Applicants whose tuition fees are fully or partially funded by an external
sponsor are not eligible.
3.5  Successfully submit a completed scholarship application using the official personal
application link issued by Aston University.
3.6  Eligibility is assessed based on the applicant’s programme, funding status, and fee
classification as recorded at the scholarship application deadline. Subsequent changes to
programme choice, funding arrangements, or fee status will not be applied retrospectively.
SIR ADRIAN CADBURY CHANCELLOR'S SCHOLARSHIP › 04 / 10
4 APPLICATION PROCESS AND DEADLINES › › ›
4.1  The Sir Adrian Cadbury Chancellor’s Scholarship is a competitive, application-based award.
4.2  Eligible applicants will be issued a personal scholarship application link to the email
address recorded on their Aston University applicant record after receiving an offer to study.
4.3  It is the applicant’s responsibility to:
ensure their contact details are accurate;
check junk or spam folders; and
access and submit the application using the issued link.
Failure to receive or access the application link does not constitute grounds for appeal unless a
system error is formally confirmed by Aston University.
4.4  Applications submitted via any other route will not be considered.
4.5  Applicants must submit:
a completed application form; and
a written statement of approximately 500 words outlining how they intend to make a
positive impact and use their degree to support communities.
Statements of 550 words or more, or of 450 words or fewer, will be excluded
from assessment.
SIR ADRIAN CADBURY CHANCELLOR'S SCHOLARSHIP › 05 / 10
4 APPLICATION PROCESS AND DEADLINES · CONTINUED › › ›
4.6  An application is deemed submitted only once an automated submission confirmation has
been issued. Incomplete, draft, or unconfirmed applications will not be assessed.
4.7  Application deadlines, decision timelines, and application windows will be published on
Aston University’s website: aston.ac.uk/international/scholarships.
4.8  It is the applicant’s responsibility to consult the published webpage and ensure submission
by the stated deadline. The University is not responsible for missed deadlines resulting from
failure to consult published information.
4.9  Where the number of eligible applications exceeds the number of available awards,
scholarships will be allocated following a competitive assessment process. The University is
not required to award a scholarship to all eligible applicants.
SIR ADRIAN CADBURY CHANCELLOR'S SCHOLARSHIP › 06 / 10
5 AWARD BASIS, EXCLUSIVITY, AND SUPERSESSION › › ›
5.1  Due to the high value of the award, the Sir Adrian Cadbury Chancellor’s Scholarship
cannot be held in conjunction with any other internally or externally managed scholarship,
bursary, fee discount, or tuition fee award, unless explicitly confirmed otherwise in writing by
Aston University.
5.2  Where an applicant is eligible for, or has been offered, more than one scholarship or tuition
fee discount, only one award may be held per programme of study.
The single award of the highest monetary value will normally apply, as determined by
Aston University.
Where the Sir Adrian Cadbury Chancellor’s Scholarship represents the highest value award, it
will supersede all other scholarships or fee discounts.
The University’s determination of the applicable award is final.
5.3  Applicants progressing from foundation providers, pre-masters providers, or via formal
progression or articulation agreements remain eligible to be considered, subject to meeting all
other eligibility requirements.
5.4  Where a progression-, pathway-, or partner-specific scholarship or tuition fee discount
exists, the award of the Sir Adrian Cadbury Chancellor’s Scholarship, if greater in value, will
override and replace any such alternative award if the applicant is successful.
SIR ADRIAN CADBURY CHANCELLOR'S SCHOLARSHIP › 07 / 10
6 RECEIVING AND RETAINING THE SCHOLARSHIP › › ›
6.1  The scholarship will be applied to the student’s tuition fee account only after:
the required programme deposit has been paid;
the appropriate SITS scholarship code has been applied to the student record; and
the student has successfully enrolled within the required enrolment period.
Where applicable, the scholarship is also conditional upon the student having received a
Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) and holding a valid Student visa.
6.2  Unless otherwise stated, the scholarship applies to tuition fees only and to the approved
academic year of entry. No cash alternative is available.
6.3  Students must remain fully enrolled and in attendance, as defined by Aston University, in
order to retain the scholarship.
6.4  Students who withdraw part-way through an academic year will no longer be eligible for the
scholarship. Any tuition fee reduction already applied may be withdrawn, and the student will be
liable for the full tuition fee for that academic year.
6.5  Students repeating modules, whether with or without attendance, are not eligible to receive
the scholarship in respect of the repeated study.
6.6  Where a student suspends their studies and takes a Leave of Absence:
if the Leave of Absence covers a complete academic year, no tuition fee is charged and no
scholarship is payable;
if taken part-way through an academic year, scholarship eligibility will be assessed in line
with Aston University’s Tuition Fees Charging Policy and may be adjusted on a pro-rata
basis.
6.7  Where sector-wide UKVI processing delays or external visa issues materially affect
enrolment, Aston University may, at its sole discretion, review eligibility on a case-by-case
basis. Such review does not guarantee continuation of the scholarship and does not establish
a precedent.
SIR ADRIAN CADBURY CHANCELLOR'S SCHOLARSHIP › 08 / 10
7 APPEALS AND FINAL DECISION › › ›
7.1  Scholarship decisions are made by a University selection panel operating in accordance
with internal procedures. No member of staff outside the designated process has authority to
vary or overturn a decision.
7.2  Appeals may be made only on the grounds of procedural error, defined as a demonstrable
failure by Aston University to follow the published application or assessment process, which
must be clearly evidenced and materially relevant to the outcome.
7.3  Appeals will not be considered on the grounds of:
academic judgement or comparative merit;
the content, quality, or score of an application;
disagreement with the outcome of the assessment;
the exercise of panel discretion;
the availability, allocation, or exhaustion of scholarship awards; or
comparisons with other applicants or awards made.
7.4  The University does not provide individual feedback on unsuccessful applications
and is not required to disclose scores, rankings, thresholds, assessor comments, or
panel deliberations.
7.5  Appeals must be submitted in writing within fourteen (14) calendar days of the tuition fee
invoice being raised on the applicant’s student record. The invoice date is used solely to
calculate the appeal submission window and does not constitute confirmation of scholarship
eligibility or award.
7.6  Where no procedural error is identified, the original decision will stand and will not be
reconsidered. Failure to submit an appeal within the stated timeframe will be taken as
acceptance of the original decision.
7.7  Once the appeals process has concluded, the University will not enter into
further correspondence.

Purpose and scope
These Terms and Conditions set out the eligibility criteria, application process, assessment
framework, award conditions, and appeals process for the Sir Adrian Cadbury Chancellor’s
Scholarship for international students commencing study at Aston University in the January
2027, April 2027, or September 2027 intake.
The scholarship honours the legacy of Sir Adrian Cadbury and supports students who
demonstrate integrity, social responsibility, and a commitment to making a positive impact
through their academic and professional ambitions.
The Sir Adrian Cadbury Chancellor’s Scholarship is a competitive, application-based award.
Meeting the eligibility criteria and submitting an application does not create any expectation,
entitlement, or presumption that a scholarship will be awarded.
Website content is provided for guidance only. In the event of any discrepancy between
website content and these Terms and Conditions, these Terms and Conditions shall
take precedence.
These Terms and Conditions are correct at the time of publication and may be amended
where necessary.
1 SCHOLARSHIP VALUE › › ›
1.1  The Sir Adrian Cadbury Chancellor’s Scholarship provides a £10,000 tuition fee reduction.
1.2  The scholarship is applied as a tuition fee waiver only and has no cash value.
1.3  The award cannot be used for deposits, accommodation, maintenance, or any other costs.
SIR ADRIAN CADBURY CHANCELLOR'S SCHOLARSHIP › 02 / 10
2 ELIGIBLE PROGRAMMES › › ›
2.1  The scholarship is available to applicants holding an offer for an eligible full-time
undergraduate or postgraduate taught programme delivered on campus at Aston University,
commencing in the January 2027, April 2027, or September 2027 intake, unless explicitly
excluded below.
2.2  The following postgraduate programmes are excluded from eligibility:
All MRes programmes SEPTEMBER ONLY
All MBA programmes ALL INTAKES
All PhD and research programmes ALL INTAKES
Overseas Pharmacists Assessment Programme (OSPAP) PgDip SEPTEMBER ONLY
MSc Physician Associate Practice SEPTEMBER ONLY
MPH Public Health SEPTEMBER ONLY
2.3  The following undergraduate programmes are excluded from eligibility:
BSc Nursing Studies (Adult Nursing) SEPTEMBER ONLY
BSc Nursing Studies (Mental Health) SEPTEMBER ONLY
MBChB Medicine SEPTEMBER ONLY
MOptom Optometry SEPTEMBER ONLY
MPharm Pharmacy SEPTEMBER ONLY
BSc Healthcare Science (Audiology) SEPTEMBER ONLY
2.3a  The exclusions in clauses 2.2 and 2.3 apply to the January 2027, April 2027 and
September 2027 intakes alike. Each excluded programme is tagged to show the intakes in
which it is delivered: those marked September only are not offered in January or April, while
those marked All intakes remain excluded whenever they are delivered. PhD and research
programmes have variable start dates that do not align with taught intakes, and are excluded
throughout. The tags are provided for guidance only and do not extend or limit the exclusions
set out above. Where an excluded programme is subsequently made available in any 2027
intake, whether or not it is currently delivered in that intake, applicants for that programme will
remain ineligible for the Scholarship.
2.4  Aston University reserves the right to amend the list of eligible or excluded programmes
where required for regulatory, professional, or strategic reasons.
SIR ADRIAN CADBURY CHANCELLOR'S SCHOLARSHIP › 03 / 10
3 ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA › › ›
Applicants must meet all of the following criteria at the point of application:
3.1  Be classified as an international (overseas fee-paying) student for tuition fee purposes.
3.2  Hold an offer for an eligible programme at Aston University for January 2027, April 2027, or
September 2027 entry.
3.3  Meet all academic, English language, and non-academic conditions stated in their offer
letter by the required deadlines.
3.4  Be self-funded. Applicants whose tuition fees are fully or partially funded by an external
sponsor are not eligible.
3.5  Successfully submit a completed scholarship application using the official personal
application link issued by Aston University.
3.6  Eligibility is assessed based on the applicant’s programme, funding status, and fee
classification as recorded at the scholarship application deadline. Subsequent changes to
programme choice, funding arrangements, or fee status will not be applied retrospectively.
SIR ADRIAN CADBURY CHANCELLOR'S SCHOLARSHIP › 04 / 10
4 APPLICATION PROCESS AND DEADLINES › › ›
4.1  The Sir Adrian Cadbury Chancellor’s Scholarship is a competitive, application-based award.
4.2  Eligible applicants will be issued a personal scholarship application link to the email
address recorded on their Aston University applicant record after receiving an offer to study.
4.3  It is the applicant’s responsibility to:
ensure their contact details are accurate;
check junk or spam folders; and
access and submit the application using the issued link.
Failure to receive or access the application link does not constitute grounds for appeal unless a
system error is formally confirmed by Aston University.
4.4  Applications submitted via any other route will not be considered.
4.5  Applicants must submit:
a completed application form; and
a written statement of approximately 500 words outlining how they intend to make a
positive impact and use their degree to support communities.
Statements of 550 words or more, or of 450 words or fewer, will be excluded
from assessment.
SIR ADRIAN CADBURY CHANCELLOR'S SCHOLARSHIP › 05 / 10
4 APPLICATION PROCESS AND DEADLINES · CONTINUED › › ›
4.6  An application is deemed submitted only once an automated submission confirmation has
been issued. Incomplete, draft, or unconfirmed applications will not be assessed.
4.7  Application deadlines, decision timelines, and application windows will be published on
Aston University’s website: aston.ac.uk/international/scholarships.
4.8  It is the applicant’s responsibility to consult the published webpage and ensure submission
by the stated deadline. The University is not responsible for missed deadlines resulting from
failure to consult published information.
4.9  Where the number of eligible applications exceeds the number of available awards,
scholarships will be allocated following a competitive assessment process. The University is
not required to award a scholarship to all eligible applicants.
SIR ADRIAN CADBURY CHANCELLOR'S SCHOLARSHIP › 06 / 10
5 AWARD BASIS, EXCLUSIVITY, AND SUPERSESSION › › ›
5.1  Due to the high value of the award, the Sir Adrian Cadbury Chancellor’s Scholarship
cannot be held in conjunction with any other internally or externally managed scholarship,
bursary, fee discount, or tuition fee award, unless explicitly confirmed otherwise in writing by
Aston University.
5.2  Where an applicant is eligible for, or has been offered, more than one scholarship or tuition
fee discount, only one award may be held per programme of study.
The single award of the highest monetary value will normally apply, as determined by
Aston University.
Where the Sir Adrian Cadbury Chancellor’s Scholarship represents the highest value award, it
will supersede all other scholarships or fee discounts.
The University’s determination of the applicable award is final.
5.3  Applicants progressing from foundation providers, pre-masters providers, or via formal
progression or articulation agreements remain eligible to be considered, subject to meeting all
other eligibility requirements.
5.4  Where a progression-, pathway-, or partner-specific scholarship or tuition fee discount
exists, the award of the Sir Adrian Cadbury Chancellor’s Scholarship, if greater in value, will
override and replace any such alternative award if the applicant is successful.
SIR ADRIAN CADBURY CHANCELLOR'S SCHOLARSHIP › 07 / 10
6 RECEIVING AND RETAINING THE SCHOLARSHIP › › ›
6.1  The scholarship will be applied to the student’s tuition fee account only after:
the required programme deposit has been paid;
the appropriate SITS scholarship code has been applied to the student record; and
the student has successfully enrolled within the required enrolment period.
Where applicable, the scholarship is also conditional upon the student having received a
Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) and holding a valid Student visa.
6.2  Unless otherwise stated, the scholarship applies to tuition fees only and to the approved
academic year of entry. No cash alternative is available.
6.3  Students must remain fully enrolled and in attendance, as defined by Aston University, in
order to retain the scholarship.
6.4  Students who withdraw part-way through an academic year will no longer be eligible for the
scholarship. Any tuition fee reduction already applied may be withdrawn, and the student will be
liable for the full tuition fee for that academic year.
6.5  Students repeating modules, whether with or without attendance, are not eligible to receive
the scholarship in respect of the repeated study.
6.6  Where a student suspends their studies and takes a Leave of Absence:
if the Leave of Absence covers a complete academic year, no tuition fee is charged and no
scholarship is payable;
if taken part-way through an academic year, scholarship eligibility will be assessed in line
with Aston University’s Tuition Fees Charging Policy and may be adjusted on a pro-rata
basis.
6.7  Where sector-wide UKVI processing delays or external visa issues materially affect
enrolment, Aston University may, at its sole discretion, review eligibility on a case-by-case
basis. Such review does not guarantee continuation of the scholarship and does not establish
a precedent.
SIR ADRIAN CADBURY CHANCELLOR'S SCHOLARSHIP › 08 / 10
7 APPEALS AND FINAL DECISION › › ›
7.1  Scholarship decisions are made by a University selection panel operating in accordance
with internal procedures. No member of staff outside the designated process has authority to
vary or overturn a decision.
7.2  Appeals may be made only on the grounds of procedural error, defined as a demonstrable
failure by Aston University to follow the published application or assessment process, which
must be clearly evidenced and materially relevant to the outcome.
7.3  Appeals will not be considered on the grounds of:
academic judgement or comparative merit;
the content, quality, or score of an application;
disagreement with the outcome of the assessment;
the exercise of panel discretion;
the availability, allocation, or exhaustion of scholarship awards; or
comparisons with other applicants or awards made.
7.4  The University does not provide individual feedback on unsuccessful applications
and is not required to disclose scores, rankings, thresholds, assessor comments, or
panel deliberations.
7.5  Appeals must be submitted in writing within fourteen (14) calendar days of the tuition fee
invoice being raised on the applicant’s student record. The invoice date is used solely to
calculate the appeal submission window and does not constitute confirmation of scholarship
eligibility or award.
7.6  Where no procedural error is identified, the original decision will stand and will not be
reconsidered. Failure to submit an appeal within the stated timeframe will be taken as
acceptance of the original decision.
7.7  Once the appeals process has concluded, the University will not enter into
further correspondence.
SIR ADRIAN CADBURY CHANCELLOR'S SCHOLARSHIP › 09 / 10
8 WITHDRAWAL, AMENDMENTS, AND LIABILITY › › ›
8.1  Aston University reserves the right to withdraw the scholarship if information provided
by the applicant is found to be false or misleading, or if the student no longer meets the
eligibility criteria.
8.2  The University accepts no liability for costs incurred by applicants in connection with the
scholarship application process.
8.3  Aston University reserves the right to amend or withdraw the scholarship where required
for regulatory, operational, or strategic reasons.
› › ›

and September 2027 intakes.
1 0  ·  F U R T H E R  I N F O R M A T I O N  A N D  E N Q U I R I E S
All enquiries relating to the Sir Adrian Cadbury Chancellor’s Scholarship should be
directed to Aston University’s International Office.

BSc Nursing Studies (Adult Nursing) SEPTEMBER ONLY
BSc Nursing Studies (Mental Health) SEPTEMBER ONLY
MBChB Medicine SEPTEMBER ONLY
MOptom Optometry SEPTEMBER ONLY
MPharm Pharmacy SEPTEMBER ONLY
BSc Healthcare Science (Audiology) SEPTEMBER ONLY
2.3a  The exclusions in clauses 2.2 and 2.3 apply to the January 2027, April 2027 and
September 2027 intakes alike. Each excluded programme is tagged to show the intakes in
which it is delivered: those marked September only are not offered in January or April, while
those marked All intakes remain excluded whenever they are delivered. PhD and research
programmes have variable start dates that do not align with taught intakes, and are excluded
throughout. The tags are provided for guidance only and do not extend or limit the exclusions
set out above. Where an excluded programme is subsequently made available in any 2027
intake, whether or not it is currently delivered in that intake, applicants for that programme will
remain ineligible for the Scholarship.
2.4  Aston University reserves the right to amend the list of eligible or excluded programmes
where required for regulatory, professional, or strategic reasons.
SIR ADRIAN CADBURY CHANCELLOR'S SCHOLARSHIP › 03 / 10
3 ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA › › ›
Applicants must meet all of the following criteria at the point of application:
3.1  Be classified as an international (overseas fee-paying) student for tuition fee purposes.
3.2  Hold an offer for an eligible programme at Aston University for January 2027, April 2027, or
September 2027 entry.
3.3  Meet all academic, English language, and non-academic conditions stated in their offer
letter by the required deadlines.
3.4  Be self-funded. Applicants whose tuition fees are fully or partially funded by an external
sponsor are not eligible.
3.5  Successfully submit a completed scholarship application using the official personal
application link issued by Aston University.
3.6  Eligibility is assessed based on the applicant’s programme, funding status, and fee
classification as recorded at the scholarship application deadline. Subsequent changes to
programme choice, funding arrangements, or fee status will not be applied retrospectively.
SIR ADRIAN CADBURY CHANCELLOR'S SCHOLARSHIP › 04 / 10
4 APPLICATION PROCESS AND DEADLINES › › ›
4.1  The Sir Adrian Cadbury Chancellor’s Scholarship is a competitive, application-based award.
4.2  Eligible applicants will be issued a personal scholarship application link to the email
address recorded on their Aston University applicant record after receiving an offer to study.
4.3  It is the applicant’s responsibility to:
ensure their contact details are accurate;
check junk or spam folders; and
access and submit the application using the issued link.
Failure to receive or access the application link does not constitute grounds for appeal unless a
system error is formally confirmed by Aston University.
4.4  Applications submitted via any other route will not be considered.
4.5  Applicants must submit:
a completed application form; and
a written statement of approximately 500 words outlining how they intend to make a
positive impact and use their degree to support communities.
Statements of 550 words or more, or of 450 words or fewer, will be excluded
from assessment.
SIR ADRIAN CADBURY CHANCELLOR'S SCHOLARSHIP › 05 / 10
4 APPLICATION PROCESS AND DEADLINES · CONTINUED › › ›
4.6  An application is deemed submitted only once an automated submission confirmation has
been issued. Incomplete, draft, or unconfirmed applications will not be assessed.
4.7  Application deadlines, decision timelines, and application windows will be published on
Aston University’s website: aston.ac.uk/international/scholarships.
4.8  It is the applicant’s responsibility to consult the published webpage and ensure submission
by the stated deadline. The University is not responsible for missed deadlines resulting from
failure to consult published information.
4.9  Where the number of eligible applications exceeds the number of available awards,
scholarships will be allocated following a competitive assessment process. The University is
not required to award a scholarship to all eligible applicants.
SIR ADRIAN CADBURY CHANCELLOR'S SCHOLARSHIP › 06 / 10
5 AWARD BASIS, EXCLUSIVITY, AND SUPERSESSION › › ›
5.1  Due to the high value of the award, the Sir Adrian Cadbury Chancellor’s Scholarship
cannot be held in conjunction with any other internally or externally managed scholarship,
bursary, fee discount, or tuition fee award, unless explicitly confirmed otherwise in writing by
Aston University.
5.2  Where an applicant is eligible for, or has been offered, more than one scholarship or tuition
fee discount, only one award may be held per programme of study.
The single award of the highest monetary value will normally apply, as determined by
Aston University.
Where the Sir Adrian Cadbury Chancellor’s Scholarship represents the highest value award, it
will supersede all other scholarships or fee discounts.
The University’s determination of the applicable award is final.
5.3  Applicants progressing from foundation providers, pre-masters providers, or via formal
progression or articulation agreements remain eligible to be considered, subject to meeting all
other eligibility requirements.
5.4  Where a progression-, pathway-, or partner-specific scholarship or tuition fee discount
exists, the award of the Sir Adrian Cadbury Chancellor’s Scholarship, if greater in value, will
override and replace any such alternative award if the applicant is successful.
SIR ADRIAN CADBURY CHANCELLOR'S SCHOLARSHIP › 07 / 10
6 RECEIVING AND RETAINING THE SCHOLARSHIP › › ›
6.1  The scholarship will be applied to the student’s tuition fee account only after:
the required programme deposit has been paid;
the appropriate SITS scholarship code has been applied to the student record; and
the student has successfully enrolled within the required enrolment period.
Where applicable, the scholarship is also conditional upon the student having received a
Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) and holding a valid Student visa.
6.2  Unless otherwise stated, the scholarship applies to tuition fees only and to the approved
academic year of entry. No cash alternative is available.
6.3  Students must remain fully enrolled and in attendance, as defined by Aston University, in
order to retain the scholarship.
6.4  Students who withdraw part-way through an academic year will no longer be eligible for the
scholarship. Any tuition fee reduction already applied may be withdrawn, and the student will be
liable for the full tuition fee for that academic year.
6.5  Students repeating modules, whether with or without attendance, are not eligible to receive
the scholarship in respect of the repeated study.
6.6  Where a student suspends their studies and takes a Leave of Absence:
if the Leave of Absence covers a complete academic year, no tuition fee is charged and no
scholarship is payable;
if taken part-way through an academic year, scholarship eligibility will be assessed in line
with Aston University’s Tuition Fees Charging Policy and may be adjusted on a pro-rata
basis.
6.7  Where sector-wide UKVI processing delays or external visa issues materially affect
enrolment, Aston University may, at its sole discretion, review eligibility on a case-by-case
basis. Such review does not guarantee continuation of the scholarship and does not establish
a precedent.
SIR ADRIAN CADBURY CHANCELLOR'S SCHOLARSHIP › 08 / 10
7 APPEALS AND FINAL DECISION › › ›
7.1  Scholarship decisions are made by a University selection panel operating in accordance
with internal procedures. No member of staff outside the designated process has authority to
vary or overturn a decision.
7.2  Appeals may be made only on the grounds of procedural error, defined as a demonstrable
failure by Aston University to follow the published application or assessment process, which
must be clearly evidenced and materially relevant to the outcome.
7.3  Appeals will not be considered on the grounds of:
academic judgement or comparative merit;
the content, quality, or score of an application;
disagreement with the outcome of the assessment;
the exercise of panel discretion;
the availability, allocation, or exhaustion of scholarship awards; or
comparisons with other applicants or awards made.
7.4  The University does not provide individual feedback on unsuccessful applications
and is not required to disclose scores, rankings, thresholds, assessor comments, or
panel deliberations.
7.5  Appeals must be submitted in writing within fourteen (14) calendar days of the tuition fee
invoice being raised on the applicant’s student record. The invoice date is used solely to
calculate the appeal submission window and does not constitute confirmation of scholarship
eligibility or award.
7.6  Where no procedural error is identified, the original decision will stand and will not be
reconsidered. Failure to submit an appeal within the stated timeframe will be taken as
acceptance of the original decision.
7.7  Once the appeals process has concluded, the University will not enter into
further correspondence.
SIR ADRIAN CADBURY CHANCELLOR'S SCHOLARSHIP › 09 / 10
8 WITHDRAWAL, AMENDMENTS, AND LIABILITY › › ›
8.1  Aston University reserves the right to withdraw the scholarship if information provided
by the applicant is found to be false or misleading, or if the student no longer meets the
eligibility criteria.
8.2  The University accepts no liability for costs incurred by applicants in connection with the
scholarship application process.
8.3  Aston University reserves the right to amend or withdraw the scholarship where required
for regulatory, operational, or strategic reasons.
› › ›
9  ·  T E R M S  A N D  C O N D I T I O N S  V A L I D I T Y
These Terms and Conditions apply to the January 2027, April 2027,
and September 2027 intakes.

All enquiries relating to the Sir Adrian Cadbury Chancellor’s Scholarship should be
directed to Aston University’s International Office.
