Appendix B Glossary  
 
These meanings apply only to Aston University Home and EU Scholarship Policy 2018/19 
and may not hold the same meanings or be interpreted in the same way in other documents.   
 
Academic Term 
The academic year is divided into three academic terms for undergraduate payment 
arrangements. 
 
Academic year  
This is the period over which Aston University teaches a programme.  For most 
undergraduate programmes, this normally begins at the start of October and ends in the 
middle of June.   Students should normally be in attendance during this period. 
 
Attendance  
For the purposes of Aston Scholarship approvals, a student is considered to be in 
attendance if Aston University’s student records systems show that they are a current 
student.   Attendance requirements to pass a degree programme may differ and should be 
clarified with the specific programme leader. 
 
Care Leaver 
For the purposes of this policy a care leaver has identified this at pre-enrolment and is 
defined as “If you were looked after for at least 13 weeks since the age of 14, and were in 
the care of the local authority and/or a health and social care trust on your 16th birthday”  
 
Deferred studies  
This is when exams and/or assessments are delayed until an agreed period of time has 
elapsed.   
 
Equivalent or Lower Qualification 
A student holds an Equivalent or Lower Qualification8 if they already hold an awarded 
qualification which is at the same level as or is higher than the programme they will be 
studying at Aston University. 
 
EU student  
This is a student who is an EU national (or the relevant family member of an EU national) 
and who qualifies to be considered for a tuition fee loan from the UK government.  These 
students cannot be charged more than £9,250 for their tuition fees.  The rules about who 
qualifies as an EU student depend on the immigration status of the student and their family 
members and where they have all been living.   
 
Home student  
This is a student who qualifies to be considered for a tuition fee loan and grants and loans 
for living costs from the UK government.  These students cannot be charged more than 
£9,250 for their tuition fees.  The rules about who qualifies as a home student depend on 
nationality, the immigration status of the student and their family members and where they 
all have been living.   
 
Household Income  
																																																													
8	As	defined	by	the	Higher	Education	Funding	Council	for	England	
15	
	
This is the household income as calculated by the relevant funding authority for a student’s 
application for student funding from the UK government.  It is not possible for Aston 
University to accept any alternative assessment method of a student’s household income.   
 
My Aston Portal (MAP)  
This is the Aston University online student portal through which students can view and 
update personal information and find information about their programme.  Students will be 
able to access information about the progress of Aston Scholarship assessments and 
approvals from their student homepage on MAP.   
 
Re-enrolment  
All students are expected to re-enrol each September, irrespective of their start date.  The 
purpose of re-enrolment is to confirm that the student accepts the University’s terms and 
conditions and the University’s Regulations for that specific academic year.  The re-
enrolment process is also used to update any changes to the student’s personal information.  
Re-enrolment is via MAP and the student will be emailed when the MAP task is available for 
the student to complete.  
 
Repeating studies as if for the first time  
This is when exams, assessments or modules are retaken but are treated as a first attempt 
and the mark the student receives is not limited to the pass mark, this is usually due to 
exceptional circumstances that are agreed on an individual case by case basis.   
 
Repeating studies with attendance  
This is when a student does not progress to the next level of study and has to retake exams 
and/or assessments in the following year and is required to attend all of the lectures, classes 
and tutorials for those modules.   
 
Repeating studies without attendance  
This is when a student does not progress to the next level of study and has to retake exams 
and/or assessments in the following year and is not required to attend any of the lectures, 
classes and tutorials for those modules.   
 
Repeating studies with partial attendance  
This is when a student has to retake exams, assessments and/or modules in the following 
year and is required to attend some of the lectures, classes and tutorials for those modules.   
 
Sandwich placement year  
This is a period of industrial, professional, linguistic or occupational training/work experience 
or study abroad which is approved by the University and forms part of the assessment for a 
sandwich degree or language degree at Aston University.  Sometimes a student is paid 
during their placement for the work they do by their placement employer which is called a 
paid placement.  In other cases, students do not receive any money from their placement 
employer for their work and this is called an unpaid placement.  If the placement takes place 
outside of the UK then it is considered to be a work or study placement overseas.   
 
Satisfactory academic performance  
For the purposes of Aston Scholarship approvals, a student is considered to have a 
satisfactory academic performance if they have been accepted to start the first year of their 
programme or they have been considered by an Examination Board to have passed and to 
be eligible to progress into the next stage of study.   
 
Special Support Grant  
16	
	
This is a grant for living costs from the UK Government which is for students who have an 
entitlement to receive Social Security Benefits (for example they have children or are 
disabled).  It is assessed and awarded by the relevant Student Finance body.   
 
Stage of study 
Stage 1 equates to the entry to year 1 of a degree programme or year 0 of the Integrated 
Foundation Year Programme, 
Stage 2 follows stage 1 after successful completion of that year of study, 
Stage P is the placement/sandwich year and often follows stage 2, 
Stage 3 follows stage 2 after successful completion of that year of study for those students 
whose programme of study is made up of four or more taught years of study e.g. MPharm, 
Stage F is the final year of study of a degree programme. 
 
Student Awards Agency for Scotland  
This is the organisation that assesses and awards student funding from the UK government 
to Home students who live in Scotland.  This organisation also assesses and awards student 
funding from the UK government to EU students who study in Scotland.   
 
Student Finance England  
This is the organisation that assesses and awards student funding from the UK government 
to Home students who live in England.   
 
Student Finance Northern Ireland  
This is the organisation that assesses and awards student funding from the UK government 
to Home students who live in Northern Ireland.   
 
Student Finance Services  
This is the organisation that assesses and awards student funding from the UK government 
to EU students in England, Wales and Northern Ireland.  It is also sometimes known as the 
EU Team or the European Services Team.   
 
Student Finance Wales  
This is the organisation that assesses and awards student funding from the UK government 
to Home students who live in Wales.   
 
Student Loans Company  
This is the organisation that manages the payment and repayment of loans and grants for 
student support funding.  This organisation is also responsible for collating information about 
household income and sharing this information with Universities for bursary and scholarship 
assessments.   
 
Suspending studies (Leave of Absence)  
This is when a student stops their studies for a period (normally longer than 60 days) for 
reasons such as illness.  This is also sometimes called a Leave of Absence.   
 
UCAS  
This stands for the University and Colleges Admission System.  It is the system students use 
to apply for undergraduate places at universities and colleges in the UK.

UNDERGRADUATE SCHOLARSHIPS 
 
Aston University reviews its portfolio of scholarships on an annual basis.  Scholarships 
offered for one entry cohort may not be offered for following cohorts.  The Terms and 
Conditions of specific scholarships may differ dependent on the year of first offering. 
 
1. Purpose and Scope  
 
1.1 This section of the document outlines the eligibility and assessment criteria for students 
to receive scholarships from Aston University as part of the Higher Education funding 
arrangements for students starting undergraduate degree programmes in 2017/18.  This 
policy is correct at the time of publication but may be subject to change. 
 
2. General Provisions  
 
2.1 A student qualifies to be considered for an Aston Scholarship if:  
 
(a) the student will start a new full time undergraduate degree programme at Aston 
University between 1st September 2017 and the 31st August 2018. 
 
(b) the student will be liable to pay tuition fees of £9,250 or £1,250 in the placement year or 
they are studying an Equivalent or Lower Qualification1 and  liable to pay tuition fees of 
£9,250 or £1,250 in the placement year. These fee amounts are subject to inflationary 
increases in line with government policy. 
 
(c) the student is not a resident of the Channel Islands or the Isle of Man (unless the student 
is entitled to benefit from European Community provisions relating to employment or 
establishment and is in receipt of UK student support funding as a home or EU student).

2.2 A student who is awarded a scholarship will be eligible to receive that scholarship in line 
with the conditions that applied in their original year of entry irrespective of subsequent 
transfers or suspension of studies. 
 
2.3 The household income thresholds used to assess eligibility for the award of a 
scholarship approved on household income will be reviewed once in the academic year 
where a student enters stage 1 of a programme of study. 
 
2.4 A student will not be entitled to receive a scholarship in any academic year for which 
they do not have to pay tuition fees.   
 
2.5 With the exception of a placement year, a student will only be eligible to be considered 
for an Aston Scholarship approved on household income for an academic year if they have 
made an application to be income assessed for the same year by Student Finance England, 
Student Finance Wales, Student Finance Northern Ireland, Student Awards Agency for 
Scotland or Student Finance Services.

2.7 A student will not be eligible to receive a scholarship in full or in part if they are, at the 
time when payment is due to be made to them, considered by the University to be in 
academic debt3.   For the purposes of this policy a student will be considered to be in 
academic debt to the University if they have received the third notice that a payment is 
overdue. 
 
3.  Approving and awarding  
 
3.1 Students will only be approved for Aston Scholarships once in an academic year.   
Scholarship entitlement will normally be determined by the 30th November 2017 using the 
information that is available to Aston University at that time.  Any scholarship assessments 
which cannot be considered at the end of November because the required information is not 
yet available will be reviewed on a monthly basis until all relevant information has been 
received and the student’s scholarship entitlement can be determined.  It is not normally 
possible to consider a student for an award of an Aston Scholarship after 30th May of the 
academic year in question.   
 
3.2 Students do not need to apply to be considered for a scholarship because Aston 
University will use UCAS data, household income information provided by the Student Loans 
Company and information held on University records for placement years, to determine 
awards.   
 
3.3 Students who are eligible for one or more of the Aston Scholarships will receive 
communications concerning their award/s through My Aston Portal (MAP).  
 
3.4 Students who are eligible for one or more of the Aston Scholarships or the Aston Aspire 
Scholarship Programme will be required to confirm the format they wish that scholarship to 
take, in line with the choices offered in the first term of each academic year.  This 
confirmation of choice will be final and will not be amended. 
 
3.5 The Student Loans Company charges interest on tuition fee loans at a daily rate from the 
date payments are made to universities.  Aston University cannot accept any responsibility 
for interest applied to tuition fee loans by the Student Loans Company.   
 
3.6 Eligibility for a scholarship approved on household income will be determined on the 
basis of information provided by the Student Loans Company once the student has been 
fully enrolled on the degree programme.  Aston University aims to consider scholarships 
based on household income within eight weeks of receiving household income information 
from the Student Loans Company.  Any student who is approved for an income-based 
scholarship will be notified via MAP.  The University will notify the Student Loans Company 
about fee discounts and changes in tuition fee liability.

information held on University records about previous scholarship approvals and placement

Any Aston Scholarship applied to the student for that academic year will be revoked and the

3.12 Students who have been assessed as eligible for a Placement Scholarship but whose

POSTGRADUATE SCHOLARSHIPS 
	
Taught Postgraduate Care-leavers Support Scholarship 
 
1. Purpose and Scope  
1.1 This section of the document outlines the eligibility and assessment criteria for students 
to receive scholarships from Aston University for students starting taught postgraduate 
degree programmes in 2017/18.  This policy is correct at the time of publishing but will be 
reviewed annually and is subject to change.   
 
2. Application eligibility 
 
2.1 A student may be considered to receive a Postgraduate Care-leavers Support Scheme 
Scholarship (PCSS) if: 
 
a) they are classed as Home/EU for tuition fee purposes and they are not defined as 
studying for an Equivalent or Lower Qualification12 
 
b) they are holding an offer for a taught postgraduate Masters programme at Aston 
University which will start between 1st September 2017 and 1st June 2018 
 
c) they have identified that they are a Care Leaver at application stage 
 
d) the Scholarship amount will be £3,000 for a full time student; where a student has 
enrolled as a part-time student their scholarship will be awarded on a pro-rata basis. 
 
2.2 A student who is awarded PCSS will be eligible to receive a scholarship for their taught 
postgraduate Masters programme studied at Aston University in 2017/18.  The Scholarship 
will be received as a tuition fee discount.  If the student’s tuition fee exceeds the Scholarship 
amount awarded the student will remain liable for the remaining fee outstanding. 
 
3. General Provisions 
 
3.1 A student who has their fees paid by a sponsor will not be eligible for an Aston 
Scholarship. 
 
3.2 A student will not be eligible to receive a scholarship in full or in part if they are, at the 
time when payment is due to be made to them, considered to be in debt to the University.   
For the purposes of this policy a student will be considered to be in debt to the University if 
they have received the third notice that a payment is overdue. 
 
3.3 Students who are enrolled upon a distance learning programme at Aston University are 
not eligible for this scholarship. 
 
4.  Approving and awarding  
 
4.1 A student’s scholarship eligibility will be approved on an annual basis.  Receipt of any 
scholarship in any year of the degree programme does not necessarily guarantee approval 
of a scholarship in subsequent years.

4.2 Students will not need to apply to be approved for a PCSS scholarship because Aston 
University will use UCAS data and information provided during the application process to 
determine awards. 
 
4.3 PCSS Scholarships will only be approved once in an academic year.  Scholarship 
entitlement will normally be approved before the commencement of the degree programme.  
It is not normally possible to consider a student for an award once the degree programme 
has commenced. 
 
4.5 PCSS Scholarships will normally be available only to students who have been in 
attendance, as defined by the University throughout term one and term two and are still in 
attendance at the start of term three.  Students who withdraw from Aston University part way 
through an academic year will not be eligible to receive a scholarship in respect of that year.  
The student will be liable to repay any overpayment that may result from this.   
 
4.6 Students who are repeating their studies are not eligible for scholarships regardless of 
whether they are repeating with attendance, without attendance, or with partial attendance. 
 
4.7 Where a student suspends their studies and takes a Leave of Absence for a complete 
academic year (i.e.  October- October) no tuition fee is charged and, therefore, the student 
will not be eligible to receive a scholarship.   When a student resumes their studies, following 
a Leave of Absence for a complete academic year, they will be eligible to receive the 
scholarship in line with the conditions that applied in their original year of entry. 
 
4.8 Students who suspend their studies part way through an academic year and take a 
Leave of Absence will be eligible to receive a scholarship for the academic terms they have 
completed in full.  When a student resumes their studies following a Leave of Absence, part 
way through an academic year they will only be eligible to receive a scholarship for the terms 
they will complete in full.  The amount of scholarship will be approved on a pro rata basis 
and in line with Aston University’s Tuition Fees Charging Policy.   
 
4.9 PCSS Scholarships are valid for study on a postgraduate taught Master’s programme at 
Aston University and are not transferable to another University. 
 
4.10 The PCSS Scholarships are valid for programmes of study commencing in the 
academic year 2017/18 only and cannot be carried forward to another academic year. 
 
4.11 If any information provided in the application is found to be false or missing any offer of 
a Postgraduate Scholarship may be withdrawn.  The applicant may be liable for any tuition 
fees incurred. 
 
4.12 Applicants must meet all conditions of their offer (e.g. offer is conditional on obtaining 
specified grades) to be eligible for a scholarship. 
 
4.13 Applicants who qualify for more than one scholarship will only receive the one which is 
the most financially valuable to them. 
 
4.14 The Aston Graduate discount will be applied to tuition fees for applicants who qualify for 
the PCSS Scholarship.

Appendix B Glossary  
 
These meanings apply only to Aston University Home and EU Scholarship Policy 2017/18 
and may not hold the same meanings or be interpreted in the same way in other documents.   
 
Academic Term 
The academic year is divided into three academic terms for undergraduate payment 
arrangements. 
 
Academic year  
This is the period over which Aston University teaches a programme.  For most 
undergraduate programmes, this normally begins at the start of October and ends in the 
middle of June.   Students should normally be in attendance during this period. 
 
Alumni Scholarships 
These Scholarships are offered by the Development and Alumni Relations Department of 
Aston University from funds donated by alumni of Aston University.  These Scholarships 
might be named after a specific donor or may be from a general fund donated by more than 
one donor. 
 
Alumni Named Scholarships 
These Scholarships are offered by the Development and Alumni Relations Department of 
Aston University from funds donated by alumni of Aston University.  These Scholarships are 
named after a specific donor. 
 
Attendance  
For the purposes of Aston Scholarship approvals, a student is considered to be in 
attendance if Aston University’s student records systems show that they are a current 
student.   Attendance requirements to pass a degree programme may differ and should be 
clarified with the specific programme leader. 
 
Care leaver 
For the purposes of this policy a care-leaver has identified this at pre-enrolment and is 
defined as “If you were looked after for at least 13 weeks since the age of 14, and were in 
the care of the local authority and/or a health and social care trust on your 16th birthday” 
(Buttle Trust) 
 
Deferred studies  
This is when exams and/or assessments are delayed until an agreed period of time has 
elapsed.   
 
Equivalent or Lower Qualification 
A student holds an Equivalent or Lower Qualification13 if they already hold an awarded 
qualification which is at the same level as or is higher than the programme they will be 
studying at Aston University. 
 
EU student  
This is a student who is an EU national (or the relevant family member of an EU national) 
and who qualifies to be considered for a tuition fee loan from the UK government.  These 
students cannot be charged more than £9,250 for their tuition fees.  The rules about who 
																																																													
13	As	defined	by	the	Higher	Education	Funding	Council	for	England	
19	
	
December	2016	
qualifies as an EU student depend on the immigration status of the student and their family 
members and where they have all been living.   
 
Home student  
This is a student who qualifies to be considered for a tuition fee loan and grants and loans 
for living costs from the UK government.  These students cannot be charged more than 
£9,250 for their tuition fees.  The rules about who qualifies as a home student depend on 
nationality, the immigration status of the student and their family members and where they 
all have been living.   
 
Household Income  
This is the household income as calculated by the relevant funding authority for a student’s 
application for student funding from the UK government.  It is not possible for Aston 
University to accept any alternative assessment method of a student’s household income.   
 
My Aston Portal (MAP)  
This is the Aston University online student portal through which students can view and 
update personal information and find information about their programme.  Students will be 
able to access information about the progress of Aston Scholarship assessments and 
approvals from their student homepage on MAP.   
 
Re-enrolment  
All students are expected to re-enrol each September, irrespective of their start date.  The 
purpose of re-enrolment is to confirm that the student accepts the University’s terms and 
conditions and the University’s Regulations for that specific academic year.  The re-
enrolment process is also used to update any changes to the student’s personal information.  
Re-enrolment is via MAP and the student will be emailed when the MAP task is available for 
the student to complete.  
 
Repeating studies as if for the first time  
This is when exams, assessments or modules are retaken but are treated as a first attempt 
and the mark the student receives is not limited to the pass mark, this is usually due to 
exceptional circumstances that are agreed on an individual case by case basis.   
 
Repeating studies with attendance  
This is when a student does not progress to the next level of study and has to retake exams 
and/or assessments in the following year and is required to attend all of the lectures, classes 
and tutorials for those modules.   
 
Repeating studies without attendance  
This is when a student does not progress to the next level of study and has to retake exams 
and/or assessments in the following year and is not required to attend any of the lectures, 
classes and tutorials for those modules.   
 
Repeating studies with partial attendance  
This is when a student has to retake exams, assessments and/or modules in the following 
year and is required to attend some of the lectures, classes and tutorials for those modules.   
 
Sandwich placement year  
This is a period of industrial, professional, linguistic or occupational training/work experience 
or study abroad which is approved by the University and forms part of the assessment for a 
sandwich degree or language degree at Aston University.  Sometimes a student is paid 
during their placement for the work they do by their placement employer which is called a 
paid placement.  In other cases, students do not receive any money from their placement 
20	
	
December	2016	
employer for their work and this is called an unpaid placement.  If the placement takes place 
outside of the UK then it is considered to be a work or study placement overseas.   
 
Satisfactory academic performance  
For the purposes of Aston Scholarship approvals, a student is considered to have a 
satisfactory academic performance if they have been accepted to start the first year of their 
programme or they have been considered by an Examination Board to have passed and to 
be eligible to progress into the next stage of study.   
 
Special Support Grant  
This is a grant for living costs from the UK Government which is for students who have an 
entitlement to receive Social Security Benefits (for example they have children or are 
disabled).  It is assessed and awarded by the relevant Student Finance body.   
 
Stage of study 
Stage 1 equates to the entry to year 1 of a degree programme or year 0 of the Foundation 
Year Programme, 
Stage 2 follows stage 1 after successful completion of that year of study, 
Stage P is the placement/sandwich year and often follows stage 2, 
Stage 3 follows stage 2 after successful completion of that year of study for those students 
whose programme of study is made up of four or more taught years of study e.g. MPharm, 
Stage F is the final year of study of a degree programme. 
 
Student Awards Agency for Scotland  
This is the organisation that assesses and awards student funding from the UK government 
to Home students who live in Scotland.  This organisation also assesses and awards student 
funding from the UK government to EU students who study in Scotland.   
 
Student Finance England  
This is the organisation that assesses and awards student funding from the UK government 
to Home students who live in England.   
 
Student Finance Northern Ireland  
This is the organisation that assesses and awards student funding from the UK government 
to Home students who live in Northern Ireland.   
 
Student Finance Services  
This is the organisation that assesses and awards student funding from the UK government 
to EU students in England, Wales and Northern Ireland.  It is also sometimes known as the 
EU Team or the European Services Team.   
 
Student Finance Wales  
This is the organisation that assesses and awards student funding from the UK government 
to Home students who live in Wales.   
 
Student Loans Company  
This is the organisation that manages the payment and repayment of loans and grants for 
student support funding.  This organisation is also responsible for collating information about 
household income and sharing this information with Universities for bursary and scholarship 
assessments.   
 
Suspending studies (Leave of Absence)  
This is when a student stops their studies for a period (normally longer than 60 days) for 
reasons such as illness.  This is also sometimes called a Leave of Absence.   
21	
	
December	2016	
 
UCAS  
This stands for the University and Colleges Admission System.  It is the system students use 
to apply for undergraduate places at universities and colleges in the UK.

Undergraduate Scholarships 
 
The Aston Scholarship Portfolio 
 
Aston University reviews its portfolio of Scholarships on an annual basis.  Scholarships 
offered for one entry cohort may not be offered for following cohorts.  The Terms and 
Conditions of specific scholarships may differ dependent on the year of first offering. 
 
 
1 Purpose and Scope  
 
1.1 This section of the document outlines the eligibility and assessment criteria for students 
to receive scholarships from Aston University as part of the Higher Education funding 
arrangements for students starting undergraduate degree programmes in 2016/17.  This 
policy is correct at the time of publication but may be subject to change. 
 
2 General Provisions  
 
2.1 A student qualifies to be considered for an Aston Scholarship if:  
 
(a) the student will start a new full time undergraduate degree programme at Aston 
University between 1st September 2016 the 31st August 2017. 
 
(b) the student will be liable to pay tuition fees of £9,000 or £1,000 in the placement year or 
they are studying an Equivalent or Lower Qualification1 and  liable to pay tuition fees of 
£10,500 or £2,500 in the placement year 
 
(c) the student is not a resident of the Channel Islands or the Isle of Man (unless the student 
is entitled to benefit from European Community provisions relating to employment or 
establishment and is in receipt of UK student support funding as a home or EU student).   
 
(d) the student qualifies to receive student support funding as part of the finance 
arrangements for new students starting their degree programmes between 1st September 
2016 the 31st August 2017 except if they are studying an Equivalent or Lower Qualification 
 
2.2 A student who is awarded a scholarship will be eligible to receive that scholarship in line 
with the conditions that applied in their original year of entry irrespective of subsequent 
transfers or suspension of studies. 
 
2.3 The household income thresholds used to assess eligibility for the award of a 
scholarship approved on household income will be reviewed once each academic year.   
 
2.4 A student will not be entitled to receive a scholarship in any academic year for which 
they do not have to pay tuition fees.   
 
2.5 With the exception of a placement year, a student will only be eligible to be considered 
for an Aston Scholarship approved on household income for an academic year if they have 
made an application to be income assessed for the same year by Student Finance England, 
Student Finance Wales, Student Finance Northern Ireland, Student Awards Agency for 
Scotland or Student Finance Services.   
																																																													
1	As	defined	by	the	Higher	Education	Funding	Council	for	England	(see	Glossary)	
3	 	 v7	Oct	15	
	
 
2.6 A student who has their fees paid by a sponsor will not be eligible for an Aston 
Scholarship2. 
 
2.7 A student will not be eligible to receive a scholarship in full or in part if they are, at the 
time when payment is due to be made to them, considered by the University to be in 
academic debt3.   For the purposes of this policy a student will be considered to be in 
academic debt to the University if they have received the third notice that a payment is 
overdue. 
 
3.  Approving and awarding  
 
3.1 Students will only be approved for Aston Scholarships once in an academic year.   
Scholarship entitlement will normally be determined by the end of November using the 
information that is available to Aston University at that time.  Any scholarship assessments 
which cannot be considered at the end of November because the required information is not 
yet available will be reviewed on a monthly basis until all relevant information has been 
received and the student’s scholarship entitlement can be determined.  It is not normally 
possible to consider a student for an award of an Aston Scholarship after 30th May of the 
academic year in question.   
 
3.2 Students do not need to apply to be considered for a scholarship because Aston 
University will use UCAS data, household income information provided by the Student Loans 
Company and information held on University records for placement years, to determine 
awards.   
 
3.3 Students who are eligible for one of more of the Aston Scholarships will receive 
communications concerning their award/s through My Aston Portal (MAP)  
 
3.4 Students who are eligible for one or more of the Aston Scholarships or the Aston Aspire 
Scholarship Programme will be required to confirm the format they wish that scholarship to 
take, in line with the choices offered in the first term of each academic year.  This 
confirmation of choice will be final and will not be amended. 
 
3.5 The Student Loans Company charges interest on tuition fee loans at a daily rate from the 
date payments are made to universities.  Aston University cannot accept any responsibility 
for interest applied to tuition fee loans by the Student Loans Company.   
 
3.6 Eligibility for a scholarship approved on household income will be determined on the 
basis of information provided by the Student Loans Company once the student has been 
fully enrolled on the degree programme.  Aston University aims to consider scholarships 
based on household income within eight weeks of receiving household income information 
from the Student Loans Company.  Any student who is approved for an income-based 
scholarship will be notified via MAP.  The University will notify the Student Loans Company 
about fee discounts and changes in tuition fee liability.   
 
																																																													
2 For	the	purposes	of	this	policy	a	sponsor	is	an	external	organisation,	not	a	family	member	nor	the	
Student	Loans	Company. 
3	As	defined	in	the	Aston	Finance	Sanctions	Policy	
4	 	 v7	Oct	15	
	
3.7 Eligibility for a scholarship during a placement year will be approved on the basis of 
information held on University records about previous scholarship approvals and placement 
details.  Approvals of scholarships for placement years will be communicated to students via 
MAP usually by the end of term one of that academic year4.  The University will notify the 
Student Loans Company about any fee discounts and changes in tuition fee liability.   
 
3.8  Where a student has a choice to take their scholarship in the form of tuition fee discount 
and has taken out a tuition fee loan from the Student Loans Company, the University is 
required to notify the Student Loans Company of any changes in a student’s tuition fee 
liability.  If a student has taken out the maximum tuition fee loan available to pay their tuition 
fee in full, their maximum tuition fee loan entitlement and payments should be adjusted 
accordingly by the Student Loans Company.  If a student has only taken a partial tuition fee 
loan to pay part of their tuition fees, the student will need to contact the Student Loans 
Company to adjust the amount of loan they wish to borrow.   
 
3.9 Where a student has a choice and has chosen to take their scholarship in the form of 
accommodation discount but leaves Aston University accommodation within six weeks of the 
beginning of their first term, their scholarship will automatically be re-designated as a tuition 
fee discount. 
 
3.10 For Aston Scholarships where eligible students are given a choice of award, students 
must make their choices by the deadline that will be published on MAP.   
 
3.11 For Aston Scholarships where eligible students are given a choice of award and they 
have selected payment directly into their bank account, students must provide their bank 
account details when asked to by the published deadline on MAP.   Should a student not 
provide this information by the published deadline, the award will default to be a tuition fee 
discount.  This award will not be reversible. 
 
3.12  Aston Scholarships will normally only be available to students who have been in 
attendance, as defined by the University throughout term one and term two and are still in 
attendance at the start of term three.  Students who withdraw from Aston University part way 
through an academic year will not be eligible to receive a scholarship in respect of that year.  
Any scholarship applied to the student for that academic year as the result of an Aston 
Scholarship will be revoked and the full cost for that period will be recovered.   
 
3.13 Students who have been assessed as eligible for a Placement Scholarship but whose 
eligibility changes after the award has been confirmed, may have their award amended on a 
pro-rata basis to reflect the period of time that the eligibility was in place.  Students will be 
liable to repay any overpayment of the award that may result from this. 
 
3.14 Students who are repeating their studies that are not deferred are not eligible for 
scholarships regardless of whether they are repeating with attendance, without attendance, 
or with partial attendance.   
 
3.15 Where a student suspends their studies and takes a Leave of Absence for a complete 
academic year, no tuition fee is charged and, therefore, the student will not be eligible to 
receive a scholarship. 
 
																																																													
4	The	academic	year	is	defined	in	the	Glossary	
5	 	 v7	Oct	15	
	
3.16 Students who suspend their studies part way through an academic year will be eligible 
to receive a scholarship for the academic terms they have completed in full.  Students who 
suspend their studies and return from a suspension of studies part way through an academic 
year will only be eligible to receive a scholarship for the terms they will complete in full.  The 
amount of scholarship will be approved on a pro rata basis and in line with Aston University’s 
Tuition Fees Charging Policy for that academic year.   
 
4.  Eligibility criteria for Aston University Undergraduate Scholarships  
 
Aston University offers two scholarship packages.  The first scholarship package is approved 
on the basis of academic excellence or placement details.  The second scholarship package 
is approved based on household income as calculated by the Student Loans Company  
 
Scholarships that are approved on the basis of academic excellence or placement 
details  
 
4.1 Aston Excellence Scholarship  
 
4.1.1 A student is eligible to receive an Aston Excellence Scholarship if:  
 
(a) at enrolment the student meets the general provisions outlined in paragraph 2.1 and  
 
(b) prior to enrolment the student has achieved grades AAB+ in their A levels (or equivalent 
qualifications as outlined in Appendix A).  The grades refer to the student’s highest 
qualifications, not their entry qualifications.   
 
4.1.2 A student who is awarded an Aston Excellence Scholarship will be eligible to receive:  
 
(a) the choice of either: 
 
(i) a £1,000 discount from their accommodation costs, paid in two equal 
instalments of £500 in the second and third terms, when they enter stage 1 of 
a programme of study and are resident in Aston Student Village, 
 
or 
 
(ii) a £1,000 tuition fee discount when they enter stage 1 of a programme of 
study, 
 
or 
 
(iii) if the student is not resident in Aston Student Village they can choose a 
payment of £1,000, paid in two equal instalments of £500  into their bank 
account in the second and third terms when they enter stage 1 of a 
programme of study. 
 
(b) where the student undertakes a placement year 5 as part of their degree programme and 
where a placement tuition fee is charged to the student, the student will be eligible to 
receive the choice of either: 
 
																																																													
5	This includes students on the MEng/MBiol/MOptom courses with an integrated placement study year  
6	 	 v7	Oct	15	
	
(i) a £1,000 discount from their accommodation paid in two equal instalments of 
£500 in the second and third terms, when they are resident in Aston Student 
Village or 
 
(ii) a £1,000 tuition fee discount, 
 
or 
 
(iii) if the student is not resident in Aston Student Village they can choose a 
payment of £1,000, paid in two equal instalments of £500 into their bank 
account in the second and third terms. 
 
4.1.3 A student who is awarded an Aston Excellence Scholarship can also be considered for 
scholarships approved on household income for the same academic year.   
 
4.1.4 A student will only be awarded one scholarship in relation to the placement year.   
 
4.1.5 Eligibility for an Aston Scholarship based on achievement will normally be approved on 
the basis of information provided by UCAS.  Eligibility for Aston Scholarships based on 
achievement will be communicated to students as part of their Unconditional Offer and will 
normally be confirmed by the end of November.  Information will be available through the 
student homepage on MAP.  Notification will be sent to the Student Loans Company about 
fee discounts and changes in tuition fee liability where appropriate by Aston University.   
 
4.2 Aston Placement Scholarship  
 
4.2.1 A student is eligible to receive an Aston Placement Scholarship if:  
 
(a) the student meets the general provisions outlined in paragraph 2.1, and  
 
(b) the student is undertaking an unpaid placement for their sandwich placement year, or 
 
(c) the student is undertaking a work or study placement overseas, or 
 
(d) the student undertaking the MEng/MBiol/MOptom integrated placement study year.  
 
4.2.2 A student who is awarded an Aston Placement Scholarship will be eligible to choose 
between receiving either:  
 
(i) a £1,000 discount from their accommodation costs for their placement year 
paid, in two equal instalments of £500 in the second and third terms, when 
they are resident in Aston Student Village 
 
or 
 
(ii) a £1,000 tuition fee discount, 
 
or 
 
(iii) if the student is not resident in Aston Student Village they can choose a 
payment of £1,000, paid in two equal instalments of £500  into their bank 
account in the second and third terms. 
 
7	 	 v7	Oct	15	
	
4.2.3 A student can only be awarded one scholarship for the placement year so students 
cannot receive any other Scholarship awards for this specific year. 
 
Scholarships that are approved on household income  
 
4.3 Aston Aspire Scholarship Programme  
 
The Aston Aspire Scholarship Programme is targeted at:  
 
 UK domiciled students who have been assessed by Student Finance England, 
Student Finance Wales, Student Finance Northern Ireland, Student Awards Agency 
for Scotland or Student Finance Services to have a household income up to and 
including £18,000, and 
 are living in Aston Student Village in year one of their studies,  or  
 who have identified that they are a Care Leaver 6 at pre-enrolment.   
 
4.3.1 A student is eligible to receive an Aston Aspire Scholarship Programme award if:  
 
 (a) the student meets the general provisions outlined in paragraph 2.1, and  
 
 (b) the student is regarded as a “home student” for fee purposes and 
 
 (c) the student is in receipt of an amount of Maintenance Grant or Special Support Grant 
from either Student Finance England, Student Finance Wales, Student Finance Northern 
Ireland, Student Awards Agency for Scotland or Student Finance Services for the current 
academic year, and  
 
(d) the student has currently been assessed by either Student Finance England, Student 
Finance Wales, Student Finance Northern Ireland, Student Awards Agency for Scotland or 
Student Finance Services to have a household income of up to and including £18,000, and 
has either:  
 
(e) lived in Aston Student Village for the full duration of stage 1 of their programme of study 
and has paid their residence fees in full, or 
 
(f) has identified that they are a Care Leaver at pre-enrolment. 
 
4.3.2 A student who is awarded an Aston Aspire Scholarship Programme award will be 
eligible to receive:  
 
(a) a £1,000 discount from the cost of their of accommodation paid in the third term, when 
they enter stage 1 of a programme of study and are resident in Aston Student Village.   
 
  
																																																													
6	For the purposes of this policy a care-leaver has identified this at pre-enrolment and is defined as “If you were looked after 
for at least 13 weeks since the age of 14, and were in the care of the local authority and/or a health and social care trust on 
your 16th birthday” (Buttle Trust)	
8	 	 v7	Oct	15	
	
In their subsequent Placement Year7 they will be eligible to receive: 
 
(b) either: 
 
(i) a £1,000 discount where the student undertakes a placement year as part of 
their degree programme and where a placement tuition fee8 is charged to the 
student; 
Or 
 
(ii) £1,000, paid in two equal instalments into their bank account in the second 
and third term. 
 
4.3.3 Students who have identified they are a care-leaver  at pre-enrolment and are not 
resident Aston Student Village are entitled to a £1,000 tuition fee discount.  In their 
subsequent Placement Year they will be eligible to receive either: 
 
(i) a £1,000 tuition fee discount where the student undertakes a placement year 
as part of their degree programme and where a placement tuition fee9 is 
charged to the student; 
Or 
 
(ii) £1,000 paid in two equal instalments into their bank account in the second 
and third terms. 
 
4.3.4 A student can only be eligible for one scholarship award for the placement year.  
 
4.4 Aston Alumni Scholarships  
 
4.4.1 A student will be eligible to be awarded an Aston Alumni Scholarship if they qualify to 
be awarded both an Aston Excellence Scholarship and an Aston Aspire Scholarship in stage 
1 of their programme and agrees to the responsibilities expected of them under the terms of 
the Alumni Scholarship Award as set out below: 
 
(i) Upon receipt of an Alumni Scholarship, the student will: 
 
(ii) on reasonable request from the Development & Alumni Relations Office, 
participate in periodic events organised by the University at which some of 
the alumni donors might be present; 
(iii) on reasonable request from the Development & Alumni Relations Office, 
contribute to University publications where these Scholarships are promoted; 
(iv) comply with any reasonable request from the Development and Alumni 
Relations Office. 
  
																																																													
7	This includes students on the MEng/MBiol/MOptom courses with an integrated placement study year	
8	Placement	tuition	fee	is	currently	£1,000.	
9	Placement	tuition	fee	is	currently	£1,000.	
9	 	 v7	Oct	15	
	
4.4.2 A student who is awarded an Aston Alumni Scholarship will be eligible to receive:  
 
(a) the choice of either: 
 
(i) a £2,000 discount from their accommodation costs, paid in two equal 
instalments of £1000 in the second and third terms, when they enter stage 1 
of a programme of study and are resident in Aston Student Village, 
 
or 
 
(ii) a £2,000 tuition fee discount when they enter stage 1 of a programme of 
study, 
 
or 
 
(iii) if the student is not resident in Aston Student Village they can choose a 
payment of £2,000, paid in two equal instalments of £1000  into their bank 
account in the second and third terms when they enter stage 1 of a 
programme of study. 
 
(b) where the student undertakes a placement year 10 as part of their degree programme and 
where a placement tuition fee is charged to the student, the student will be eligible to 
receive the choice of either: 
 
(i) a £1,000 discount from their accommodation paid in two equal instalments of 
£500 in the second and third terms, when they are resident in Aston Student 
Village or 
 
(ii) a £1,000 tuition fee discount, 
 
or 
 
(iii) if the student is not resident in Aston Student Village they can choose a 
payment of £1,000, paid in two equal instalments of £500 into their bank 
account in the second and third terms. 
 
4.4.3 A student who is eligible for the Alumni Scholarship is not eligible to receive an Aston 
Excellence Scholarship and/or an Aston Aspire Scholarship in the same academic 
year. 
 
4.4.4 A student will only be awarded one scholarship in relation to the placement year.   
 
4.4..5 Upon receipt of an Alumni Named Scholarship, the student will: 
 
(i) through the  Development & Alumni Relations Office maintain contact with the 
Donor or their family by way of an annual communication within specified 
deadlines; 
(ii) through the  Development & Alumni Relations Office may meet the donor 
and, where this occurs, the meeting will be arranged and attended by a 
representative from the Development & Alumni Relations Office;

(iv) comply with any reasonable request from the Development and Alumni

4.4..6 The student will be paid the proportion of their Scholarship relating to the Aston 
Excellence Scholarship under the same terms, conditions and critiera as described in 
section 4.1.   
 
4.4..7 The student will be paid the proportion of their Scholarship relating to the Aston 
Aspire Scholarship under the same terms, conditions and criteria as described in section 4.3 
 
4.4..8 The University will decide whether to offe r a student the opportunity to receive either 
an Aston Excellence and Aspire Scholarship or an Aston Alumni Scholarship on the basis of 
a random selection process. 
 
4.4.9 The Alumni Scholarship will be either awarded under the title ‘Alumni Scholarship’ or 
it may be titled after a specific alumni donor (Alumni Named Scholarship).  It is expected that 
most Alumni Scholarships will be named after a specific donor. 
 
4.4.10 Should a student fail to uphold their responsibilities in relation to the Aston Alumni 
Scholarship Award their scholarship will be replaced by an Aston Excellence Scholarship.

Appendix B Glossary  
 
These meanings apply only to Aston University Home and EU Scholarship Policy 2016/17 
and may not hold the same meanings or be interpreted in the same way in other documents.   
 
Academic Term 
The academic year is divided into three academic terms for undergraduate payment 
arrangements. 
 
Academic year  
 
This is the period over which Aston University teaches a programme.  For most 
undergraduate programmes, this normally begins at the start of October and ends in the 
middle of June.   Students should normally be in attendance during this period. 
 
Alumni Scholarships 
 
These Scholarships are offered by the Development and Alumni Relations Department of 
Aston University from funds donated by alumni of Aston University.  These Scholarships 
might be named after a specific donor or may be from a general fund donated by more than 
one donor. 
 
Alumni Named Scholarships 
 
These Scholarships are offered by the Development and Alumni Relations Department of 
Aston University from funds donated by alumni of Aston University.  These Scholarships are 
named after a specific donor. 
 
Aston Scholarship 
 
There are two types of Aston Scholarships.  The first are not approved on household income 
and are approved on the basis of academic excellence11 or placement12 details.  These are 
the Aston Excellence and the Aston Placement Scholarships.  The second type of 
scholarships is approved based on the household income.  These are the National 
Scholarship Programme awards, and the Aston Progression Scholarship.   
 
Attendance  
 
For the purposes of Aston Scholarship approvals, a student is considered to be in 
attendance if Aston University’s student records systems show that they are a current 
student.   Attendance requirements to pass a degree programme may differ and should be 
clarified with the specific programme leader. 
 
Care leaver 
For the purposes of this policy a care-leaver has identified this at pre-enrolment and is 
defined as “If you were looked after for at least 13 weeks since the age of 14, and were in 
																																																													
11	If	the	student	has	GCE	A	level	grade	AAB	or	above,	or	equivalent	(see	the	Appendix	for	definition	of	
equivalences).	
12	If	the	student	takes	a	paid	placement	year	or	year	abroad,	the	tuition	fee	for	that	year	will	be	just	
£1,000.		If	the	student	takes	an	unpaid	placement	year,	there	will	be	no	tuition	fee.	
18	 	 v7	Oct	15	
	
the care of the local authority and/or a health and social care trust on your 16th birthday” 
(Buttle Trust) 
 
Deferred studies  
 
This is when exams and/or assessments are delayed until an agreed period of time has 
elapsed.   
 
Equivalent or Lower Qualification 
 
A student holds an Equivalent or Lower Qualification13 if they already hold an awarded 
qualification which is at the same level as or is higher than the programme they will be 
studying at Aston University. 
 
ERASMUS fee waivers  
 
Students who undertake a work or study placement outside of the UK but within the EEA 
may qualify for financial help from an organisation called ERASMUS.  In some cases, 
ERASMUS will pay the student’s tuition fees for their placement year and this is called an 
ERASMUS fee waiver.   
 
EU student  
 
This is a student who is an EU national (or the relevant family member of an EU national) 
and who qualifies to be considered for a tuition fee loan from the UK government.  These 
students cannot be charged more than £9,000 for their tuition fees.  The rules about who 
qualifies as an EU student depend on the immigration status of the student and their family 
members and where they have all been living.   
 
Home student  
 
This is a student who qualifies to be considered for a tuition fee loan and grants and loans 
for living costs from the UK government.  These students cannot be charged more than 
£9,000 for their tuition fees.  The rules about who qualifies as a home student depend on 
nationality, the immigration status of the student and their family members and where they 
all have been living.   
 
Household Income  
 
This is the household income as calculated by the relevant funding authority for a student’s 
application for student funding from the UK government.  It is not possible for Aston 
University to accept any alternative assessment method of a student’s household income.   
 
Maintenance grant  
 
This is a grant for living costs from the UK Government which is assessed and awarded by 
the relevant Student Finance national body.  Students cannot receive the Maintenance Grant 
and the Special Support Grant at the same time.   
 
 
																																																													
13	As	defined	by	the	Higher	Education	Funding	Council	for	England	
19	 	 v7	Oct	15	
	
My Aston Portal (MAP)  
 
This is the Aston University online student portal through which students can view and 
update personal information and find information about their programme.  Students will be 
able to access information about the progress of Aston Scholarship assessments and 
approvals from their student homepage on MAP.   
Re-enrolment  
 
All students are expected to re-enrol each September, irrespective of their start date.  The 
purpose of re-enrolment is to confirm that the student accepts the University’s terms and 
conditions and the University’s Regulations for that specific academic year.  The re-
enrolment process is also used to update any changes to the student’s personal information.  
Re-enrolment is via MAP and the student will be emailed when the MAP task is available for 
the student to complete.  
 
Repeating studies as if for the first time  
 
This is when exams, assessments or modules are retaken but are treated as a first attempt 
and the mark the student receives is not limited to the pass mark, this is usually due to 
exceptional circumstances that are agreed on an individual case by case basis.   
 
Repeating studies with attendance  
 
This is when a student does not progress to the next level of study and has to retake exams 
and/or assessments in the following year and is required to attend all of the lectures, classes 
and tutorials for those modules.   
 
Repeating studies without attendance  
 
This is when a student does not progress to the next level of study and has to retake exams 
and/or assessments in the following year and is not required to attend any of the lectures, 
classes and tutorials for those modules.   
 
Repeating studies with partial attendance  
 
This is when a student has to retake exams, assessments and/or modules in the following 
year and is required to attend some of the lectures, classes and tutorials for those modules.   
 
Sandwich placement year  
 
This is a period of industrial, professional, linguistic or occupational training/work experience 
or study abroad which is approved by the University and forms part of the assessment for a 
sandwich degree or language degree at Aston University.  Sometimes a student is paid 
during their placement for the work they do by their placement employer which is called a 
paid placement.  In other cases, students do not receive any money from their placement 
employer for their work and this is called an unpaid placement.  If the placement takes place 
outside of the UK then it is considered to be a work or study placement overseas.   
 
Satisfactory academic performance  
 
For the purposes of Aston Scholarship approvals, a student is considered to have a 
satisfactory academic performance if they have been accepted to start the first year of their 
programme or they have been considered by an Examination Board to have passed and to 
be eligible to progress into the next stage of study.   
20	 	 v7	Oct	15	
	
 
Special Support Grant  
 
This is a grant for living costs from the UK Government which is for students who have an 
entitlement to receive Social Security Benefits (for example they have children or are 
disabled).  It is assessed and awarded by the relevant Student Finance body.  Students 
cannot receive the Special Support Grant and the Maintenance Grant at the same time.   
 
Stage of study 
Stage 1 equates to the entry to year 1 of a degree programme, 
Stage 2 follows stage 1 after successful completion of that year of study, 
Stage P is the placement/sandwich year and often follows stage 2, 
Stage 3 follows stage 2 after successful completion of that year of study for those students 
whose programme of study is made up of four or more taught years of study e.g. MPharm, 
Stage F is the final year of study of a degree programme. 
 
Student Awards Agency for Scotland  
 
This is the organisation that assesses and awards student funding from the UK government 
to Home students who live in Scotland.  This organisation also assesses and awards student 
funding from the UK government to EU students who study in Scotland.   
 
Student Finance England  
 
This is the organisation that assesses and awards student funding from the UK government 
to Home students who live in England.   
 
Student Finance Northern Ireland  
 
This is the organisation that assesses and awards student funding from the UK government 
to Home students who live in Northern Ireland.   
 
Student Finance Services  
 
This is the organisation that assesses and awards student funding from the UK government 
to EU students in England, Wales and Northern Ireland.  It is also sometimes known as the 
EU Team or the European Services Team.   
 
Student Finance Wales  
 
This is the organisation that assesses and awards student funding from the UK government 
to Home students who live in Wales.   
 
Student Loans Company  
 
This is the organisation that manages the payment and repayment of loans and grants for 
student support funding.  This organisation is also responsible for collating information about 
household income and sharing this information with Universities for bursary and scholarship 
assessments.   
 
Suspending studies (Leave of Absence)  
 
This is when a student stops their studies for a period (normally longer than 60 days) for 
reasons such as illness.  This is also sometimes called a Leave of Absence.   
21	 	 v7	Oct	15	
	
 
UCAS  
 
This stands for the University and Colleges Admission System.  It is the system students use 
to apply for undergraduate places at universities and colleges in the UK.

Undergraduate Scholarships 
 
1 Purpose and Scope  
 
1.1 This section of the document outlines the eligibility and assessment criteria for students 
to receive scholarships from Aston University as part of the Higher Education funding 
arrangements for students starting undergraduate degree programmes in 2015/16 who do 
not receive sponsorship for their fees1.    This policy is correct at the time of publishing but 
will be reviewed annually and is subject to change.   
 
2 General Provisions  
 
2.1 A student who is not defined as studying an Equivalent or Lower Qualification2 qualifies 
to be considered for an Aston Scholarship if:  
 
(a) the student will start a new full time undergraduate degree programme3 at Aston 
University on or after 1st September 2015 and  
 
(b) the student will be liable to pay tuition fees of £9,000 or £1,000 in the placement year and  
 
(c) the student qualifies to receive student support funding as part of the finance 
arrangements for new students starting their degree programmes on or after 1st September 
2015; and  
 
(d) the student is not a resident of the Channel Islands or the Isle of Man (unless the student 
is entitled to benefit from European Community provisions relating to employment or 
establishment and is in receipt of UK student support funding as a home or EU student).   
 
2.2 A student who is defined as studying an Equivalent or Lower Qualification only qualifies 
to be considered for an Aston Scholarship4 if:  
 
(a) the student will start a new full time undergraduate degree programme at Aston 
University on or after 1st September 2015; and  
 
(b) the student will be liable to pay tuition fees of £10,500 or £2,500 in the placement year 
and  
 
(c) the student is not a resident of the Channel Islands or the Isle of Man (unless the student 
is entitled to benefit from European Community provisions relating to employment or  
establishment).   
 
2.3 The household income thresholds used to assess eligibility for the award of a 
scholarship approved on household income will be reviewed once each academic year.   
                                                             
1 For the purposes of this policy a sponsor is an external organisation, not a family member or the Student 
Loans Company   
2 As defined by the Higher Education Funding Council for England (see Glossary)  
3 Not including Foundation Degree Programmes. 
4 Students who are defined as studying an Equivalent or Lower Qualification are currently only eligible for 
the Aston Excellence Scholarship. 
3  v3 Feb 15 
 
 
2.4 A student will not be entitled to receive a scholarship in any academic year for which 
they do not have to pay tuition fees unless it is an unpaid placement year or year abroad, or 
deferred studies, repeating as if for the first time.   
 
2.5 With the exception of a placement year, a student will not be eligible to be considered for 
an Aston Scholarship approved on household income for an academic year unless they 
have made an application to be income assessed for the same year by Student Finance 
England, Student Finance Wales, Student Finance Northern Ireland, Student Awards 
Agency for Scotland or Student Finance Services.   
 
2.6 A student who has their fees paid by a sponsor will not be eligible for an Aston 
Scholarship5. 
 
2.7 A student will not be eligible to receive a scholarship in full or in part if they are, at the 
time when payment is due to be made to them, considered to be in debt to the University.   
For the purposes of this policy a student will be considered to be in academic debt6 to the 
University if they have received the third notice that a payment is overdue. 
 
3.  Approving and awarding  
 
3.1 A student’s scholarship eligibility will be approved on an annual basis.  Receipt of any 
scholarship in any year of the degree programme does not necessarily guarantee approval 
of a scholarship in subsequent years.  The exception to this is the Placement Scholarship, 
which once awarded will not be revoked unless the student does not meet the general 
requirements for the Placement Scholarship. 
 
3.2 Students will not need to apply to be considered for a scholarship because Aston 
University will use UCAS data, household income information provided by the Student Loans 
Company and information held on University records for placement years, to determine 
awards.   
 
3.3 Students who are eligible for one or more of the Aston Scholarships or the Aston Aspire 
Scholarship Programme will be required to confirm the format they wish that scholarship to 
take, in line with the choices offered in the first term of each academic year.  This 
confirmation of choice will be final and will not be amended. 
 
3.4 Students will only be approved for Aston Scholarships once in an academic year.   
Scholarship entitlement will normally be approved by the end of November using the 
information that is available to Aston University at that time.  Any scholarship assessments 
which cannot be considered at the end of November because the required information is not 
yet available will be reviewed on a monthly basis until all relevant information has been 
received and the student’s scholarship entitlement can be approved.  It is not normally 
possible to consider a student for an award of an Aston Scholarship after 30th May of the 
academic year in question.   
 
                                                             
5 For the purposes of this policy a sponsor is an external organisation, not a family member nor the 
Student Loans Company. 
6 As defined in the Aston Finance Sanctions Policy 
4  v3 Feb 15 
 
3.5 The Student Loans Company charges interest on tuition fee loans at a daily rate from the 
date payments are made to universities.  Aston University cannot accept any responsibility 
for interest applied to tuition fee loans by the Student Loans Company.   
 
3.6 Eligibility for a scholarship approved on household income will be considered on the 
basis of information provided by the Student Loans Company once the student has been 
fully enrolled on the degree programme.  Aston University aims to consider and approve 
scholarships based on household income within eight weeks of receiving household income 
information from the Student Loans Company.  Any student who is approved for an income-
based scholarship will be notified via MAP.  Notification will be sent to the Student Loans 
Company about fee discounts and changes in tuition fee liability.   
 
3.7 Eligibility for a scholarship during a placement year will be approved on the basis of 
information held on University records about previous scholarship approvals and placement 
details.  Approvals of scholarships for placement years will be communicated to students via 
MAP usually by the end of term one.  Notification will be sent to the Student Loans Company 
about any fee discounts and changes in tuition fee liability.   
 
3.8  Where a student has chosen to take their scholarship in the form of tuition fee discount

Appendix B  Glossary   
 
These meanings apply only to Aston University Home and EU Scholarship Policy 2015/16 
and may not hold the same meanings or be interpreted in the same way in other documents.   
 
Academic Term 
The academic year is divided into three academic terms for undergraduate payment 
arrangements. 
 
Academic year  
 
This is the period over which Aston University teaches a programme.  For most 
undergraduate programmes, this normally begins at the start of October and ends in the 
middle of June.   Students should normally be in attendance during this period. 
 
Alumni Scholarships 
 
These Scholarships are offered by the Development and Alumni Relations Department of 
Aston University from funds donated by alumni of Aston University.  These Scholarships 
might be named after a specific donor or may be from a general fund donated by more than 
one donor. 
 
Alumni Named Scholarships 
 
These Scholarships are offered by the Development and Alumni Relations Department of 
Aston University from funds donated by alumni of Aston University.  These Scholarships are 
named after a specific donor. 
 
Aston Scholarship 
 
There are two types of Aston Scholarships.  The first are not approved on household income 
and are approved on the basis of academic excellence12 or placement13 details.  These are 
the Aston Excellence and the Aston Placement Scholarships.  The second type of 
scholarships is approved based on the household income.  These are the National 
Scholarship Programme awards, and the Aston Progression Scholarship.   
 
Attendance  
 
For the purposes of Aston Scholarship approvals, a student is considered to be in 
attendance if Aston University’s student records systems show that they are a current 
student.   Attendance requirements to pass a degree programme may differ and should be 
clarified with the specific programme leader. 
 
Care leaver 
For the purposes of this policy a care-leaver has identified this at pre-enrolment and is 
defined as “If you were looked after for at least 13 weeks since the age of 14, and were in 
                                                             
12 If the student has GCE A level grade AAB or above, or equivalent (see the Appendix for definition of 
equivalences). 
13 If the student takes a paid placement year or year abroad, the tuition fee for that year will be just 
£1,000.  If the student takes an unpaid placement year, there will be no tuition fee. 
25  v3 Feb 15 
 
the care of the local authority and/or a health and social care trust on your 16th birthday” 
(Buttle Trust) 
 
Deferred studies  
 
This is when exams and/or assessments are delayed until an agreed period of time has 
elapsed.   
 
Equivalent or Lower Qualification 
 
A student holds an Equivalent or Lower Qualification14 if they already hold an awarded 
qualification which is at the same level as or is higher than the programme they will be 
studying at Aston University. 
 
ERASMUS fee waivers  
 
Students who undertake a work or study placement outside of the UK but within the EEA 
may qualify for financial help from an organisation called ERASMUS.  In some cases, 
ERASMUS will pay the student’s tuition fees for their placement year and this is called an 
ERASMUS fee waiver.   
 
EU student  
 
This is a student who is an EU national (or the relevant family member of an EU national) 
and who qualifies to be considered for a tuition fee loan from the UK government.  These 
students cannot be charged more than £9,000 for their tuition fees.  The rules about who 
qualifies as an EU student depend on the immigration status of the student and their family 
members and where they have all been living.   
 
Home student  
 
This is a student who qualifies to be considered for a tuition fee loan and grants and loans 
for living costs from the UK government.  These students cannot be charged more than 
£9,000 for their tuition fees.  The rules about who qualifies as a home student depend on 
nationality, the immigration status of the student and their family members and where they 
all have been living.   
 
Household Income  
 
This is the household income as calculated by the relevant funding authority for a student’s 
application for student funding from the UK government.  It is not possible for Aston 
University to accept any alternative assessment method of a student’s household income.   
 
Maintenance grant  
 
This is a grant for living costs from the UK Government which is assessed and awarded by 
the relevant Student Finance national body.  Students cannot receive the Maintenance Grant 
and the Special Support Grant at the same time.   
 
 
                                                             
14 As defined by the Higher Education Funding Council for England  
26  v3 Feb 15 
 
My Aston Portal (MAP)  
 
This is the Aston University online student portal through which students can view and 
update personal information and find information about their programme.  Students will be 
able to access information about the progress of Aston Scholarship assessments and 
approvals from their student homepage on MAP.   
Re-enrolment  
 
All students are expected to re-enrol each September, irrespective of their start date.  The 
purpose of re-enrolment is to confirm that the student accepts the University’s terms and 
conditions and the University’s Regulations for that specific academic year.  The re-
enrolment process is also used to update any changes to the student’s personal information.  
Re-enrolment is via MAP and the student will be emailed when the MAP task is available for 
the student to complete.  
 
Repeating studies as if for the first time  
 
This is when exams, assessments or modules are retaken but are treated as a first attempt 
and the mark the student receives is not limited to the pass mark, this is usually due to 
exceptional circumstances that are agreed on an individual case by case basis.   
 
Repeating studies with attendance  
 
This is when a student does not progress to the next level of study and has to retake exams 
and/or assessments in the following year and is required to attend all of the lectures, classes 
and tutorials for those modules.   
 
Repeating studies without attendance  
 
This is when a student does not progress to the next level of study and has to retake exams 
and/or assessments in the following year and is not required to attend any of the lectures, 
classes and tutorials for those modules.   
 
Repeating studies with partial attendance  
 
This is when a student has to retake exams, assessments and/or modules in the following 
year and is required to attend some of the lectures, classes and tutorials for those modules.   
 
Sandwich placement year  
 
This is a period of industrial, professional, linguistic or occupational training/work experience 
or study abroad which is approved by the University and forms part of the assessment for a 
sandwich degree or language degree at Aston University.  Sometimes a student is paid 
during their placement for the work they do by their placement employer which is called a 
paid placement.  In other cases, students do not receive any money from their placement 
employer for their work and this is called an unpaid placement.  If the placement takes place 
outside of the UK then it is considered to be a work or study placement overseas.   
 
Satisfactory academic performance  
 
For the purposes of Aston Scholarship approvals, a student is considered to have a 
satisfactory academic performance if they have been accepted to start the first year of their 
programme or they have been considered by an Examination Board to have passed and to 
be eligible to progress into the next stage of study.   
27  v3 Feb 15 
 
 
Special Support Grant  
 
This is a grant for living costs from the UK Government which is for students who have an 
entitlement to receive Social Security Benefits (for example they have children or are 
disabled).  It is assessed and awarded by the relevant Student Finance body.  Students 
cannot receive the Special Support Grant and the Maintenance Grant at the same time.   
 
Stage of study 
Stage 1 equates to the entry to year 1 of a degree programme, 
Stage 2 follows stage 1 after successful completion of that year of study, 
Stage P is the placement/sandwich year and often follows stage 2, 
Stage 3 follows stage 2 after successful completion of that year of study for those students 
whose programme of study is made up of four or more taught years of study e.g. MPharm, 
Stage F is the final year of study of a degree programme. 
 
Student Awards Agency for Scotland  
 
This is the organisation that assesses and awards student funding from the UK government 
to Home students who live in Scotland.  This organisation also assesses and awards student 
funding from the UK government to EU students who study in Scotland.   
 
Student Finance England  
 
This is the organisation that assesses and awards student funding from the UK government 
to Home students who live in England.   
 
Student Finance Northern Ireland  
 
This is the organisation that assesses and awards student funding from the UK government 
to Home students who live in Northern Ireland.   
 
Student Finance Services  
 
This is the organisation that assesses and awards student funding from the UK government 
to EU students in England, Wales and Northern Ireland.  It is also sometimes known as the 
EU Team or the European Services Team.   
 
Student Finance Wales  
 
This is the organisation that assesses and awards student funding from the UK government 
to Home students who live in Wales.   
 
Student Loans Company  
 
This is the organisation that manages the payment and repayment of loans and grants for 
student support funding.  This organisation is also responsible for collating information about 
household income and sharing this information with Universities for bursary and scholarship 
assessments.   
 
Suspending studies (Leave of Absence)  
 
This is when a student stops their studies for a period (normally longer than 60 days) for 
reasons such as illness.  This is also sometimes called a Leave of Absence.   
28  v3 Feb 15 
 
 
UCAS  
 
This stands for the University and Colleges Admission System.  It is the system students use 
to apply for undergraduate places at universities and colleges in the UK.
