By studying in London you will have prime location to open up numerous employment and career opportunities, thanks to the city's extensive industry connections and vibrant professional network. How you will learn At Aston University London, every programme on your chosen pathway will begin with a common landing module to introduce key fundamental concepts required by the rest of the pathway and to introduce you to the learning and teaching style of our innovative London courses. You will be taught by a combination of academic and industry experts to ensure you have the best possible chance of success in your degree. Our block teaching model means you will be able to plan your time around two days on campus each week, with the opportunity to spend more flexible time working on your individual and group projects. You will study at most two modules at a time, allowing you to focus in-depth on your chosen specialism and continually work on projects. What you will learn Our programme blends specialised knowledge with practical skills, covering the fundamentals of international business. Exploring diverse theories and concepts, the course unpacks the dynamics of international trade, examines how companies structure their overseas operations and evaluates the influence of foreign direct investment on host countries. In the taught stage, you will delve into advanced international business topics. You will analyse various international business strategies and compare business dynamics in developing economies to more economically developed countries. You will also explore factors influencing international business strategies, such as economic, management and policy issues, developing your ability to think strategically and deliver successful international business strategy. The programme also emphasises transferable skills like teamwork, leadership and communication, equipping you for a versatile career in international business. In the dissertation phase, you will undertake a research project on an international business topic of your choice, showcasing your ability to conduct independent research with a clear consideration of ethics, theory and methods. You will also benefit greatly from the location of your studies, with around one-third of all international students in the UK residing in London, Aston University London provides a dynamic, multicultural learning environment that enhances both personal and professional growth. Impact on people and finance Ben chose to study MSc International Business at Aston University because of its reputation as a leading business school in the middle of a vibrant city. Discover Ben's journey Course objectives Meets the needs of local, national and international candidates, enabling them to learn by the exchange of experience as well as formal academic study. Develops the lifelong learning and personal development skills that equip you to aspire to senior positions and enhance your employability. Enables you to reflect upon and develop your own position in relation to corporate responsibility, sustainability and ethics. Develops awareness of skills needed to work effectively in cross-cultural and interdisciplinary teams. Develops an understanding of the global business environment (including shifting competitive advantages) that influence business decisions and operations. Develops an ability to assess the effects of major economic, policy, social and technical trends and factors on businesses operating internationally. Develops the ability to assess the challenges and opportunities involved in the management and operations of multinational enterprises and other enterprises operating in international contexts. Develops inquiry, applied research and problem-solving skills to enable lifelong learning and professional development. Modules Modules and learning outcomes Taught stage Dissertation stage Learning outcomes Module Title Credits Enterprise Strategy (BMM108L) This module equips you with the analytical and practical skills to evaluate business opportunities and develop an understanding of what it means to be entrepreneurial in different contexts. You will explore entrepreneurial action and challenges in relation to commercial start-ups, social enterprises, family businesses, and corporate venturing. Entrepreneurial skills will be developed through in-class activities and case studies, supported by guest lectures from established entrepreneurs. The module encourages you to consider entrepreneurship as a viable alternative to traditional employment and to develop an entrepreneurial mindset. 15 International Marketing Management ( BMM115L) This module applies key marketing principles and concepts in an international context. You will develop your decision-making skills in the formulation and implementation of international marketing plans, while also building cultural sensitivity alongside your analytical and creative abilities. 15 Simulation for Management Decision Making (BBM115L) This module focuses on the modelling of business systems using computer simulation. It provides you with the knowledge and skills required to critically analyse complex problem situations and develop solutions through the use of simulation models. 15 Effective Management Consultancy (BBM104L) This module introduces you to different approaches for structuring consulting interventions and helps you develop an understanding of both effective and ineffective consulting practice. You will be better prepared to carry out successful consulting projects within organisations, whether as an external consultant or as a line manager addressing a one-off problem-solving task. Working in teams, you will apply team coaching principles to a self-selected challenge and use Soft Systems Methodology (SSM) to develop your consulting, analytical, and problem-solving skills. 15 International Economic Environment (BBM117L) This module equips you with the ability to evaluate and analyse real-world economic issues that impact global business operations. By critically examining the international macroeconomic environment, you will gain insight into how these factors influence strategic decision-making and market outcomes for firms operating in an international context. You will also learn to synthesise the various factors shaping market behaviour and draw international comparisons, considering their implications for business performance and consumer welfare. 15 International Business Strategy (BBM107L) This module explores the strategic challenges and opportunities that firms face in a globalised economy. You will examine key factors influencing international business decisions, including market entry strategies, competitive advantage across regions, and the impact of political, economic, and cultural environments. You will also study strategic alliances, mergers and acquisitions, and the management of multinational enterprises. By integrating theory with real-world case studies, you will develop the skills to formulate and implement international strategies, assess global risks, and adapt to the complexities of operating across borders in a dynamic business environment. 15 Innovation in the UK and Global Business Environment (BBM129L) This module provides you with an in-depth understanding of how digital technologies are reshaping industries, driving innovation, and transforming business models, alongside the practical skills and strategic insight required to lead and implement effective digital transformation initiatives in a dynamic business environment. 15 Aston Global Advantage (BSM100L) The AGA will allow you to reflect on the benefits of working in a multicultural environment, harnessing the skills associated with intercultural communication. This module focusses on personal and professional development harnessing collaboration from stakeholders from a range of communities and sectors. The module prepares you to be informed practitioners and where applicable they will be considering and evaluating research from a wide variety of sources throughout the module. This module does not require any research for which ethical approval will be necessary. 15 Total 120 *Availability of any optional modules will be subject to staff availability and a minimum number of students who express an interest in studying the optional modules. Read more » Module Title Credits Industry Research with an Entrepreneurial Mindset (AL4IRE) You will develop the skills to identify and address real-world challenges with creativity, critical thinking, and sustainability in mind. By applying research methods, design thinking, and entrepreneurial principles, you will generate industry-relevant proposals, analyse complex problems, and develop innovative solutions, equipping yourself to translate theory into actionable insights for business, community, and societal impact. Assessment is via an individual project proposal and an ethics quiz. 15 Independent Industry Project (AL4IIP) You will undertake an independent research project addressing a contemporary business issue relevant to your programme. By applying advanced research strategies, critical analysis, and project management skills under the guidance of a supervisor, you will evaluate complex problems, generate evidence-based insights, and communicate findings effectively, preparing yourself to make a meaningful impact in professional and organisational contexts. Assessment is via a final research report. 45 Total 60 *Availability of any optional modules will be subject to staff availability and a minimum number of students who express an interest in studying the optional modules. Read more » Programme outcomes On successful completion of both the taught and dissertation stage, you will be able to: Promote social responsibility, sustainability, accountability and ethical practice in business practice. Critically evaluate a range of complex situations, which may include finance, accounting, organisational behaviour, strategy, IT security, analytics, artificial intelligence, taking account of the inter-relationships of these topics and their interactions with other areas of business, industry and the external environment. Derive a range of transferable skills that are necessary for a successful career in business and enhance your employability. These may include: IT and computing skills, presentation and report writing skills, communication and team working (collaboration) skills, self-confidence, reflective practice, problem solving, leadership, decision making skills and ability to assimilate into multicultural and cross-cultural work teams. Derive the ability to undertake independent research with an applied business focus. Critically evaluate and construct knowledge of the changing global business landscape and developments and innovations in business practice. Critique and apply core theories in international business. Critically analyse and evaluate international business theories. Evaluate knowledge and derive skills required for assessing and developing international business strategies and operations. Critically analyse and evaluate the knowledge and skills required to understand and assess the international business environment. Read more » We may update our courses to reflect best practices and academic developments. If we do, we’ll let you know of any changes at the earliest opportunity by updating our course webpages. If you have already received an offer, we’ll write to you directly to let you know of the changes. Entry requirements One of the following: 2:2 (lower second-class honours) degree or equivalent Equivalent overseas degree recognised by Aston University (see international students tab below for more information) Additional requirements International students Extensive work experience You will also need to provide: A professional reference If you are a current student or recent graduate (within the last 2-3 years), we will ask for an academic reference If you are currently employed and not a recent graduate, we will ask for a professional reference An official academic transcript of your university grades to date A completed application form. Read more » Aston University is a diverse, close community and welcomes international students on many of our postgraduate programmes. Students from over 120 countries choose to study with us every year. Qualifications in your country For details of equivalent qualifications in your country, use our area pages below: Africa Americas Australia North East Asia Europe Middle East and North Africa South Asia South East Asia Western and Central Asia English language requirements Applicants whose first language is not English will be required to provide evidence of an English language qualification. Our requirements are: IELTS 6.5 overall, 3 bands with 6.0, and no more than one band with 5.5 or equivalent How to apply Find out more about applying Read more » We recognise the value of extensive professional experience. If you do not have the academic qualifications but have extensive and relevant professional experience and a proven ability to succeed, we would welcome your application. The information contained on this website details the typical entry requirements for this course for the most commonly offered qualifications. Applicants with alternative qualifications may wish to enquire with the relevant admissions teams prior to application whether or not their qualifications are deemed acceptable. For less commonly encountered qualifications this will be judged on a case-by-case basis in consultation with the academic admissions tutor. Read more » If you have any questions about the application process please get in touch with our team: Email: contact@london.aston.ac.uk Call: +44 (0)20 4536 4601 Read our guide to applying Fees and scholarships Course fees UK students (2026/27) Annual tuition fees: £14,000 International students (2026/27) Annual tuition fees: £25,500 More information on fees The United Kingdom government has confirmed that European Union (EU), other European Economic Area (EEA) and Swiss nationals commencing academic courses in England from August 2021 will no longer be charged the same tuition rates as UK students. Tuition fees for students are reviewed annually and may increase in subsequent years in line with inflation linked to the Retail Price Index (RPI) to take account of the University’s increased costs of delivering the Programme. Any such increase shall always be in accordance with the law. When undertaking a placement year, a placement year fee applies. Fees and funding Scholarships At Aston University London we are committed to supporting the most talented and hardworking students to achieve their potential by providing a range of scholarships to help lower tuition and living costs. To find out if you are eligible for scholarships and discounts, please contact us now . Assessment The programme will be assessed through a combination of class tests, individual and group coursework, projects, presentations and practical assessments. Our Postgraduate programmes at Aston University London have no exam assessments. Career prospects Being in London will open you to more opportunities for employment and future careers due to its extensive industry connections and vibrant professional network. The transferable skills that our business programmes provide mean that our graduates are successful in finding employment in a wide range of roles such as: Management consultant Strategy consultant Recruitment director Management trainee General manager Investment banker Research analyst Marketing manager Sales manager Our graduates have gone on to work at companies such as HSBC, IBM, Unilever, Vodafone, Hertz-Bosch. AI & Digital Innovation & Entrepreneurship Inclusive Leadership Environmental Sustainability Discover Power Skills Course description BSc (Hons) Global Business and Management (Top-up) Our BSc (Hons) Global Business and Management (Top-up) degree at Aston University will equip you with the skills, deep knowledge and practical understanding required by business managers of the 21st century. What we will provide First-class teaching in the UK’s second-largest city, delivered by a diverse array of staff who will inspire and excite you. Our inspirational teaching staff have established a reputation for developing innovative teaching methods, pioneering the use of gamification and creating games and simulations to make our students’ learning experience more rewarding. We are also an Adobe Creative Campus meaning you will have access to top-notch software licenses, including Adobe and Solidworks, commonly used in industry. What you will provide It is important you learn how to adapt a growth mindset to your studies – understanding that intelligence and success come from applying yourself, a willingness to learn and an ambition and drive to excel. You must be able to demonstrate critical thinking, have a passion for business and be excited about what contributes to the economy and society. What skills we teach You will develop management and leadership skills that are applicable to real life situations. Our graduates are problem solvers who have developed the essential skills needed to keep up to date with the ever-changing world of business. Career prospects As an Aston University Business and Management graduate, you will be equipped for a range of different career options. Our recent graduates have gone on to work across the public, private and third sectors for organisations including: Amazon, Channel 4, Jaguar Land Rover and J.P. Morgan. Hear from one of our graduates, Simba Rwambiwa, in this episode of the After Aston I... podcast: How will you learn Our teaching approach is both modern and innovative. At the beginning of your course, you'll be assigned a personal tutor for individual study guidance. Module tutors are readily available to answer questions, and all lectures are recorded for future reference. Our emphasis is on practical knowledge application, with guest lectures from prominent business leaders and mentoring programs offering unique insights. Our renowned Visiting Professors , top UK business figures, share their expertise and expectations from students and graduates. Complementing traditional teaching, our virtual learning environment provides electronic support materials. You'll have access to the University Library's extensive collection of over 25,000 books and electronic journals. University-wide services like the careers service, Jobshop, counselling and advice services, sports facilities, and Chaplaincy enhance your overall university experience and prepare you for your professional career. Aston University also offers an array of extracurricular activities, including clubs and societies like Aston Bright Futures, which works with leading businesses across various sectors. These activities not only enrich your student experience but also help you explore your specific interests and career pathways. Maastricht Case Competition Hear from Aston Business School students about their experience competing in the 13th International Case Competition at Maastricht University’s School of Business and Economics. Student experiences What you will learn The degree will provide you with an understanding of the various functions of management. We make extensive use of group working and presentations to prepare you for the reality of working life. You will study key business and management theory and create strategies for both national and international enterprises. You will evaluate leadership, reflect on behaviour and competencies, apply innovative problem-solving, and communicate business plans effectively. The programme ensures in-depth knowledge and equips you with practical skills and work experience for a successful transition into the professional world. Course objectives Equips you with the ability to apply a breadth of business concepts. Develops your analytical skills and reasoning, undertaking complex analysis, and making evidence-informed decisions. Facilitates the acquisition of transferable intellectual and analytical skills within a management context. Enables the development of responsible managers. Solve complex problems and generate effective solutions. Communicate information and ideas effectively and purposefully. Engage with current trends, opportunities and challenges in business management. Articulate strategic thinking within a management context. Appreciate ethical challenges to inform decision making. We’ll make sure to let you know of any changes to modules at the earliest opportunity by updating our course webpages. We’ll do our best to provide as much optional choice as we can, but timetabling constraints may mean it isn’t possible to take some module combinations. Explore our scholarships Assessment The programme will be assessed through a combination of written and oral examinations, class tests, individual and group coursework, projects, presentations and practical assessments. Career prospects Our BSc (Hons) Global Business and Management programme will prepare you for a range of careers across the public, private and third sectors. Our graduates are among the highest paid in the country, earning on average £33,200 three years after graduating, and £42,000 five years after graduating (Longitudinal Education Outcomes, 2025). The transferable skills that our business and management programmes provide mean that our graduates are successful in finding employment in a wide range of roles such as: Market intelligence analyst Legal project manager Business development manager Marketing specialist Head of resources Digital project manager Senior manager Assistant manager Commercial analyst Strategy specialist Account manager Operations manager Area manager Teacher Our graduates have gone on to work at companies such as: Atos, PwC, DHL, Santander, National Grid, Nissan, KPMG, BMW Group UK, Lidl GB, Network Rail, Amazon, Rolls Royce, FDM Group, Deloitte and Jaguar Land Rover. Entrepreneurial success Founder of Protein Package, George Greenhill says his decision to study at Aston University was because of the excellent reputation of Aston Business School. Discover George's journey Aston Business School graduates achieve some amazing things - whether it's setting up their own businesses, landing competitive graduate schemes, or making real differences within their communities. Hear from our graduates Be part of our community Once you have joined us at Aston University, you’ll always be part of our community, even beyond graduation. Alumni services Frequently asked questions What kind of jobs does a degree in Global Business and Management lead to? You will gain strategic management skills and a broad knowledge of business. Our graduates are in high demand and go into a wide range of roles in the private, public and not-for-profit sectors. Recent roles have included: Market intelligence analyst Legal project manager Business development manager Marketing specialist Head of resources Digital project manager Senior manager Assistant manager Commercial analyst Strategy specialist Account manager Operations manager Area manager Teacher Recent companies have included: Atos PwC DHL Santander National Grid Nissan KPMG BMW Group UK Lidl GB Network Rail Amazon Rolls Royce FDM Group Deloitte Jaguar Land Rover Why should international students choose Aston University? Aston University is a diverse, close community and welcomes international students on many of our undergraduate programmes. Students from over 120 different countries chose to study with us every year and Aston is not only a great place to study, based in the centre of Birmingham, it’s also a great place to live. Aston’s professional work placements can improve your chance of securing a graduate job. Placements give you experience, confidence and opportunities and as an Aston student, you’ll be better prepared for your future career. Choosing to start your Aston journey with our foundation programme in business will help you develop specialist knowledge to ensure that you are fully prepared to study your chosen undergraduate course. By being based in London you will be part of a vibrant cosmopolitan city and community, renowned for its diverse skills, cultures, beliefs, and wealth of knowledge. What we will provide First-class teaching, in the UK's capital city, delivered by a diverse array of staff who will inspire and excite you. There are practical activities, including simulation exercises, reflective case studies, collaborative group work, thought-provoking class discussions as well as inspiring lectures and tutorials. We are also an Adobe Creative Campus meaning you will have access to top-notch software licenses, including Adobe and Solidworks, commonly used in industry. Aston University London is a gateway to a multitude of industry connections and networking opportunities, set against the backdrop of a city known for its international diversity and cultural richness. What you will provide It is important you learn how to adapt a growth mindset to your studies – understanding that intelligence and success come from applying yourself, a willingness to learn and an ambition and drive to excel. You must be able to demonstrate critical thinking, have a passion for business and be excited about what contributes to the economy and society. What skills we teach You will develop management and leadership skills that are applicable to real life situations. Our graduates are problem solvers who have developed the essential skills needed to keep up to date with the ever-changing world of business. Career prospects As an Aston University Global Business and Management graduate, you will be equipped for a range of different career options. Our recent graduates have gone on to work across the public, private and third sectors for organisations including: Amazon, Channel 4, Jaguar Land Rover and J.P. Morgan. By studying in London you will have prime location to open up numerous employment and career opportunities, thanks to the city's extensive industry connections and vibrant professional network. How you will learn You will be taught by a combination of academic and industry experts. Our block teaching model means you will be able to plan your time around two days on campus each week, with the opportunity to spend more flexible time working on your individual and group projects. What you will learn The degree will provide you with an understanding of the various functions of management. We make extensive use of group working and presentations to prepare you for the reality of working life. You will study key business and management theory and create strategies for both national and international enterprises. You will evaluate leadership, reflect on behaviour and competencies, apply innovative problem-solving, and communicate business plans effectively. The programme ensures in-depth knowledge and equips you with practical skills and work experience for a successful transition into the professional world. You will also benefit greatly from the location of your studies, with around one-third of all international students in the UK residing in London, Aston University London provides a dynamic, multicultural learning environment that enhances both personal and professional growth. Course objectives Equips you with the ability to apply a breadth of business concepts. Develops your analytical skills and reasoning, undertaking complex analysis, and making evidence-informed decisions. Facilitates the acquisition of transferable intellectual and analytical skills within a management context. Enables the development of responsible managers. Modules Modules and learning outcomes Taught stage Learning outcomes Module Title Credits Global Working The aim of this module is to develop your cultural awareness and intercultural business competence through gaining the knowledge, skills, and mind-set appropriate for operating in the global working environment. You will study key theories in cultural variation and cross-cultural working, and will apply these to the complex working styles and communication challenges faced by international organisations, their employees and those responsible for managing global workforces. 15 Strategic Management In this module you will develop a critical understanding of how organisations formulate and implement effective strategic decisions to achieve a sustainable competitive advantage. The module is structured to have a highly practical focus, however wherever relevant corporate connections have been established and continue to be developed. 15 Theories and Practice of Leadership This module aims to provide you with an evidence-based management lens to leadership. You will learn to use theory and research to consider what effective leadership means, and the wider issues surrounding leadership practice. The module will examine effective leadership from various perspectives. Efforts will also be made to ascertain what effective leader behaviours look like, in addition to understanding the ethical issues surrounding leadership. Both a historical and a contemporary approach to leadership will be adopted throughout the module. 15 Effective Management Consultancy 1 The module will introduce you to the management consultancy industry, its emergence and history. It will then go on to explore the industry and its structure, size and growth, the key areas, firms and activities. It will introduce you to the nature of management consultancy and what it means. The module will review the sources of disruption in the management consultancy industry and the main areas of activity in the industry including strategy, financial advisory, operations, information technology and technology and human resources. 15 Global Marketing This module is designed to develop a comprehensive understanding of the special requirements for successfully conducting international marketing activities, as many businesses today have expanded and are continuing to expand in the global arena. Their success largely depends on their ability to apply business concepts in foreign markets, but also have to respond and adapt to global challenges (e.g. pandemics). This module aims to develop your skills in holistically applying marketing principles to an international setting. During the module, it is hoped that you will develop a cultural sensitivity in addition to enhancing your analytical and creative skills. 15 Sustainable Operations Management The module aims to develop critical and analytical thinking to assess sustainable operations management alongside the provision of a range of robust theories, frameworks, and tools to enhance the sustainability performance of organisations. 15 Effective Management Consultancy 2 This module aims to give you an appreciation of different types of consulting approaches - both `hard' and `soft' - that are used by contemporary consulting firms. It will give you an understanding in more detail of one approach i.e. Soft Systems Methodology and develop useful consulting skills through application on a team based exercise. 15 Business Ethics Business ethics embodies a complex web of human relationships; in a world where many business ventures extend across geographical and cultural barriers, this module considers whether there is an ‘international common core’ in business ethics. It also addresses issues in relations to cultural values and cultural relativism. The primary focus of this module is ethics, social responsibility and sustainability. The overall aim of this module is to provide you with the critical knowledge and practical skills to identify and navigate, ethical issues across geographical and cultural borders. 15 Total 120 Read more » Programme outcomes On successful completion of both the taught and dissertation stage, you will be able to: Critically appraise theoretical approaches and business models. Solve complex problems and generate effective solutions. Communicate information and ideas effectively and purposefully. Engage with current trends, opportunities and challenges in business management. Articulate strategic thinking within a management context. Appreciate ethical challenges to inform decision making. If you have already received an offer, we’ll write to you directly to let you know of the changes. AI & Digital Innovation & Entrepreneurship Inclusive Leadership Environmental Sustainability Discover Power Skills Course description BSc (Hons) Global Business and Management (Top-up) (London) Our BSc (Hons) Global Business and Management (Top-up) degree at Aston University will equip you with the skills, deep knowledge and practical understanding required by business managers of the 21st century. By being based in London you will be part of a vibrant cosmopolitan city and community, renowned for its diverse skills, cultures, beliefs, and wealth of knowledge. What we will provide First-class teaching, in the UK's capital city, delivered by a diverse array of staff who will inspire and excite you. There are practical activities, including simulation exercises, reflective case studies, collaborative group work, thought-provoking class discussions as well as inspiring lectures and tutorials. We are also an Adobe Creative Campus meaning you will have access to top-notch software licenses, including Adobe and Solidworks, commonly used in industry. Aston University London is a gateway to a multitude of industry connections and networking opportunities, set against the backdrop of a city known for its international diversity and cultural richness. What you will provide It is important you learn how to adapt a growth mindset to your studies – understanding that intelligence and success come from applying yourself, a willingness to learn and an ambition and drive to excel. You must be able to demonstrate critical thinking, have a passion for business and be excited about what contributes to the economy and society. What skills we teach You will develop management and leadership skills that are applicable to real life situations. Our graduates are problem solvers who have developed the essential skills needed to keep up to date with the ever-changing world of business. Career prospects As an Aston University Global Business and Management graduate, you will be equipped for a range of different career options. Our recent graduates have gone on to work across the public, private and third sectors for organisations including: Amazon, Channel 4, Jaguar Land Rover and J.P. Morgan. By studying in London you will have prime location to open up numerous employment and career opportunities, thanks to the city's extensive industry connections and vibrant professional network. How you will learn You will be taught by a combination of academic and industry experts. Our block teaching model means you will be able to plan your time around two days on campus each week, with the opportunity to spend more flexible time working on your individual and group projects. What you will learn The degree will provide you with an understanding of the various functions of management. We make extensive use of group working and presentations to prepare you for the reality of working life. You will study key business and management theory and create strategies for both national and international enterprises. You will evaluate leadership, reflect on behaviour and competencies, apply innovative problem-solving, and communicate business plans effectively. The programme ensures in-depth knowledge and equips you with practical skills and work experience for a successful transition into the professional world. You will also benefit greatly from the location of your studies, with around one-third of all international students in the UK residing in London, Aston University London provides a dynamic, multicultural learning environment that enhances both personal and professional growth. Course objectives Equips you with the ability to apply a breadth of business concepts. Develops your analytical skills and reasoning, undertaking complex analysis, and making evidence-informed decisions. Facilitates the acquisition of transferable intellectual and analytical skills within a management context. Enables the development of responsible managers. Modules Modules and learning outcomes Taught stage Learning outcomes Module Title Credits Global Working The aim of this module is to develop your cultural awareness and intercultural business competence through gaining the knowledge, skills, and mind-set appropriate for operating in the global working environment. You will study key theories in cultural variation and cross-cultural working, and will apply these to the complex working styles and communication challenges faced by international organisations, their employees and those responsible for managing global workforces. 15 Strategic Management In this module you will develop a critical understanding of how organisations formulate and implement effective strategic decisions to achieve a sustainable competitive advantage. The module is structured to have a highly practical focus, however wherever relevant corporate connections have been established and continue to be developed. 15 Theories and Practice of Leadership This module aims to provide you with an evidence-based management lens to leadership. You will learn to use theory and research to consider what effective leadership means, and the wider issues surrounding leadership practice. The module will examine effective leadership from various perspectives. Efforts will also be made to ascertain what effective leader behaviours look like, in addition to understanding the ethical issues surrounding leadership. Both a historical and a contemporary approach to leadership will be adopted throughout the module. 15 Effective Management Consultancy 1 The module will introduce you to the management consultancy industry, its emergence and history. It will then go on to explore the industry and its structure, size and growth, the key areas, firms and activities. It will introduce you to the nature of management consultancy and what it means. The module will review the sources of disruption in the management consultancy industry and the main areas of activity in the industry including strategy, financial advisory, operations, information technology and technology and human resources. 15 Global Marketing This module is designed to develop a comprehensive understanding of the special requirements for successfully conducting international marketing activities, as many businesses today have expanded and are continuing to expand in the global arena. Their success largely depends on their ability to apply business concepts in foreign markets, but also have to respond and adapt to global challenges (e.g. pandemics). This module aims to develop your skills in holistically applying marketing principles to an international setting. During the module, it is hoped that you will develop a cultural sensitivity in addition to enhancing your analytical and creative skills. 15 Sustainable Operations Management The module aims to develop critical and analytical thinking to assess sustainable operations management alongside the provision of a range of robust theories, frameworks, and tools to enhance the sustainability performance of organisations. 15 Effective Management Consultancy 2 This module aims to give you an appreciation of different types of consulting approaches - both `hard' and `soft' - that are used by contemporary consulting firms. It will give you an understanding in more detail of one approach i.e. Soft Systems Methodology and develop useful consulting skills through application on a team based exercise. 15 Business Ethics Business ethics embodies a complex web of human relationships; in a world where many business ventures extend across geographical and cultural barriers, this module considers whether there is an ‘international common core’ in business ethics. It also addresses issues in relations to cultural values and cultural relativism. The primary focus of this module is ethics, social responsibility and sustainability. The overall aim of this module is to provide you with the critical knowledge and practical skills to identify and navigate, ethical issues across geographical and cultural borders. 15 Total 120 Read more » Programme outcomes On successful completion of both the taught and dissertation stage, you will be able to: Critically appraise theoretical approaches and business models. Solve complex problems and generate effective solutions. Communicate information and ideas effectively and purposefully. Engage with current trends, opportunities and challenges in business management. Articulate strategic thinking within a management context. Appreciate ethical challenges to inform decision making. Read more » We may update our courses to reflect best practices and academic developments. If we do, we’ll let you know of any changes at the earliest opportunity by updating our course webpages. If you have already received an offer, we’ll write to you directly to let you know of the changes. AI & Digital Innovation & Entrepreneurship Inclusive Leadership Environmental Sustainability Discover Power Skills Course description BSc (Hons) Global Business and Management (Top-up) (London) Our BSc (Hons) Global Business and Management (Top-up) degree at Aston University will equip you with the skills, deep knowledge and practical understanding required by business managers of the 21st century. By being based in London you will be part of a vibrant cosmopolitan city and community, renowned for its diverse skills, cultures, beliefs, and wealth of knowledge. What we will provide First-class teaching, in the UK's capital city, delivered by a diverse array of staff who will inspire and excite you. There are practical activities, including simulation exercises, reflective case studies, collaborative group work, thought-provoking class discussions as well as inspiring lectures and tutorials. We are also an Adobe Creative Campus meaning you will have access to top-notch software licenses, including Adobe and Solidworks, commonly used in industry. Aston University London is a gateway to a multitude of industry connections and networking opportunities, set against the backdrop of a city known for its international diversity and cultural richness. What you will provide It is important you learn how to adapt a growth mindset to your studies – understanding that intelligence and success come from applying yourself, a willingness to learn and an ambition and drive to excel. You must be able to demonstrate critical thinking, have a passion for business and be excited about what contributes to the economy and society. What skills we teach You will develop management and leadership skills that are applicable to real life situations. Our graduates are problem solvers who have developed the essential skills needed to keep up to date with the ever-changing world of business. Career prospects As an Aston University Global Business and Management graduate, you will be equipped for a range of different career options. Our recent graduates have gone on to work across the public, private and third sectors for organisations including: Amazon, Channel 4, Jaguar Land Rover and J.P. Morgan. By studying in London you will have prime location to open up numerous employment and career opportunities, thanks to the city's extensive industry connections and vibrant professional network. How you will learn You will be taught by a combination of academic and industry experts. Our block teaching model means you will be able to plan your time around two days on campus each week, with the opportunity to spend more flexible time working on your individual and group projects. What you will learn The degree will provide you with an understanding of the various functions of management. We make extensive use of group working and presentations to prepare you for the reality of working life. You will study key business and management theory and create strategies for both national and international enterprises. You will evaluate leadership, reflect on behaviour and competencies, apply innovative problem-solving, and communicate business plans effectively. The programme ensures in-depth knowledge and equips you with practical skills and work experience for a successful transition into the professional world. You will also benefit greatly from the location of your studies, with around one-third of all international students in the UK residing in London, Aston University London provides a dynamic, multicultural learning environment that enhances both personal and professional growth. Course objectives Equips you with the ability to apply a breadth of business concepts. Develops your analytical skills and reasoning, undertaking complex analysis, and making evidence-informed decisions. Facilitates the acquisition of transferable intellectual and analytical skills within a management context. Enables the development of responsible managers. Modules Modules and learning outcomes Taught stage Learning outcomes Module Title Credits Global Working The aim of this module is to develop your cultural awareness and intercultural business competence through gaining the knowledge, skills, and mind-set appropriate for operating in the global working environment. You will study key theories in cultural variation and cross-cultural working, and will apply these to the complex working styles and communication challenges faced by international organisations, their employees and those responsible for managing global workforces. 15 Strategic Management In this module you will develop a critical understanding of how organisations formulate and implement effective strategic decisions to achieve a sustainable competitive advantage. The module is structured to have a highly practical focus, however wherever relevant corporate connections have been established and continue to be developed. 15 Theories and Practice of Leadership This module aims to provide you with an evidence-based management lens to leadership. You will learn to use theory and research to consider what effective leadership means, and the wider issues surrounding leadership practice. The module will examine effective leadership from various perspectives. Efforts will also be made to ascertain what effective leader behaviours look like, in addition to understanding the ethical issues surrounding leadership. Both a historical and a contemporary approach to leadership will be adopted throughout the module. 15 Effective Management Consultancy 1 The module will introduce you to the management consultancy industry, its emergence and history. It will then go on to explore the industry and its structure, size and growth, the key areas, firms and activities. It will introduce you to the nature of management consultancy and what it means. The module will review the sources of disruption in the management consultancy industry and the main areas of activity in the industry including strategy, financial advisory, operations, information technology and technology and human resources. 15 Global Marketing This module is designed to develop a comprehensive understanding of the special requirements for successfully conducting international marketing activities, as many businesses today have expanded and are continuing to expand in the global arena. Their success largely depends on their ability to apply business concepts in foreign markets, but also have to respond and adapt to global challenges (e.g. pandemics). This module aims to develop your skills in holistically applying marketing principles to an international setting. During the module, it is hoped that you will develop a cultural sensitivity in addition to enhancing your analytical and creative skills. 15 Sustainable Operations Management The module aims to develop critical and analytical thinking to assess sustainable operations management alongside the provision of a range of robust theories, frameworks, and tools to enhance the sustainability performance of organisations. 15 Effective Management Consultancy 2 This module aims to give you an appreciation of different types of consulting approaches - both `hard' and `soft' - that are used by contemporary consulting firms. It will give you an understanding in more detail of one approach i.e. Soft Systems Methodology and develop useful consulting skills through application on a team based exercise. 15 Business Ethics Business ethics embodies a complex web of human relationships; in a world where many business ventures extend across geographical and cultural barriers, this module considers whether there is an ‘international common core’ in business ethics. It also addresses issues in relations to cultural values and cultural relativism. The primary focus of this module is ethics, social responsibility and sustainability. The overall aim of this module is to provide you with the critical knowledge and practical skills to identify and navigate, ethical issues across geographical and cultural borders. 15 Total 120 Read more » Programme outcomes On successful completion of both the taught and dissertation stage, you will be able to: Critically appraise theoretical approaches and business models. Solve complex problems and generate effective solutions. Communicate information and ideas effectively and purposefully. Engage with current trends, opportunities and challenges in business management. Articulate strategic thinking within a management context. Appreciate ethical challenges to inform decision making. Any - True False Apply filters Clear all Home Courses Haematology and Transfusion Science Standalone module Haematology and Transfusion Science Standalone module Ready to enhance your expertise in haematology and transfusion science, exploring the biology of blood disorders and interpreting clinical data to advance your biomedical science career? Location: Online via distance learning (plus some face-to-face sessions at Aston University, Birmingham) Applications are now closed Course type Professional short courses/CPD Entry requirements See our entry requirements Duration One year Start date September 2026 Module overview Entry requirements Fees Delivery and assessment Applications are now closed Module overview Studied via blended learning (online and in-person sessions), this standalone module offers a detailed overview of haematology and transfusion science, emphasising the pathophysiology of blood disorders and clinical data interpretation. Ideal for topping up your degree to become a registered Biomedical Scientist or advancing your professional development, it enhances your understanding of diagnosing and managing blood disorders. The module covers the structure, function and production of blood cells; normal haemostasis; and the diagnosis and investigation of anaemias, haematological malignancies and bleeding and thrombotic disorders. It also includes haematological techniques for disease screening and monitoring. In transfusion science, it addresses red cell antigens, immune-mediated blood cell destruction and the preparation, storage and selection of blood components, including potential adverse effects. This is a level 5 module (equivalent level of study to a foundation degree or Diploma of Higher Education) worth 10 credits . Module tutor(s): Dr Ross Pallett ; Dr Amreen Bashir Why Haematology and Transfusion Science at Aston University? Top-up your degree Top-up your existing degree to become a registered biomedical scientist Professionally accredited This module is associated with an IBMS-accredited programme Research active staff Learn from passionate research-active academics in specialist areas of haematology and transfusion science Previous Next Objectives and outcomes Enables you to understand the biology underlying the pathophysiology of haematological disorders. Enables you to interpret clinical data related to haematological conditions as part of your continuing professional development. On successful completion of this module you will be able to: Describe and evaluate the normal functioning of haematological systems. Discuss and analyse the causes, diagnosis, prognosis and treatment of haematological disorders. Discuss and evaluate the preparation, storage and uses of blood products, and the risks associated with their use. Critically appraise the application of laboratory tests and demonstrate knowledge of the laboratory equipment, routine processes and methodologies used to test patient samples in clinical laboratories. Speak to our Admissions Team If you have any questions about the application process please get in touch with our postgraduate admissions team: Email: professionalcpd@aston.ac.uk Read our guide to applying Entry requirements You must have a non-accredited undergraduate degree in Biomedical Sciences or an undergraduate degree in a related field (such as biology or biochemistry). Top-up CPD International students Taking this module in order to 'top-up' your existing degree for IBMS registration: Prior to registering for a top-up module (or modules) you need to contact the Institute of Biomedical Science . They will assess your degree in order to confirm that it is eligible for 'top-up' and to determine the additional subject areas in which you need further qualifications. We recommend you contact the IBMS by June in the year of application to ensure that you have confirmation of your module requirements in time to register for your module(s) with Aston University. Degrees not eligible for top-up: If your degree is not eligible for top up but you still wish to become a registered Biomedical Scientist, we recommend that you apply to take our accredited BSc (Hons) Biomedical Science undergraduate degree. Read more » Undertaking this module for professional development: No additional requirements apply. Read more » We welcome applications from international students who are already in the UK with a valid visa. Unfortunately we are not able to accept applications from international students who wish to come to the UK solely to take this course. We are also not able to accept international students to take the distance learning route. You will be asked to provide a scanned copy of your UK visa, and of your passport when you submit the online registration form so that we can check you are eligible to take the top up modules. Students taking this course by distance learning must be based in the UK. Read more » Biomedical modules suite Our full list of available modules in this suite of courses includes: Cell Biology Cellular Pathology Clinical Biochemistry Human Anatomy and Physiology Haematology and Transfusion Science Immunology Molecular Biology and Genetics Medical Microbiology Fees UK students (2026/27) £850 per 10 credits More information on fees The United Kingdom government has confirmed that European Union (EU), other European Economic Area (EEA) and Swiss nationals commencing academic courses in England from August 2021 will no longer be charged the same tuition rates as UK students. Tuition fees for students are reviewed annually and may increase in subsequent years in line with inflation linked to the Retail Price Index (RPI) to take account of the University’s increased costs of delivering the Programme. Any such increase shall always be in accordance with the law. When undertaking a placement year, a placement year fee applies. More information on fees Delivery and assessment This course is delivered via blended learning. You must attend an online induction session in week zero (mid-September), at which we will show you how to access your university record and Blackboard (your Virtual Learning Environment). All course material, including recorded lectures, self-assessment quizzes, timetables and some directed reading will be available on Blackboard online; coursework submission and feedback are also mainly via this route. Blackboard allows you to access a comprehensive range of study materials, scientific journals, e-journals, databases and much more. Blended learning: the study can be spread out over the term and a week-by-week study guide is available. Recorded lectures are made available after they are delivered to attendance students as detailed above. Practical experience: a single three-hour on-campus practical is associated with this module; attendance is compulsory unless you can provide evidence of equivalent learning in the workplace. Assessment Assessments must be in person on campus plus there will be an on campus exam in April 2027. Hello, what would you like to ask us? Hello! We are a team of current Aston University students from various parts of the world, studying a wide range of postgraduate subjects. Feel free to ask us anything about studying at Aston University. Ask us anything now Career prospects Our CPD courses offer you the opportunity to enhance your knowledge and skills in order to develop your career. In addition, our ethos is to equip you to make a real difference in your field. These modules will allow you to obtain the academic competences that are required to apply to the Health Professions Council for Registration as a Biomedical Scientist. Be part of our community Once you have joined us at Aston University, you’ll always be part of our community, even beyond graduation. Location: Online via distance learning Applications are now closed Course type Professional short courses/CPD Entry requirements See our entry requirements Duration Four months Start date October 2026 Module overview Entry requirements Fees Delivery and assessment Applications are now closed Module overview Please note the application deadline for this course is Monday 31 August 2026. Studied via distance learning, this standalone module introduces health psychology, focusing on how behavioral and psychological factors affect health. You will learn about common mental health and perceptual conditions in clinical practice, along with communication strategies for managing patients with additional psychological needs. The indicative content of the module includes an overview of health psychology and its relevance in patient care. You will examine conditions such as autism, depression, anxiety and obsessive-compulsive disorder, as well as perceptual psychological deficits like spatial neglect, synaesthesia and Charles-Bonnet syndrome. Emphasis is placed on developing appropriate bedside manners, understanding when alternative communication approaches are necessary, and learning how to signpost patients to services while following safeguarding practices. This is a level 7 module (equivalent level of study to a postgraduate or masters degree) worth 20 credits . Module tutor(s): Dr Samantha Strong Why Health and Patient Psychology at Aston University? Excellent prospects Ranked 2nd in the UK for ‘graduate prospects – on track’ (Optometry, Ophthalmics and Orthoptics; Complete University Guide, 2025) Specialist facilities Access cutting-edge equipment in our ophthalmic simulation suite Research active staff Learn from passionate research-active academics in specialist areas of optometry, ophthalmics and orthoptics Previous Next Objectives and outcomes Introduces you to health psychology by exploring how behavioral and psychological factors, such as thoughts and beliefs, influence health. Provides knowledge of mental health and perceptual psychological conditions that may appear in clinical settings. Teaches communication strategies for managing patients with additional psychological needs and delivering interventions to promote healthy habits. On successful completion of this module you will be able to: Explain what health psychology is and discuss the role that behavioural and psychological factors play in a person's overall health. Demonstrate knowledge of common mental health problems and recognise and assist patients affected by these conditions in clinical practice. Use appropriate methods of communication with patients who have additional psychological needs or whose health may be impacted by behavioural or psychological factors. Speak to our Admissions Team If you have any questions about the application process please get in touch with our postgraduate admissions team: Email: professionalcpd@aston.ac.uk Read our guide to applying Entry requirements You should be a registered optometrist with the UK General Optical Council (GOC) or another eye care professional. Fees UK students (2026/27) £715 per 10 credits (£1,430 for full module) More information on fees The United Kingdom government has confirmed that European Union (EU), other European Economic Area (EEA) and Swiss nationals commencing academic courses in England from August 2021 will no longer be charged the same tuition rates as UK students. Tuition fees for students are reviewed annually and may increase in subsequent years in line with inflation linked to the Retail Price Index (RPI) to take account of the University’s increased costs of delivering the Programme. Any such increase shall always be in accordance with the law. When undertaking a placement year, a placement year fee applies. More information on fees Delivery and assessment This course is delivered via distance learning. You will access learning materials for general study, revision and assessment via our virtual learning environment, Blackboard. This platform allows you to access a comprehensive range of study materials, scientific journals, e-journals, databases and much more. Method of delivery Learning hours Small group activity 4 hours Independent activity 166 hours Structured activity 20 hours Formative assessment activity 10 hours Total 200 hours Assessment The assessment for this standalone module comprises a multiple-choice question element and a portfolio with two distinct components: Multiple choice questions (10%): An untimed, open-book test with ten multiple choice questions per lecture, hosted on Blackboard. Portfolio (90%): A 2,000-word assignment involving a case study and discussion of evidence-based management strategies, and a 1,000-word self-reflection essay on how the module will transform your approach to practice. Any - True False Apply filters Clear all Home Courses Health Psychology MSc Health Psychology MSc Study our British Psychological Society (BPS) accredited Health Psychology MSc and discover more about how biology, psychology, behaviour, and social factors influence health and illness. Location: Aston University, Birmingham Apply now Register your interest Course type Full-time Entry requirements UK 2:2 honours Psychology degree (with BPS accreditation) or international equivalent Duration One year Start date September 2027 Course overview Course description Facilities Course objectives Modules Entry requirements Fees and scholarships Apply now Register your interest GUARANTEED INTERNSHIPS WITH EVERY MASTER'S DEGREE Find out more Course overview Health psychology explores how behaviour influences health and illness, and how we support people living with long-term conditions. Health psychologists apply psychological knowledge to understand health behaviours and design interventions that encourage positive change. They play a crucial role in areas such as: Supporting patients’ emotional and psychological well-being. Helping healthcare professionals build effective communication and relationships with patients. Working with health and social care organisations to promote well-being and reduce health inequalities. From public health and health inequalities to the psychobiology of illness and chronic conditions, Aston’s BPS-accredited Health Psychology MSc gives you a deep grounding in the theories and applications of the field - preparing you for a rewarding career in health psychology and beyond. "The staff are very supportive and are always happy to help. We were taught a range of transferrable skills for roles in the academic field as well as clinical. The lectures were engaging and incorporated real-life examples that we were able to understand how skills and theory are used in practice." Magda Skubera Health Psychology MSc Supply Teacher of Psychology at King Edward VI College Why Health Psychology at Aston University? Internationally recognised research 100% of our health and life sciences research environment has been ranked as being at least internationally excellent, with 50% being world-leading Research-active academics Study alongside active research staff from a broad range of specialist psychology areas Professional accreditation Gain a degree accredited by the British Psychological Society (BPS) Previous Next Why I chose to study Health Psychology MSc at Aston University Hear from Health Psychology alumni, Deepa Lad about why she chose Aston University to continue her postgraduate psychology studies. Course description Health Psychology MSc Our Health Psychology MSc at Aston will equip you with the skills, insights, and confidence required to understand health behaviours and to develop psychological interventions to support behaviour change. What we will provide First-class teaching in the UK's second-largest city, delivered by a diverse array of staff who will inspire and excite you, fantastic facilities that will bring your course to life through hands-on, practical experience and years of close industry collaboration that is harnessed to provide you with learning based on real-world needs. What you will provide It is important you learn how to adapt a growth mindset to your studies - understanding that intelligence and success come from applying yourself. You must be able to demonstrate critical thinking and have ambition and drive to excel. What skills we teach As a Health Psychology student, you will learn the skills to work as a competent health psychologist with an understanding of the theory underpinning health psychology. You’ll build your knowledge of advanced research methodology, and the analysis of qualitative and quantitative data to carry out independent work and conduct your final research project in a relevant specialist topic of your choosing. Career prospects Many of our graduates go on to complete further training (Stage 2) to become a Chartered Psychologist with the British Psychological Society and a Health Psychologist registered with the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC). Many have also taken up roles within the NHS to run interventions to improve patients' health and manage their illness or to evaluate and re-design existing health services. How you will learn Our teaching style is modern and innovative, with a hands-on approach that bridges the gap between theory and practice. This enables you to apply your skills as you progress through your course, marrying your learning with practical examples, all designed to prepare you for the world of work. You will engage in a variety of teaching and learning methods, including lectures, practical sessions, tutorials, seminars, and a research project. What you will learn By studying Health Psychology MSc at Aston, you will gain an in-depth understanding of the theory underpinning health psychology. You’ll build your knowledge of advanced research methodology, including the analysis of qualitative and quantitative data to carry out your own research project in a specialist topic under expert supervision. From health inequalities and public health to psychobiology of illness and long term conditions, our full-time, on-campus Health Psychology MSc will provide you with an in-depth understanding of the theories and methods used in underpinning health psychology. This course has been designed to give you an ideal base for a rewarding career in health psychology and related fields. MSc Health Psychology Taster Lecture What Makes The Public Support Or Oppose Health Policies? Facilities As a Health Psychology MSc student, you’ll have access to specialist facilities designed to give you practical, hands-on experience. You’ll learn in an environment that mirrors real-world practice, guided by expert academics and industry professionals. Our facilities include: Dedicated psychology laboratories Feeding laboratory Observation suite with covert audio-visual recording Experiment and testing rooms Large labs for focus groups and audience-based studies Neurophysiological equipment, including electroencephalography (EEG) Eye-tracking, face and emotion recognition technology Electrodermal recording systems You’ll also benefit from close links with the Aston Institute of Health and Neurodevelopment, with access to its on-campus clinics and research facilities - enhancing both your learning and research opportunities. Course objectives Provides you with the opportunities to realise your academic potential through a range of learning experiences. Encourages you, through a practical approach, to have a passion for Psychology and an enthusiasm for learning. To deliver a programme of a standard which satisfies the accreditation requirements of the British Psychological Society. To provide you with an intellectually rigorous and contemporary education in and understanding of the theory, practice, and methods of psychology, which will help you to identify and achieve your personal, academic, and professional goals and aspirations in the field of psychology. To develop students’ understanding of an advanced research methodology and analysis of qualitative and quantitative data to enable them to carry out independent work of publishable standard. To produce graduates with skills and abilities in research and enquiry, information literacy, personal and intellectual autonomy, and ethical, social and professional understanding in order to tackle effectively the contemporary issues facing people, organisations, and society. Produce graduates who will be able to contribute to a broad spectrum of career opportunities spanning academic, commercial, clinical practice, healthcare, and more. Modules Modules and learning outcomes Taught stage Dissertation Stage Taught stage modules In your taught stage, you will study the following core module: Module Title Credits Advanced Research Methods: This module will help you to develop knowledge and skills in designing, conducting, and appraising research in applied health settings. 30 Health Behaviours and Interventions: This module will help you to understand how health psychology theories can explain and predict health-related behaviours, and how to design, implement, and evaluate health behaviour change interventions. 30 Health Inequalities and Public Health: This module will help you understand the ways in which individual psychological variables interact with social, cultural, environmental and policy variables to affect health and health inequalities. 30 Psychobiology of Illness and Long-term conditions: This module will help you to develop a critical understanding of the interrelationships between psychological, behavioural and biological processes and their effects on ill health, and the diagnosis and management of long-term conditions. 30 Total 120 Read more » Dissertation stage modules In your dissertation stage, you will study the following core module: Module Title Credits Research Project: This module will help you to undertake a supervised, independent, empirical research project where you will integrate and apply the skills you have acquired during the programme. 60 Total 60 Read more » We may update our courses to reflect best practices and academic developments. If we do, we’ll let you know of any changes at the earliest opportunity by updating our course webpages. If you have already received an offer, we’ll write to you directly to let you know of the changes. Gain the advantage The Aston Global Advantage (AGA) is fully embedded into all postgraduate Health & Life Sciences programmes (of 180 credits), meaning you develop professional skills, teamwork abilities and real‑world experience as an integral part of your course. Because each programme tailors the AGA to its discipline, you learn through authentic activities relevant to your field. This integrated approach enhances your readiness for a rapidly changing global workplace by helping you apply knowledge in practice, build confidence, and develop the competencies employers value most. Aston Global Advantage Entry requirements A 2:2 or above Psychology degree (or recognised international equivalent) that is accredited by the British Psychological Society (BPS). This ensures that students are eligible for Graduate Basis for Chartered (GBC) membership of the BPS. Students who are applying from outside the UK , or who do not have a BPS accredited Bachelor’s degree in Psychology, must check directly with the BPS to see if they qualify for GBC. See international student information below for international equivalent information. International students Aston University is a diverse, close community and welcomes international students to many of our postgraduate programmes.
